Storm water runoff flows through the property and discharges into the wetlands untreated. The project will remove soil and fill material, construct engineered wetlands to treat storm water prior to discharging into the Snow Creek tributary, and restore functioning wetlands. Other components include sidewalks and a shared-use path connection from the Tahoe Vista Recreation Beach to the North Tahoe Regional Park.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Fisheries, Recreation, Soil Conservation, Water Quality

properties.ProjectName: Big Meadow Watershed Fire Regime Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This 640-acre project restores upland, riparian, aspen, and meadow habitat in Big Meadow Creek watershed and restores fire on the landscape. We  thinned conifers from most of the project area and began burning slash piles. Future priorities include: burn remaining slash piles, thin areas with  a lack of resilient forest conditions, and use prescribed fire to restore native meadow vegetation. There is an urgent need to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires, and massive tree die off from insects, by treating hazardous fuels that have accumulated in these forests. There is also a need to use prescribed fire  to reintroduce natural disturbances as a means of improving resilient conditions.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: South Shore Hazardous Fuels Reduction and Ecosystem Restoration

These treatments would reduce the level of hazardous fuels within the defense and threat zones. This includes the use of mechanical harvesters and chainsaws for thinning to reduce live tree densities and mechanical chipping to reduce the amount of existing dead and down biomass.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

Upon completion, this project will provide 17.5 miles of stream and 100 lake acres for this federally threatened species and be the largest interconnected habitat for LCT in the Sierra's. With partner funding, LTBMU staff began implementation of a new method in 2023 to improve effectiveness and efficiency of treatment methods in the project area.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Fish and Wildlife; California Tahoe Conservancy; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Trout Unlimited; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; U.S. Forest Service

properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Rosewood Creek Restoration - Middle Reach (Area A)
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This stream restoration project included the construction of a new channel along 90 percent of this reach to improve riparian functions, reduce stream velocities during high flows, improve forest health with selective tree thinning, and improve fish habitat by removing obstructions. The new channel was engineered to prevent further bed and bank erosion, reconnect the stream to the surrounding floodplain, and promote reestablishment of viable fish populations in Rosewood Creek by improving the stream geometry.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: SEZ Mitigation Funds; Tahoe Bonds Act; U.S. Bureau of Reclamation

properties.ProjectName: Griff Creek Stream Habitat Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Griff Creek is located within the Griff Creek watershed in Kings Beach along the north shore of Lake Tahoe. Due to development in the urbanized area of Kings Beach, the once braided stream channel system with natural flood control zones has been forced into a single channel that has resulted in significant bank erosion and incised channels. The purpose of the project is to improve the water quality in the Griff Creek watershed within the residential area of Kings Beach by preventing further stream degradation, installing water quality enhancement features, and restoring stream environmental zones where feasible.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Integrated Regional Water Management Plan Funds (IWRMP); Placer County General Fund; SEZ Mitigation Funds; U.S. Bureau of Reclamation

properties.ProjectName: Glenridge Defense Zone Fuels Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: Fuels were treated along Sugar Pine Point State Park boundary and the adjacent Glenridge residential subdivision. Thirty-seven acres of forest was thinned and resulting forest debris piles were burned
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Upper Truckee River and Marsh Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Project is a large, ecosystem restoration project on the Upper Truckee River and marsh. In 2025, the Conservancy completed the project that includes new pilot channels and wetlands, an accessible to all pedestrian trail to Lake Tahoe, and aquatic invasive species removal.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: 319 Funds; California Department of Fish and Wildlife; California Tahoe Conservancy; California Wildlife Conservation Board; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Proposition 1; U.S. Army Corps of Engineers; U.S. Bureau of Reclamation

properties.ProjectName: State Route 28 Crystal Bay (431 to CA Stateline) Erosion Control & Water Quality Improvement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This project will include water quality improvements for State Route 28 from SR 431 to the CA/NV Stateline.  The project includes the implementation of source control measures (rock rip-rap, vegetation, and land coverage removal) for steep cut slopes and eroding shoulder areas, curb/gutter, trench drains and stormdrain piping for collection of storm water and drop inlets and water quality detention basins for treatment.  This project is a high priority for water quality improvements due to its close proximity to Lake Tahoe and the presence of highly erosive cut and fill slopes throughout the project area.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District; Nevada Department of Transportation; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Bonds Act; U.S. Federal Highway Administration

properties.ProjectName: Highway 50 Water Quality Improvement Project Phase I
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The project area is comprised of three discontinuous segments from Cave Rock to the US 50/SR 28 intersection. Significant cut slopes exist throughout the project area and contribute a significant amount of sediment to stormwater. Slope stabilization options such as revegetation and soil/rock nailing and refacing will be evaluated through the alternative design process. In addition, facilities for the conveyance and treatment of stormwater will be evaluated and designed. The first phase of the project includes the stabilization of four cut slopes which were prioritized due to their sediment production and connectivity to stream systems.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Department of Transportation; Nevada State Gas Tax; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Federal Highway Administration

properties.ProjectName: Sawmill 2A Bike Path and Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This project included the construction of a Class I Bike Path from Lake Tahoe Blvd to Echo View Drive and treatment of eroding cut and fill slopes in the County right-of-way and revegetation of disturbed areas.  Perform right-of-way acquisitions as needed.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Soil Conservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: AQ Mitigation Funds; California Tahoe Conservancy; Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Program (CMAQ); Regional Surface Transportation Program Funds (RSTP); Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Christmas Valley Erosion Control Project - Phase 2C
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The Christmas Valley Erosion Control Project - Phase 2C encompasses the streets of Santa Claus Drive, Saint Nick Way, the southernmost end of Blitzen Road, and Elf Lane (includes Christmas Valley Unit Nos. 1 and 2). The main goals of the Project are related to improving the water quality of runoff to Lake Tahoe by reducing erosion and sediment flow originating in the Project area. The Project goals are remove/reduce fine sediment originating from the Project areas prior to reaching the Upper Truckee River to the maximum extent practicable. Remove/reduce coarse sediment originating from the Project areas prior to reaching the Upper Truckee River to the maximum extent practicable.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Montgomery Estates Area 1 Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Improvements will include re-vegetation of disturbed soils, drainage stabilization (e.g., paved gutters, rock lined channels), infiltration and sedimentation facilities (e.g., veg. treatment ponds and various sediment traps).
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Echo View 2 Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This Project is the second Phase of the Echo View Estates Erosion Control Project which was completed in 1988. The primary goal of this Project is to help improve the clarity of Lake Tahoe by reducing water quality impacts caused by the development of the Echo View Estates subdivision on Angora Creek., which is a tributary to the Upper Truckee River. The objective of the Project is to reduce the transport of fine sediment from the Project area by constructing and enhancing water quality Best Management Practices (BMPs) with the Project area.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Sierra Tract Erosion Control Project Phase 4
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels

properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Proposition 84 (Lahontan); South Tahoe Public Utility District; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Warrior Way Water Quality Improvement Project

properties.FundingSources: Douglas County General Fund; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Central Incline Village Water Quality Improvement Project - Phase I
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This project included many small specific areas that were identified for source control and conveyance as part of the Washoe County EIP Project Assessment completed in February of 2006. The project areas for this project are within project boundaries of several completed EIP projects however the improvements constructed with this project were not included as part of the older projects. Treatment areas within the project area were prioritized based on fine sediment particle (FSP) loading identified in the "Nevada Tahoe TMDL Implementing Agencies Stormwater Load Reduction Plans Baseline and Existing Conditions Final Technical Documents" dated December 31, 2013.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels

properties.ProjectName: Al Tahoe Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The City of South Lake Tahoe is the implementing agency for this project. The Al Tahoe project area consists of two primary watersheds that drains to several storm drains that collect flow from the Al Tahoe subdivision. The project area is approximately 55 acres (bounded by US 50 to the east, Los Angeles Avenue to the south, Lake Tahoe to the north and Sacramento Avenue to the west) with ~19 acres of impervious area. Included are disturbed earthen road shoulders, single- and multi-family residences, commercial enterprises, and a popular recreation area – Regan Beach.
properties.FundingSources: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act; Proposition 50; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Estates Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This project involves treatment of stormwater and slope stabilization through revegetation, rock slope protection, retaining walls, curb and gutter, and sediment basins. Catchment and treatment of sediment is needed.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Golden Bear Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The Golden Bear subdivision was constructed with conveyance systems in the County right-of-way, including curb and gutter, drainage inlets, and underground storm drain pipe. These systems were designed to convey, but not to treat the storm water. The main goal of the Project is to reduce the very fine and fine sediment from the Montgomery Estates Unit No. 7 subdivision which will improve the clarity of Lake Tahoe.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Burke Creek Highway 50 Crossing & Realignment Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The project included the installation of a geomorphically correct crossing under U.S. Highway 50, removal of a portion of a parking lot for restoration to floodplain, spot treat headcuts upstream of Highway 50, and install conveyance improvements along the highway.  In addition,  Phase II of the project realigned Burke Creek directly downstream of Highway 50 and installed stormwater treatment infrastructure on U.S. Forest Service land.  These improvements eliminated the discharge of untreated stormwater to Burke Creek thereby reducing the transport of fine sediment particles, phosphorus, and nitrogen to Lake Tahoe.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Nevada State Gas Tax; SEZ Mitigation Funds; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Rubicon 5 Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Rubicon 5 Erosion Control Project (ECP) is one of the last ECP's within this region. There have been 7 ECP's built in this area: Victoria Drive, Rubicon (1-4), Mountain Drive, Woodland, Tamarack, Silvertip, and Lonely Gulch. The problems to be addressed with this project include the following: 
        a.  Direct discharges of runoff into Lake Tahoe.Eroding cut slopes, drainages, and roadside ditches.
        b.  Road sand/cinder accumulation on roads and discharge into drainages.
        c.  Bare shoulders used as parking turnouts.
        d.  Inadequate Private BMPs.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

The main goals of the Project are related to improving the water quality of runoff to Lake Tahoe by reducing erosion and sediment flow originating in the Project area. The Project goals are remove/reduce fine sediment originating from the Project areas prior to reaching the Upper Truckee River to the maximum extent practicable. Remove/reduce coarse sediment originating from the Project areas prior to reaching the Upper Truckee River to the maximum extent practicable.

properties.ProjectName: High Meadows/Cold Creek Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Stream channel and floodplain restoration along Cold Creek in High Meadows.  Decommissioned incised channel, constructed new channels and floodplain, installed wood debris structures, and removed lodgepole mortality.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Hills Stormwater Management/Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Hills Erosion Control Project is within the Tahoe Hills subdivision which is bordered by Highway 89 to the north and south, and by Lake Tahoe to the east . The Project area encompasses County Right of Way (ROW), Caltrans ROW, California Tahoe Conservancy, United States Forest Service, and privately owned property. The main goal of the Project is to reduce the very fine and fine sediment from the Tahoe Hills subdivision which will ultimately improve the clarity of Lake Tahoe.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Country Club Heights Stormwater Management and Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The project, located in the Country Club Heights subdivision, is roughly bounded by Highway 50, the Upper Truckee River, and Crystal Air Drive.  The project accomplished the main goal to reduce very fine/fine sediment from the County right-of-way from reaching the Upper Truckee River near Elks Club Drive to help achieve TMDL goals.  Phases 1 & 2 focused on water quality (WQ) / Stream Environment Zone (SEZ) improvements throughout the subdivision.  Phase 3 is focused on WQ / SEZ/ and User Access improvements surrounding the old “Elks Lodge” property between Elks Club Drive, Highway 50, and the Upper Truckee River.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Proposition 1; SEZ Mitigation Funds; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Sierra Nevada Yellow-Legged Frog Habitat Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore and Protect Native Fish and Wildlife
properties.ProjectDescription: Implement the decision to restore habitat (seven lakes, three stream miles) for native aquatic species with focus on the SNYLF within the Desolation Wilderness (completed in 2011).  Fish removal was complete in 2011. This area has been monitored by partner agencies and project goals were met.   Future range expansion efforts in the Glen Alpine drainage would aid in the recovery of this species and should be considered as a future EIP project.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Montgomery Estates Area 3 Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The Montgomery Estates Area 3 Erosion Control is bordered by Trout Creek to the west, Cold Creek to the north and Pioneer Trail to the south. The main goal of the Project is to improve the clarity of Lake Tahoe by reducing the detrimental water quality impacts of the Montgomery Estates subdivision on Lake Tahoe clarity. The objective of the Project is the reduction in the transport of fine sediment from the Project area by constructing water quality Best Management Practices (BMPs) prior to reaching Cold Creek and Trout Creek to the maximum extent practicable.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Zephyr Cove Resort Corral Retrofit and Rehabilitation
properties.ProjectDescription:
NEPA Analysis for the project was completed in 2009. The goal of this project was to develop a proposed action that reduces threats to the water quality of Lake Tahoe associated with the Zephyr Cove Corral, bringing the site into compliance with environmental management standards. 

The resulting Decision Memo allows the USFS to move forward with project implementation at this site.  Proposed actions include corral facility upgrades, including storm water runoff and horse waste management BMPs, trail relocation and retrofits, management of noxious weeds, and monitoring.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Fallen Leaf Bike Trail Analysis & Design
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Fallen Leaf Bike Trail Analysis and Design project provided analysis and design for a shared use trail system in the Fallen Leaf Lake area.  The trail proposal provided sustainable recreation trails for non-motorized users accessing National Forest Lands.  The plan included analyzing both existing trails and the need for additional trails within the project area in order to establish a planned and managed system to meet recreation needs while minimizing impacts to resources.
 See notes for details.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Boulder Mountain Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The Boulder Mountain Erosion Control Project includes Mountain View Estates subdivision Unit No. 10 and a portion of Unit No. 7 and encompasses the area south of Angora Highlands, north of Lake Tahoe Blvd. and west of Tahoe Mountain Road. The project goals are to treat eroding cut and fill slopes in the County right-of-way. Remove the very fine/fine particles up to 11% of the total load from the County right-of-way prior to reaching the Angora Creek. Revegetation of disturbed areas including the restoration of the Boulder Mountain Drive pavement. Stabilize areas around the County right-of-way impacted by the Angora Fire.
properties.FundingSources: South Tahoe Public Utility District; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Meyers Landfill Remediation
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Cap remediation of Meyers Landfill to prevent the migration of pollutants detected in groundwater (vinyl chloride) into Saxon Creek and adjacent drinking water wells. Project completed to 75% in 2011, and remainder of construction completed in 2012; certification of performance completed in 2016.  Ongoing groundwater and gas monitoring to continue in support of the Remedial Investigation for the groundwater operable unit. Site maintenance and drainage improvements are also ongoing, as needed.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Incline Hazardous Fuels Reduction & Healthy Forest Restoration/Implementation
properties.ProjectDescription: This project proposes to conduct project level resource surveys and environmental analyses (NEPA) and ground implementation for reduction of fuel ladders, standing and down fuel accumulations and canopy densities by modifying vegetation structure and fuel loads. The project would help restore healthy, diverse, fire resilient forest structure through tree thinning, and introduce prescribed fire for fuels reduction purposes to restore fire regimes that were historically part of the ecosystem. The project area covers North Lake Tahoe and the community near Incline Village.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: North Shore Roads Access and Travel Management Plan
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription:
The North Shore Road Transportationshed project included planning and implementation of road upgrades, stream crossings, and road decommissioning as part of a comprehensive Best Management Practices (BMP) program for roads.  Where ever possible, the enhancement, protection, and reduction of coverage in riparian zones were a primary consideration. The following deliverables were completed:

-Miles of roads inventoried or monitored:  56 miles
-Miles of roads decommissioned: 1.7 miles
-Miles of Existing Routes Improved:  41 miles
- Approximately 13 miles of roads received BMPs.  Work consisted of surface drainage work such as drainage dip shaping.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Meyers Stream Environment Zone/Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This project aims to restore approximately nine acres of stream environment zone (SEZ) partially through the reconnection of Meyers Creek to its floodplain. In the 1960’s, Meyers Creek was channelized linearly along the border of the SEZ to make way for urban development. The parcel is located on Santa Fe Road at the west end of Pioneer Trail in Meyers. By reconnecting the creek to its floodplain to restore wetland processes. The project will also have greenhouse gas reductions, groundwater recharge, flood control, water efficiency, possible regional treatment systems, and recreation. This project treats 5 miles of roadways through source control and hydrologic design.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; SEZ Mitigation Funds; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Upper Truckee River Watershed/Ecosystem Restoration: Reach 5 & 6 Planning & Reach 5 Construction
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Implementation of stream channel floodplain restoration project in Upper Truckee River, Reach 5.  NEPA/CEQA planning with this funding also included Upper Truckee Reach 6, located on California Tahoe Conservancy land. This project included improving aquatic habitat, increasing channel/floodplain connectivity, increasing meadow wetness and reducing bank erosion. The project involved new channel construction and re-activation of the floodplain on both Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit and California Tahoe Conservancy lands within the 120-acre project area meadow, restoring form and function to 7,340 ft of river channel
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Nevada Beach Day Use Area and Campground BMP Retrofit
properties.ProjectDescription:
The funding for this project was focused on Facility and BMP improvements to the Nevada 
Beach Campground (SNPLMA 096 and 062). Stormwater infiltration improvements,  one restroom with BMPs, road paving, accessibility compliant campsites, and an accessible trail were constructed to the beach.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Community Service Area (CSA) # 5 Erosion Control Project includes the developed portions of the Tahoe Cedars subdivision southwest of Highway 89 between the El Dorado County Line and Poplar Street. The goal of the Project is to reduce the concentration of fine sediment in the storm water which exits the Project area before reaching Lake Tahoe. 

The Project was split into multiple phases.  This Project represents Phases 1 and 2 which are now complete.  The final phase (Phase 3) is listed as a separate project.

properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries

properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project implemented water quality protection BMPs where appropriate, improve soil quality, install native vegetation to slow surface run-off and screen activities from the highway.

The BMPs built to accomplish the project objectives were:
1.	Infiltration basins 
2.	Highway sound and water diversion wall
3.	Decommission of abandoned well
4.	Soil decompaction
5.	Revegetation with native plants

properties.ProjectName: Taylor and Tallac Ecosystem Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The USDA Forest Service Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit (LTBMU) and the Tahoe Regional Planning Agency (TRPA) are working together to restore the Taylor and Tallac creeks and marshes in South Lake Tahoe, California by treating a 17-acre invasive weed infestation. The containment/eradication of aquatic invasive weeds in the Taylor and Tallac Creek watershed is the first phase in a larger, comprehensive Taylor and Tallac Restoration project and is critical to successfully restoring this habitat and is expected to wrap up in 2025. A design contract was awarded to obtain 100% designs and permits for phase 2. Phase 2 is expected to begin 2026/2027 (pending funding and environmental conditions).
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Shoreline Fee; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Fund; U.S. Army Corps of Engineers

properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels

properties.ProjectDescription: Removal of Incline Lake Dam structures, restoration of stream and meadow, and installation of permanent BMPs. Dam removal was completed in 2020; channel and floodplain through former dam footprint were restored and ditch decommissioned in 2021; boardwalk trail across constructed floodplain was constructed in 2022; additional ditch decommissioning and upland disturbed site restoration work occurred in 2023; and the remaining stream and meadow restoration work was completed in 2024. properties.ProjectDescription:
This Federal Project, led by the Federal Highway Administration, Office of Federal Lands Highways, Central Federal Lands Highway Division (CFLHD) includes 2 phases that were constructed separately:
- Truckee River Bridge Project includes a new, 1,700' long section of SR 89 with a new bridge over the Truckee River, 2 roundabouts. & bike paths.  The project will replace a section of sewer within the project limits.  This project was completed in 2020.
- Fanny Bridge Project includes replacement of the Fanny Bridge with a new, single span bridge and sewer replacement with an est. completion in January 2026.

Special thanks to the following project partners:  Placer County, TCPUD & BOR.

properties.ProjectDescription: The proposed project will make improvements to the US 50 corridor in the south Stateline area of Lake Tahoe by adding multi-use paths, sidewalks, pedestrian overcrossing, parking, and a roundabout at US50 and Lake Parkway intersection. The primary goal is to improve mobility, while balancing transportation needs with community goals of economic vitality and environmental preservation.

properties.ProjectDescription:
The project scope includes to components:

1. The Meeks Bay Trail project includes construction of a 0.7 mile paved, shared use path between the Meeks Bay Resort and Sugar Pine Resort.  75% of the project includes retaining walls and also includes a new bridge.  The new bridge and retaining walls will be constructed with GRS-IBS foundations to save costs, construction time, and impacts.

2.  Construction of bike paths, sidewalk, curb and gutter in Tahoe City as part of the Truckee River Bridge Project.

properties.ProjectName: Sierra Boulevard Complete Streets Project (From US Highway 50 to Barbara Avenue)
properties.ProjectDescription: The primary intent of the project was the rehabilitation of the 0.6-mile stretch of Sierra Blvd from Palmira Avenue to Barbara Ave.  The rehabilitation of Sierra Blvd included redesign of the roadway section, the addition of bike lane(s), paths, pedestrian sidewalks and the addition of streetscape improvements, including pedestrian lighting, hardscape, and landscape improvements in conjunction with a Rule 20 Utility undergrounding project that occurred in 2011-2013.  The project also provides corridor water quality improvements and tie-in with the erosion control improvements surrounding the project area.   The Complete Streets project provides a major link between the Greenway and U.S 50.

Sidewalks constructed by SW Gas in 2017 adjacent to the retail center were leveraged as part of the project by the City. Improvements include City standard streetlights for the full length of the path. Construction of improvements occurred in the summer of 2020 with final touches to complete the Project in the spring of 2021.

properties.ProjectName: Restoration/Recovery of Lahontan Cutthroat Trout in Fallen Leaf Lake
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore and Protect Native Fish and Wildlife
properties.ProjectDescription: Reintroduction and management of LCT continued in the Fallen Leaf Lake watershed in 2022 under a Memorandum of Understanding and a new scientific collection permit between FWS and CDFW. These agreements identify adaptive management priorities for establishing and protecting the lacustrine LCT population in the lake. Activities followed recommendations from the Science Panel Independent Review Report (Al-Chokhachy et al. 2020). Accomplishments included nonnative lake trout removal, installation of a fyke net, backpack electrofishing and stocking of LCT.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

properties.ProjectName: Sand Harbor Accessibility Improvement Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The project includes the replacement and upgrade of Diver's Cove and the eastern portion of picnic area walkways to ADA Accessibility standards. The overlooks will have decking and stairs constructed of open grate so that they are fully permeable and allow the infiltration of water beneath the structures.

properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Phase five of the Third and Incline Creek Restoration addressed the fish barrier on Incline Creek on the Golf course. The drop leaving the culvert was over 3 feet and restricted upper watershed migration and eroded the banks.  The culvert was also past its useful life and in disrepair.  This fish barrier improvement allows spring and fall aquatic migration. Migration from the mouth of Lake Tahoe through the previously completed restoration sites increased access to upper watershed habitat by several miles.
properties.FundingSources: 319 Funds; Incline Village General Improvement District; Lake Tahoe License Plate Program; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Slaughterhouse Healthy Forest Restoration and Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Conduct hazardous fuel reduction and forest ecosystem health treatments in the Slaughterhouse area on the east shore of the Lake Tahoe Basin. These fuel reduction treatments would cover the National Forest areas and would focus on the Urban Wildland Interface adjacent to the Glenbrook Community and the Highway 28 corridor. Treatments would reduce the level of hazardous fuels within the defense and threat zones. This includes the use of mechanical harvesters and chainsaws for thinning to reduce live tree densities and mechanical chipping to reduce the amount of existing dead and down biomass. Included in project implementation is contract administration and project monitoring. Project

The project also stabilized 2 eroding beach outfalls and provided infiltration where possible.

properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Native Vegetation and Forest Communities

Cut material was burned on site. To evaluate the state of wildlife populations in treated areas, seasonal survey and monitoring work was completed.  These surveys were used to inform future forest restoration efforts, as well as to evaluate the effects of past efforts on songbird, raptor, and mammal populations. Total of 1500 sugar pine seedlings planted on 25 acres.

This fills one of the last gaps for completing a non-motorized transportation and recreation travel alternative in the North Lake Tahoe region.  The Dollar Creek Shared Use Trail is a 2.2 mile segment from Dollar Hill into the northern Cedar Flat neighborhood. Construction was started in 2018.  Project is now complete.

properties.ProjectName: Griff Creek Restoration at Old Kingswood 500,000 Tank
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: When the NTPUD built anew 1.3 mil. gallon water storage tank and booster pump station, the District saw an opportunity to demolish the old 500,000 gallon water tank and booster pump station, both built in the 1960s, and restore a sensitive Stream Environment Zone along Griff Creek. This project was designed to improve water quality by removing infrastructure from the SEZ and restoring the area as closely as possible to pre-disturbance conditions. The priorities were to reconnect the creek with its floodplain in an area where a berm was built to protect the water tank from stream flows; re-contour and re-vegetate the site to prevent erosion and restore a diverse native plant community.
properties.FundingSources: North Tahoe Public Utility District; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Van Sickle Bi-State Park - CA Phase III Improvements

Building on a 2019 Vision Plan for the park, the Conservancy is planning to improve the Park entrance, trails, and facilities. The proposed Van Sickle Bi-State Park Safety and Equitable Access Improvement Project includes a new shared-use trail through the Park, a new entrance plaza, two improved picnic and day-use areas, interpretive and wayfinding signs, and Best Management Practices for snow storage and storm water runoff. The Conservancy also proposes to build approximately 0.35 miles of the Dennis T. Machida Memorial Greenway (Van Sickle Connector) to connect the Park to Chonokis Road. 

This item also includes the Conservancy's acquisition of a parcel at the Park entrance in 2025.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Excess Coverage Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: STPUD Upper Truckee Marsh Sewer Facilities Protection Project

properties.ProjectDescription:
The purpose of the project is to protect existing force and gravity sewer mains and the Bellevue Pump Station from flooding and channel migration using an adaptive management approach and primarily vegetative techniques. 

To close out the Adaptive Management Program for this project, final monitoring, including topographic, field hydrology, and vegetation surveys, were conducted in 2020 to demonstrate the changes in flow patterns resulting from the features installed to protect the District's utility easement. Findings from the final survey effort will be documented in a final AMP Technical Report to complete the regulatory reporting requirements for this project in 2021.
properties.FundingSources: South Tahoe Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: Oflyng Water Quality Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Urban development in the Oflyng residential area has resulted in a concentrated flow of storm water from the County of El Dorado (County) right-of-way (ROW) directed to pervious forested land as well as the Upper Truckee River. The hydrologic connectivity between Lake Tahoe and the Oflyng Drive area results in a high to moderate potential to deliver fine sediment to Lake Tahoe. Storm water runoff will be directed into infiltration improvements providing a direct reduction in the transport of fine sediment to Lake Tahoe.  It is also anticipated that urban storm water infrastructure will be upgraded to current design standards w/ conveyance improved to allow for proper flow sizing/routing.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Proposition 1; WQ Mitigation Funds

A major overhaul to the stage and electrical system is needed. The shed is in danger of collapse and the stage surface is rapidly deteriorating. NDOT & NTCD built the Bourne Meadow Basins in 2025, and NDOT will complete the basin conveyance in 2026. NTCD seeks implementation funding to complete GID/HOA stormwater treatment portion.

properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Untreated or under-treated stormwater was being directly discharged to the Lake. Stormwater infrastructure was installed along the US-50 in the NDOT right-of-way and within the Pittman Terrace neighborhood to treat stormwater runoff prior to discharge to the lake. 560 linear feet of infiltration ditch and 290 linear feet of underground infiltration galleries were installed to capture and infiltrate stormwater. The NDOT US-50 catchment was considered a high priority catchment due to its being a high pollutant loading and directly connected catchment in a highly constrained area. Project is registered in the LT Info Stormwater Tools and has the potential to garner NDOT 8 Lake Clarity Credits.
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Department of Transportation; Nevada Division of Environmental Protection; Private Property Owners; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Lake Tahoe West Landscape-Scale Restoration Partnership

This large-scale planning effort will be grounded upon input from key stakeholders and scientifically derived decision-support models incorporating water quantity/quality, carbon sequestration, climate change, fire and fuels, and wildlife habitat.

properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: South Tahoe Greenway Shared Use Trail Phases 1b & 2
properties.ProjectDescription: Completed and open to the public in fall 2021, the South Tahoe Greenway Shared Use Trail Phases 1b & 2 is the second implementation phase of the entire Greenway project, now named the Dennis T. Machida Greenway Memorial Trail. It expands on the existing bicycle network and connections in South Lake Tahoe. The approximately one mile shared use trail between Glenwood Way and Sierra Blvd, includes an elevated boardwalk near Trout Creek and Bijou Creek. A new bike bridge over Trout Creek, improves local street crossings, and connectivity to nearby amenities.
properties.FundingSources: California Active Transportation Program (ATP) Funds - Federalized; California Tahoe Conservancy; Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Program (CMAQ)

properties.ProjectName: South Tahoe Greenway Shared Use Trail Planning and Future Phases
properties.ProjectDescription: The Dennis T. Machida Memorial Greenway envisions paved trail connections from Sierra Boulevard to Van Sickle Bi-State Park, creating the second leg of the non-motorized transportation network in South Shore. Project approval occurred in 2011 and the 3.86 mile trail, including neighborhood connectors, is being constructed in phases. Phases 1a, 1b, and 2 are complete, and Phase 1c planning was recently initiated, with details reported under separate EIP projects. Phase 3 implementation is postponed. The Upper Truckee Bridge at Johnson Meadow project will extend the Greenway to the South Tahoe WYE. Future projects could extend the Greenway to Meyers.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Community Ball Fields
properties.ProjectDescription: Construct new play fields on City and College property located adjacent to South Tahoe Community College. The project consists of 4 acres of new natural grass to accommodate two FIFA standard soccer fields and other community play activities.
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Upper Keller Canyon Drainage and Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Steep eroding slopes, road cuts and concentrated drainage into unprotected road shoulders result in significant erosion and drainage issues in steep, erosion prone slopes and creates flooding and drainage issues for residents. Existing site conditions include inadequate rock lined channels on steep slopes that are overwhelmed during high intensity precipitation events. Project work will include adding in additional storm drain inlets, adding subsurface storm drain pipes that will connect rock-lined channels, and constructing basins where feasible.

properties.ProjectName: Ruby Way – Overlook Court Drainage and Erosion Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Water quality and erosion control project that will address surface runoff conditions. Existing site conditions include an undersized storm drain collection and conveyance system that is overwhelmed during high intensity storms. Project work will include adding in additional storm drain inlets, adding subsurface storm drain pipes to replace an existing steep rock-lined conveyance channel, and constructing a series of linear storm drain detention basins that will also allow infiltration of stormwater. Project improvements will redirect urban stormwater runoff into a new subsurface conveyance systems; thereby, removing overland surface flow that is impacting private and public property.
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund; Proposition 1

properties.ProjectName: Eagle Point Campground Rehabilitation
properties.ProjectDescription: Design and construct BMPs, erosion controls, and rehabilitation for campground facilities including, campsites, structures, and associated roads/trails at D.L. Bliss State Park. This includes compliance with ADA standards.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Washoe Meadows State Park Watershed Improvement and Implementation
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Road and trails planning and implementation for backcountry areas including unpaved roads, trails, etc.  This also includes BMPs.  Identifies all road and trails to be maintained by CA State Parks, improvements to those not meeting standards, and removal and restoration for those roads and trails not to be maintained.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation; South Tahoe Public Utility District; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Bijou Area Water Quality Improvement Project, Phases 2
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Stabilize roadside shoulders as a means of sediment source control to protect the newly constructed Bijou ECP Phase 1 infiltration basins.  Provide distributed infiltration as a form of hydrologic source control, acquire easements and install overflow conveyances where localized flooding results in excessive sediment tracking onto City road network, in order to improve roadway sweeping effectiveness and source control.
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Lakeview Lookout Community Wildfire Protection Plan Implementation Project
properties.ProjectDescription: This fuels reduction project was on four privately owned lots at the edge of a neighborhood in the  Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) Defense Zone. Overcrowded and/or diseased trees were thinned. Dense pockets of shrubs were also thinned. These materials, along with dead and downed woody debris were piled over the summer and burned in the following fall/winter.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Private Property Owners; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Beach Club Utility Undergrounding and SEZ Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Beach Club is located on the site of the existing Tahoe Shores Mobile Home Park on the south shore of Lake Tahoe in Douglas County, Nevada. The project involves closure of the mobile home park, removal of the 155 existing mobile home spaces, realignment of the project site roadways and utilities, construction of new condominiums and construction of a beach and swim club, expansion of the existing pier, construction of stormwater treatment facilities, and SEZ restoration.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Energy; Private (Business)

properties.ProjectName: North Tahoe and Meeks Bay CWPP Implementation
properties.ProjectDescription: The North Tahoe and Meeks Bay Community Wildfire Protection Plan Implementation Project reduced hazardous vegetation on 137 acres in the wildland-urban interface. The areas targeted for treatment included 514 priority acres of private and local government land in both North Tahoe Fire Protection District (NTFPD) and Meeks Bay Fire Protection District, however 137 acres were treated as part of this project. Recent interagency planning efforts identified this acreage as a priority to serve the goals of the Lake Tahoe Basin Multi-Jurisdictional Fuel Reduction and Wildfire Prevention Strategy, and to complete treatments identified in the Lake Tahoe Basin Community Wildfire Protection Plan, 2015
properties.FundingSources: North Tahoe Public Utility District; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Unknown or Unassigned

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Village Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Village Fuels Reduction Project was a 57 acre forest thinning and fuels reduction project located on undeveloped land west of the Tahoe Village HOA community. The project was originally funded by FEMA.  The environmental compliance was completed as a part of the Environmental Assessment completed for the FEMA projects.  The funding source was switched to U.S. Forest Service funding so that pile burning could be utilized to dispose of slash.
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: South Upper Truckee Water Quality Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The South Upper Truckee Water Quality Project (Project) encompasses Tahoe Paradise Unit 60, River Park Estates Units 1 & 2, and South Gate Subdivisions.  This includes the neighborhoods off of South Upper Truckee Road, bordered by US 50 to the north, the Upper Truckee River to the south and east, and USFS owned parcels to the west.  The primary goal of the Project is to improve the clarity of Lake Tahoe by reducing detrimental water quality impacts that are a result of the development of the subdivisions, including the reduction of the transport of fine sediment from the Project area to the Upper Truckee River by construction of appropriate water quality BMPs.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: American Rescue Plan; SEZ Mitigation Funds; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Kings Beach Pier Reconstruction
properties.ProjectDescription: The project revises the 1980 General Plan for Kings Beach State Recreation Area (KBSRA), expands the KBSRA boundary to include the 1.36-acre Kings Beach Plaza (Plaza), and considers potential land ownership transfer of the Plaza to State Parks.  The General Plan revision would provide a comprehensive framework for projects within, and management of, KBSRA over the next 20 years.  The project also includes three locational alternatives for rebuilding the Kings Beach pier to a standard that increases its functionality for boating.  The preferred pier location is to the east end of KBSRA.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation; California Tahoe Conservancy; California Wildlife Conservation Board; North Tahoe Community Alliance; Proposition 84

properties.ProjectName: Zephyr Cove Elementary School Science Center
properties.ProjectDescription: An indoor/outdoor place-based science classroom located at Zephyr Cove Elementary School. This classroom will be open to all schools in the Region as a center for students to learn about the environment and Lake Tahoe while doing science and having fun. Designed for K-6 students with curriculum based on the program areas of the Environmental Improvement Program.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe License Plate Program; Private (Business)

properties.ProjectName: Edgewood Lodge and Golf Course Improvement
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The project is located at the bottom of the Edgewood Creek watershed which drains an area of approximately 6.6 square miles. Mixed land uses within the watershed interrupted the natural hydrologic processes, and the resulting influx of nutrients and sediment degraded the quality of the watershed. This project included construction of a new 194-unit lodge complex and a series of environmental improvements including enhanced BMPs for the lodge complex, water quality improvements to the pond system, Edgewood Creek improvements, Friday’s Station dam rehabilitation, and undergrounding of existing overhead utility lines.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Soil Conservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Edgewood Companies

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Lagoon Aquatic Weeds Control Methods Test Implementation
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The Control Methods Test was approved by TRPA and Lahontan in January 2022, and implementation of the full test- ultraviolet light, aquatic herbicides and other non-herbicidal methods- began in May of 2022. In addition to the test treatment methods, extensive monitoring is being conducted to follow herbicide degradation, water quality conditions, and efficacy of treatment methods.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Lagoons Aquatic Weeds Control Methods Test Planning
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys Lagoons are a series of waterways directly connected to Lake Tahoe that are almost entirely infested with invasive aquatic weeds. At over 170 acres, it is the largest aquatic weed infestation in the lake. The Tahoe Keys Lagoons Aquatic Weed Control Methods Test is collaboratively developed project that seeks to test multiple methods of weed control to gain information on what combination of methods will have the best chance of treating the entirety of the Tahoe Keys Lagoons infestation. The environmental analysis and test project was approved by boards from TRPA and Lahontan in January 2022, with implementation slated for the Spring of 2022. Implementation project 01.03.01.000
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association; Tahoe Regional Planning Agency

properties.ProjectName: Upper Haines Canyon - Kingsbury 1000
properties.ProjectDescription: The Upper Haines Canyon Fuels Reduction Project is a 72 acre fuels reduction project located in Haines Canyon Nevada.  Haines Canyon is a steep v-shaped canyon formed by Daggett Creek.  The canyon runs from 4700 feet in elevation where it crosses Foothill Road and extends up to the summit of Kingbury Grade at an elevation of 7350 feet.  The canyon extends from the Lake Tahoe Basin down to Carson Valley.  As such, the valley is subject to diurnal winds typical of mountain canyons.  The units within the project are designed to create survivable space around homes within the canyon and to further treat fuels located within Upper Haines Canyon.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Burton Creek Forest Restoration and Prescribed Fire
properties.ProjectDescription: Forest thinning with hand crews and prescribed fire will be implemented to reduce hazardous fuels and enhance residual tree species health. This project is designed to reduce tree densities in order to modify fire behavior to reduce the potential for a catastrophic, stand replacement fire. Forest thinning with hand crews will prepare burn plots for treatment with understory prescribed fire.  Implement understory prescribed fire in four burn plots.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: Proposition 84

properties.ProjectName: Forestry - Barbara Lodi hand crew
properties.ProjectDescription: The Barbara Lodi forestry project involves cutting of trees that were marked under the guidance of a RPF for forest health and fuel reduction efforts. The project was implemented by hand crews cutting designated trees and brush.  The project is split into two phases, the first being the cutting of designated trees and brush and the second being the burning of the piles. The project is located in the south shore,  in the vicinity of Barbara and Lodi Streets, of Lake Tahoe and is 7 acres in size.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Forestry - SNPLMA 14 Fairway
properties.ProjectDescription: 6 acres of pile and burn.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Forestry - SNPLMA 14 Sunset
properties.ProjectDescription: Fuel hazard reduction by hand crew thinning conifers and piling for burning - 6 acres
properties.FundingSources: California Conservation Corps; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Forestry - Sunset South
properties.ProjectDescription: The Sunset South forestry project involves cutting of trees that were marked under the guidance of a RPF for forest health and fuel reduction efforts. The project was implemented by hand crews cutting designated trees and brush.  The project is split into two phases, the first being the cutting of designated trees and brush and the second being the burning of the piles. The project is located in the south shore, at the southeast end of the Conservancy's Sunset Stables property,  of Lake Tahoe and is 40 acres in size.
properties.FundingSources: California Conservation Corps

properties.ProjectName: Crystal Shores Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The aquatic plant removal work implemented at Crystal Shores West, Crystal Shores East, and Crystal Shores Villas was part of a multi-year lake-wide strategy to remove aquatic invasive plants from the nearshore of Lake Tahoe Basin. From 2014-2016, contracted divers used lake-bottom barriers, diver-assisted suction removal, and hand-pulling to remove 100% of the Eurasian watermilfoil in all three marinas. From 2017-2019, contracted divers surveyed all three marinas several times during the growing season and hand-pulled any plants detected (2 total).
properties.FundingSources: Crystal Shores Homeowners Association (Crystal Shores HOA); Lake Tahoe License Plate Program

properties.ProjectName: Fleur du Lac Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: Aquatic plant removal at Fleur du Lac Marina and the outer harbor is part of a multi-year lake-wide strategy to remove aquatic invasive plants from the nearshore of Lake Tahoe Basin. Bottom barriers, diver-assisted suction removal, and hand-pulling were used from 2016-2018 to reduce the Eurasian watermilfoil infestation to 0% cover. From 2018-2020, divers conducted surveillance monitoring to ensure there is not a re-occurence of this infestation. Surveillance monitoring was not conducted in 2021, but is expected to be re-initiated in 2021 and will continue to occur at this site annually (funding-dependent).
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Lakeside Marina Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The Eurasian watermilfoil and curlyleaf pondweed infestation covers approximately 1 acre inside and immediately adjacent to the marina. Ultraviolet light, benthic barriers, diver-assisted suction removal, and hand-pulling are being used to control these plant species. This project is being implemented in coordination with EIP Project Number 01.03.01.0030, Lakeside Beach & Marina Aquatic Invasive Plant Control UV Light Pilot II.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Inventive Resources, Inc; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Lakeside Marina; Lakeside Park Association; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Lakeside Beach Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The Eurasian watermilfoil and curly-leaf pondweed infestation at Lakeside Beach (swim area) is approximately 1 acre. These species have been removed using benthic barriers, diver-assisted suction removal, and hand-pulling. This project is being implemented in coordination with EIP Project Number 01.03.01.0030, Lakeside Beach & Marina Aquatic Invasive Plant Control UV Light Pilot II.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Meeks Bay Aquatic Invasive Species Plant Control and Monitoring
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: In 2015, the AIS Implementation Plan (Plan) and associated Action list prioritized projects for AIS control. Meeks Bay Marina is prioritized in the Plan because Eurasian watermilfoil occupy this habitat in the Marina. This project focuses on removal of the Eurasian watermilfoil infestation and associated monitoring. A contract was awarded in 2019 to initiate removal efforts of approximately three acres of invasive weeds in the footprint of the marina and upstream to the SR89 bridge. Treatment occurred 2019 through 2022. The treatment area is now in control monitoring to ensure it remains weed free. The project is expected to move to surveillance monitoring after 2025.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: ANS Task Force Funds; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; SB630 Funds; Section 108 U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (TRPA); U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Ski Run Channel Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The Eurasian watermilfoil and curly-leaf pondweed infestation is approximately 3.5 acres. The size and complexity of this infestation requires an integrated approach that includes treatment of the infestation in the adjacent Ski Run Marina.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: D.L Bliss Campground Hazardous Fuel Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: Forest thinning and fuel reduction took place to reduce hazardous fuels on 33 acres at D.L. Bliss State Park to protect forest resources, watershed resources, sensitive wildlife habitat, visitor safety and outdoor recreation while improving the resiliency of the forest.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: D.L Bliss SNPLMA Round 15 Hazardous Fuel Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: Forest thinning with hand crews and prescribed fire will be implemented to reduce hazardous fuels and enhance residual tree species health. This project is designed to reduce tree densities in order to modify fire behavior to reduce the potential for a catastrophic, stand replacement fire. Forest thinning with hand crews will reduce ladder fuels, overcrowded/diseased trees and enhance forest health. Thinned trees and dead and downed woody debris will be piled throughout the spring, summer and fall months and burned in the fall/winter.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Bureau of Land Management

properties.ProjectName: D.L. Bliss Gateway Hazardous Fuel Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: Forest thinning with hand crews and prescribed fire will be implemented to reduce hazardous fuels and enhance residual tree species health. This project is designed to reduce tree densities in order to modify fire behavior to reduce the potential for a catastrophic, stand replacement fire. Forest thinning with hand crews will reduce ladder fuels, overcrowded/diseased trees and enhance forest health. Thinned trees and dead and downed woody debris will be piled throughout the spring, summer and fall months and burned in the fall/winter.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Sugar Pine SNPLMA Round 14 Hazardous Fuel Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: This project included forest thinning with hand crews and prescribed fire to reduce hazardous fuels and enhance residual tree species health.  This project was designed to reduce tree densities in order to modify fire behavior to reduce the potential for a catastrophic, stand replacement fire. Forest thinning by hand crews reduced ladder fuels, overcrowded/diseased trees and enhance forest health. Thinned trees and dead and downed woody debris were piled throughout the spring, summer and fall months and burned in the fall/winter.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Bureau of Land Management

properties.ProjectName: Westshore Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) Hazardous Fuels Reduction and Forest Health Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The West Shore WUI Project proposes vegetation and fuels treatments to reduce stand densities to improve forest health, reduce fire hazards from existing fuels, and modify fire behavior to provide defensible space for adjoining developed private lands. Treatment options include ground based mechanical treatments wherever slope and road access allow, and hand treatments where steeper and/or rocky slopes prohibit mechanical equipment operations. The proposed action includes 110 treatment units, and approximately 100 urban lots, totaling approximately 4,875 acres.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE); California Wildlife Conservation Board; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: High Meadows Phase II- east and middle meadow
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This project is implementing a phase of meadow/riparian area restoration work identified within and around the 185-acre High Meadows Complex and thinning of the forest surrounding the meadow.  This project would implement restoration actions to enhance 120 acres of meadow/riparian habitat through removal of lodgepole pine encroachment in and around the meadow, and an additional 1.5 miles of stream/floodplain restoration. Stream restoration would include replacing stream flow into constructed and historic channels where they are currently flowing in ditches, filling of existing ditches, placing large wood in the channel, and constructing smaller in-channel structures.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

properties.ProjectName: Kings Beach Western Approach
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Multi-benefit project improving the mobility, walkability, water quality improvements and sustainability at the SR 267/SR 28 intersection. The existing signalized intersection at State Route (SR) 267 and SR 28 in Kings Beach limits vehicular flow during higher traffic volume periods. The project would convert the intersection to a roundabout considered to be an improvement in mobility, safety and efficiency, and LOS. Includes enhanced public transit access, sidewalks, bike lanes (Class II ) connection.  Project components will include acquisition of private ROW to meet goals and objectives.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: California Active Transportation Program (ATP) Funds - Federalized; California Active Transportation Program (ATP) Funds - State; Placer County General Fund; Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax; SHOPP Funds; Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) - California

properties.ProjectName: Lake Tahoe Boulevard Class 1 Bicycle Trail (Viking Way to South Wye)
properties.ProjectDescription:
Design and construct Class 1 bike trail, ADA compliant ramps, and pathway lighting along the 0.6 mile section of Lake Tahoe Blvd. from the Intersection of Viking Way (D-Street) to the intersection of State Hwy 89 and US Highway 50 (South Wye).
Note: Project name was updated from "Viking Way to Lake Tahoe Blvd. Class 1 Bike Trail" on 11/23/16 for consistency with the name CSLT used to apply for CMAQ funds.
properties.FundingSources: California Active Transportation Program (ATP) Funds - Federalized; California Highway Infrastructure Program (HIP); City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund; Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Program (CMAQ); On Our Way; Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation; Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) - California

properties.ProjectName: Incline Village Bike Park
properties.ProjectDescription: IVGID in partnership with the Incline Tahoe Foundation (ITF) and the Incline Bike Park (IBP) have come together in hopes of building a bike park in Incline Village, NV.  This would build a community park for all age groups and abilities to enjoy.  The Bike Park would be centrally located in town to allow users to ride their bikes to the park, instead of driving.  As seen at other similar venues in the Tahoe Basin, bike parks are a family centered event that get folks out of their cars and can have a lasting impact on human health as well as improve air quality.  This recreational project will have a lasting impact on the community with a low carbon footprint and a high return on investment.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District; Private (Business)

properties.ProjectName: Recreation and Swim Center Renovation/Replacement
properties.ProjectDescription: Replacement of existing City Recreation and Swim Center with new energy efficient and multi use facility.
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Truckee River Dam Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The aquatic plant removal work being implemented above Lake Tahoe Dam is part of a multi-year lake-wide strategy to remove Eurasian watermilfoil from the nearshore of Lake Tahoe. Divers primarily use hand-pulling at this site to remove Eurasian watermilfoil that periodically appears rooted here. In 2022, surveillance maintenance of this site is being transferred to EIP Project Number 01.03.01.0037 Lake-wide Surveillance and Site Assessments. The surveillance survey area is approximately 1.6 acres.
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation; California Department of Water Resources; California Tahoe Conservancy; SB630 Funds

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay Aquatic Invasive Species Asian Clam Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: A relatively sparse population of Asian clams were discovered near the mouth of Emerald Bay in 2009. Initial surveys estimated this infestation at approximately 3.5 acres in size just inside and on the south side of the mouth of Emerald Bay, in water depths of six (6) to thirty (30) feet. Surveys in 2011 showed the infestation had spread to approximately 5.5 acres (2011 U.C. Davis Survey Results), an increase in infestation size of over forty percent (40%) in only two (2) years. An expansion of the Emerald Bay infestation similar to that seen in South Lake Tahoe would result in considerable ecological and recreation impacts.
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation; Cleanup & Abatement Account (CAA); Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Elk Point Marina Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: Bottom barriers, diver-assisted suction removal and hand-pulling were used to control plants in the marina. In addition, the League to Save Lake Tahoe provided homeowners with Eyes on the Lake training to learn how to identify and report aquatic invasive plants. Effectively controlling plant fragments from entering the marina from Lake Tahoe continues to be a challenge. A bubble curtain was installed in 2021 at the mouth of the marina to reduce invasive aquatic plant fragments from re-infesting the area and to protect the investment. In 2025, diver-assisted suction removal was conducted, and diver surveys and plant removal will continue in 2026 and 2027.
properties.FundingSources: Elk Point County Club Homeowners Association Funds; Lake Tahoe License Plate Program; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; League to Save Lake Tahoe; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Meyers Intersection Improvements at US Highway 50 and State Route 89
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The project makes improvements to the existing T intersection at Highway 50 and State Route 89 in Meyers. The purpose of the project is to improve safety by reducing the number and severity of collisions at the intersection, improve air quality by improving walkability, reducing vehicle idling times and improving traffic flow, and improve recreation access by providing safer crossings of U.S. Highway 50 for pedestrians, connecting pathways on one side of the highway with recreation areas on the other. Near Meyers, at Route 89 South. Construct roundabout. EA 4F840
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: SHOPP Funds

properties.ProjectName: Pioneer Trail Pedestrian Project - Phase II
properties.ProjectDescription: Continue pedestrian sidewalks, lighting, transit stops, and class II bike lanes from the limits of the completed Phase 1 project (Larch Avenue) to the western limits of Ski Run Boulevard (+.45 Center line Miles).
