properties.FundingSources: AQ Mitigation Funds; California Active Transportation Program (ATP) Funds - State; California Highway Infrastructure Program (HIP); City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund; Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Program (CMAQ); Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) - California

properties.ProjectName: Adaptive Traffic Management on SR 89 and SR 267
properties.ProjectDescription: This is a coordinated project between Placer County, TRPA, Caltrans, and the Town of Truckee to adaptively manage basin entry roads of SR 89 and SR 267. The project seeks to reduce traffic congestion, reduce Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT), and provide evacuation capacity by means of constructing new transit-only lanes on SR 89 & SR 267.  The project will provide 2 additional transit priority lanes (TPLs), one in each direction. These lanes will be dedicated facilities for Tahoe Area Regional Transit (TART) buses. It is anticipated that other vanpool and mass transit vehicles will also use the lanes, with the intent of reducing the usage of single passenger vehicles in the corridors
properties.FundingSources: Placer County General Fund; Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax

properties.ProjectName: SR 28 Shared Use Path and Water Quality Improvements GMP2 - Incline Village to Sand Harbor
properties.ProjectDescription: This project constructs the shared use path from Incline (Ponderosa) to Sand Harbor. All work beyond Sand Harbor to the south is safety and water quality.  Project includes the design and implementation of water quality and erosion control features on State Route 28 from Spooner Summit to Sand Harbor State Park. The project includes source control, conveyance and treatment facilities for stormwater runoff. This project area is comprised of steep cut slopes and narrow shoulder areas for treatment.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Soil Conservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Program (CMAQ); Federal Lands Access Program (FLAP); Incline Village General Improvement District; National Scenic Byways Program Funds; Nevada Recreational Trails Grant; Nevada State Gas Tax; Question 1; Tahoe Fund; Washoe County General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe City Downtown Access Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription: Tahoe City Downtown Access Improvements: Implementing parking flow improvements outlined in the Tahoe City Mobility Study.  Primarily, parking capacity expansion, improved pedestrian access to Tahoe City commercial businesses and recreation amenities via a new Class 1 multi-use trail segment, driveway and private parking consolidation, and possible redevelopment of business and outdoor public gathering places. These improvements are expected to improve vehicular level of service (LOS) and reduce reliance on the private automobile. Placer County Project PC3015.
properties.FundingSources: North Tahoe Community Alliance; Placer County General Fund; Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax; Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) - California

properties.ProjectName: Upper Griff Creek Bridge Replacement
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project will replace a log bridge spanning Griff Creek that collapsed in 2013. Since its collapse, the public has been traversing through the creek to gain recreational access. This use has degraded the sensitive stream environment. 

The USDA Forest Service, Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit applied for and was awarded a California State Parks OHMVR Commission grant in August 2020 for $243,618 to replace the bridge. 

Conservancy staff received authorization from their Board in June 2021 to provide up to $150,000 in Habitat Conservation Fund (HCF) funding to serve as a match to the LTBMU grant. 

Anticipated construction of the new bridge will begin August 2026.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: TART Only -Free to the User Transit
properties.ProjectDescription: This free to the user transit would reduce farebox revenue by $403,000 annually, and incur $375,000 added operating costs, however it would increase transit ridership, therefore reducing reliance on the private automobile and improving Town Center roadway and intersection level of service.
properties.FundingSources: Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax; Private (Business); Town of Truckee General Fund; Truckee Tahoe Airport District

properties.ProjectName: West Shore Highway Crossing Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project is to construct various enhanced crosswalks to increase safety, improve traffic flow, and increase neighborhood and recreation access along Placer County's West Shore, utilizing both permanent and temporary infrastructure improvements. 

Phase I improvements are complete. Additional planning for future improvements continues.
properties.FundingSources: California Active Transportation Program (ATP) Funds - State; Placer County General Fund; Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax

properties.ProjectName: Inter-Regional Rail Capital Corridor to Truckee to Reno - Operation
properties.ProjectDescription: Although outside of the basin, this project is supporting and collaborating with our MPO and RTPA partners from the Capital to Reno to see expanded passenger rail services. The Corridor includes connections from Sacramento to Truckee and on to Reno, where many Tahoe visitors start their trip. Arriving by rail and connecting to regional buses is a part of the future vision to expand travel options. This project is supported by the Bi-State Consultation on Transportation and included in 2018 California State Rail Plan and the Trans-Sierra Transportation Coalition.
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Regional Planning Agency

properties.ProjectName: South Lake Tahoe Airport Improvement Project
properties.ProjectDescription: This project includes on-going Capital, Operations and Maintenance activities at the Lake Airport. This program is funded by the Airport Enterprise Fund operations budget and through grants from the Federal Aviation Administration and the State of California.  These include forest fuel reduction and fire resilience in areas surrounding the airport, and habitat modification to reduce the likelihood of wildlife/aircraft collisions.  All efforts are supported for regulatory compliance through a contract Registered Professional Forester and a contract Wildlife Biologist.  Project completed on November 19, 2021.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Soil Conservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE); Lake Tahoe Airport Enterprise Fund

properties.ProjectName: Lower Wood Creek Water Quality Improvement Project - Phase 1
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription:
This water quality improvement project in a priority treatment area in Incline Village reduces the amount of fine sediment washing into the lake and help Washoe County meet its milestone of the Lake Tahoe TMDL and improve lake clarity. 

Tasks include installation of stormwater treatment BMPs, shoulder stabilization, and culvert improvements. Benefits include improved stormwater quality release to Wood Creek & Lake Tahoe, increased protection and stream function for Wood Creek riparian and SEZ and greater TRPA Stormwater Program collaboration for BMP compliance. The project (Phase 1 & 2) is expected to earn Washoe County 30-40 credits in the Lake Clarity Crediting Program.
properties.FundingSources: 319 Funds; SEZ Mitigation Funds; Tahoe Bonds Act; WQ Mitigation Funds; Washoe County General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Upper Third & Rosewood Creeks Water Quality Improvement Project - Phase I
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This water quality improvement project is located in Incline Village. The area is highly connected to Lake Tahoe and is a priority treatment area due to a relatively large baseline FSP load. The project proposes to install stormwater treatment BMPs and shoulder stabilization within the existing Washoe County right-of-way and undeveloped public parcels, providing treatment for urban stormwater runoff to meet the Lake Tahoe TMDL. This project is on the 5-year list. Washoe County secured planning and design funding and has hired a consultant. The first TAC was held in December 2025. the Project will be implemented in two Phases.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Nevada Division of State Lands

properties.ProjectName: Meeks Meadow Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Restoration of Meeks Meadow and Meeks Creek to improve ecological function of 200 meadow acres and tribal cultural opportunities at Lake Tahoe; also treats dense fuels in 100 acres of upland forest surrounding the meadow. This project will involve partnerships among the Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California, the US Forest Service LTBMU, and California Tahoe Conservancy.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Department of Conservation, Regional Forest and Fire Capacity; National Fish and Wildlife Foundation; Proposition 1; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Upper Truckee River Johnson Meadow Restoration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription:
Acquired in April 2018, Johnson Meadow, is a 206+ acre property located in South Lake Tahoe along the Upper Truckee River. Prior to acquisition the property was privately held and served as a dairy and seasonal pasture. Following acquisition Tahoe RCD is engaged in a comprehensive phased restoration project to benefit; wildlife habitat, water quality, fisheries, recreation, vegetation preservation, soil conservation, and public open space. 
Phase 1 (Complete): Preliminary restoration analysis, planning, and design to a 30%.
Phase 2: (Current Phase): Environmental Analysis and design to final design and permitting
Phase 3: Implementation and construct
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Proposition 1; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Resource Conservation District

properties.ProjectName: Rehabilitate Meyers Creek - Lake Valley State Rec Area Reach
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Restore Meyers Creek (a tributary/infeeder stream) in vicinity of Hole 18 of the Lake Tahoe Golf Course in Lake Valley State Recreation Area.  The golf course was constructed in late 1950's (prior to current standards for erosion and water runoff control) and stream was channelized into a ditch.  Project includes construction of a more sinuous channel and revegetation to improve value as wildlife habitat.  This project is associated with proposed Upper Truckee River Restoration at Lake Tahoe Golf Course.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: 2016 NDF-SFA Fuels Reduction and Community Education and Outreach - Forest Thinning Component
properties.ProjectDescription: This project will reduce hazardous fuels and restore forest health on 20.5 acres of privately owned property within the Wildland Urban Interface of Incline Village, NV.   There are 27 homes within and adjacent to the project area and 670 more homes within one-quarter mile. Two of the parcels serve to connect current and planned fuels reduction projects on federally owned land managed by the USFS.  Crews will hand thin hazardous fuels to reduce potential fire behavior to a level that permits direct attack by first responders. Cut material will be piled and burned, or left on site in preparation for understory burning.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Division of Forestry; North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District

properties.ProjectName: Highway 50 Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: This project reduced the risk of catastrophic fire and resulting damage to communities by reducing wildland fuels within the Wildland Urban Interface (WUI). The project areas were all located within the Defense Zone of the Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District WUI and are all immediately adjacent to U.S. Forest Service Lands that have been treated.  The project was composed of 138 acres over 6 units.  The largest unit was a 100 acre property located between the communities of Round Hill and Zephyr Heights.  The other units average 7 acres and was located within communities along Highway 50 from Stateline to near Glenbrook.
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: SNPLMA Round 16 Sub Grant - NV Regional Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: This project has reduced hazardous fuels on lands within the Wildland Urban Interface Defense Zone of Incline Village, NV. 298 acres was treated using hand thinning, and understory burning. It has served to complement near-by fuels reduction projects, and previous treatments where 1st entry hand-thinning has been completed. The project is located near critical water treatment facilities, which are critical for fire-flow in the event of a wildfire, and potential evacuation centers should wildfire be active in the area.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Private Property Owners; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Glenbrook Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The Glenbrook Fuels Reduction Project is a forest fuels reduction project that will create a shaded fuel break on between 161 and 200 acres of overstocked forest within the defense zone of the wildland urban interface in the region.   The proposed project is designed to modify fire behavior and reduce flame lengths to 4 feet during 90th percentile fire weather.  This type of forest thinning project will enable firefighters to engage in structure protection in the event of a wildland fire.
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Diamond Peak Lodge Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The Diamond Peak Lodge Fuels Reduction Project reduces hazardous wildland fuels on 63 acres of local government owner land in the wildland-urban interface of Incline Village, NV to mitigate wildfire risk to the community and improve forest health. There are 500 condominium units near-by. The project removed ladder fuels, reduced dead and downed debris, increased crown to base height, reduced brush height and continuity and thinning trees from below to reduce potential fire intensity and protect nearby resources from catastrophic wildfire.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Upper Diamond Peak Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The Diamond Peak Planning Area is within the Defense and Threat Zones of the Wildland-Urban Interface of Incline Village, Nevada. Adjacent high density residential developments include Tyrolian Village and Bitterbrush Condominiums. A fire in the area could restrict the limited evacuation routes for the 500 nearby residences. Fuel reduction treatments provide a safer working environment for firefighters, protect public evacuation routes, and introduce tactical opportunities to redirect a fire approaching from the south. There are 130.5 treatable acres within the larger project area. Smaller projects will serve to treat these acres over time and as funding can be secured.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District

properties.ProjectName: LTNSP Interpretive Facilities Upgrades
properties.ProjectDescription: This project involves the installation of new interpretive panels along the East Shore Trail and updates the existing interpretive panels at Memorial Point Rest Area.  The interpretive panels were installed in 2020 and 2021.  The project was completed in 2020.  The East Shore Trail and Memorial Point had approximately 460,000 visitors in 2022.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Nevada State Parks

properties.ProjectName: Marlette Creek Restoration and SR28 Crossing Improvement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project near Thunderbird lodge on Lake Tahoe's east shore proposes to restore a portion of Marlette Creek to improve stream function, water quality, and fish habitat and provide erosion control and stormwater treatment at directly connected outfalls from SR 28. 
Specifically (1) Capture and treat State Route 28 stormwater runoff prior to entering Marlette Creek by installing treatment at each stormwater outfall.(2) Repair incision and stabilize the bed of S. Fork of Marlette Creek and provide fish passage. (3) Provide fish passage at the SR 28 culvert. (4) Stabilize SR 28 shoulders, road embankments, and dirt parking areas that are directly connected (5) alleviate ponding on SR28.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Nevada Department of Transportation; Nevada Division of State Lands; Nevada Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Meeks Bay Ecosystem Restoration (Planning & Design)
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Meeks Bay restoration project involves the planning for the future of the marina, and restoration of the Meeks Creek lagoon. The shallow warm waters of the marina create a breeding ground for Aquatic Invasive Species. The desired condition is to restore the lagoon to a natural condition while providing a recreation experience which is lighter on the landscape. In addition, the project includes upgrades to current camping and day use recreation facilities and opportunities. Phase 1 (planning & design) est. $2 million; Phase 2 (implementation and Hwy 89 bridge replacement) est. $11 million.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Lakeside Beach and Lakeside Marina Aquatic Invasive Plant Control UV Light Pilot
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: This project tested UV-C light technology in two lake environments, an enclosed waterbody (marina) and an open water body (beach littoral) system, for the treatment of aquatic invasive plant infestations. The technology has previously shown success in laboratory testing where results indicated complete mortality of plants and plant fragments treated with UVC light. In this study, a decrease in plant percent cover, mean plant height, and thus plant density, was observed. The results of this study demonstrated the efficacy of this method as a useful tool for controlling aquatic invasive plants and provided information to support future environmental document analysis and permitting needs.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Private (Business); Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Polaris Creek and Wetland Restoration, Phase I Planning
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The creek and wetland complex found along Polaris Creek has been significantly impaired due to development of residential and recreational facilities. The degraded wet meadow habitat areas adversely impact the associated fish and wildlife habitat values, and these disturbances have significant impacts on water quality, floodplain processes, and fish passage. In Phase I, an Opportunities and Constraints Feasibility Analysis has been conducted to explore the restoration potential of the Polaris Creek and Wetland complex while also addressing and accommodating recreational uses that currently occur at this site; a ball field, playground, campground, and restroom/parking facilities.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: Proposition 1; Tahoe City Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: Sand Harbor Aquatic Invasive Asian Clam Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: A population of Asian clams was discovered in Sand Harbor in 2015.  Surveyors estimated the population size at approximately 1.5 acres in the boat landing area of Sand Harbor- Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park.  Prior to work commencing, the population was estimated at 6 acres.  Once treatment began in 2017, divers discovered clams in additional areas.  The infestation was estimated to be over 25 acres in extent. With the larger infestation, the approach focused on maintenance rather than localized eradication. Three rounds of barrier relocation occured that treated a total of approximately 9.3 acres. Barriers were removed in June of 2020. See projet images for post-project results.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe License Plate Program; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Section 108 U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (TRPA); Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: North Shore Sugar Pine Restoration for Mountain Pine Beetle Outbreak Recovery
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Native Vegetation and Forest Communities
properties.ProjectDescription: Our project will collect seedlings from 100 local and diverse sugar pine trees from Crystal Bay to Tahoe City for reforestation and mountain pine beetle outbreak recovery. Five years of drought has resulted in significant mountain pine beetle-mediated mortality in sugar pine trees on the north shore of Lake Tahoe. We will collect and cultivate sugar pine seed and seedlings in 2017-2018 so that in 2020 2-year old seedlings can be out-planted at north shore restoration sites at Tahoe Vista (USFS, CTC Lands), Carnelian Bay (USFS, CTC Lands), Dollar Hill (CA State Parks and CTC lands), Tahoe City (USFS and CA State Park Lands), and Crystal Bay (NV State Lands and USFS), and private landowner's.
properties.LeadImplementer: UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe City Caltrans Yard Relocation and Restoration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Caltrans Maintenance Yard is currently located in a highly sensitive area along the Truckee River in Tahoe City, CA. This project is to plan the relocation of the maintenance yard to a more suitable industrial area and  restoration of the original site to a more natural landscape.  It includes plans to restore the area which will include removal of facilities and contaminated soils and restoring SEZ to its original function to improve treatment of runoff flowing into the Truckee River. This site will also increase public access and enhance recreation opportunities. 

The plan has been completed.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Water Quality, Noise
properties.FundingSources: Proposition 1

properties.ProjectName: TSRA SNPLMA Round 16 Hazardous Fuels Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: The TSRA SNPLMA Round 16 Hazardous Fuels Reduction project thinned forest stands and reduced fire fuels on 4 acres of Tahoe State Recreation Area property. This project was designed to reduce tree densities in order to modify fire behavior to reduce the potential for a catastrophic, stand replacement fire and increase the protection of life and property. Thinning by hand crews reduced ladder fuels, diseased trees and promotes large resilient residual trees. Thinned trees and dead and downed woody debris were chipped and or hauled off site.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Bureau of Land Management

properties.ProjectName: Sugar Pine SNPLMA Round 16 Hazardous Fuel Reduction Phase 1
properties.ProjectDescription: The SNPLMA Round 16 Phase 1 project will thin forest stands and reduce fire fuels on 108 acres of Sugar Pine Point State Park. This project is designed to reduce tree densities in order to modify fire behavior to reduce the potential for a catastrophic, stand replacement fire and increase the protection of life and property. Forest thinning with hand crews on 55 acres will reduce ladder fuels, overcrowded/diseased trees and promote the growth of large resilient residual trees. Thinned trees and dead and downed woody debris will be chipped or piled to burn. 53 acres of this project will be treated with understory prescribed fire.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Bureau of Land Management

properties.ProjectName: Spring Creek Road Improvement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The objective for this project was to upgrade the existing Spring Creek Road crossing to safely pass the 100 year flood event and minimize roadway flooding and potential crossing failure. This was delivered by constructing a bridge to replace the existing culvert crossing and reshaping the existing channel.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Rosewood Creek Continuation Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Rosewood Creek Continuation Project seeks to restore an area between two previously completed restorations on Rosewood Creek by constructing in channel grade controls using biostabilization and adding stormwater treatment where it is needed. The project's goals include improving water quality, riparian function, drought resilience, and terrestrial and aquatic habitat. The project completed water quality monitoring on Rosewood Creek that had been ongoing since 2002; the final report was submitted to the Bureau of Reclamation on September 30, 2023.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act; U.S. Bureau of Reclamation

properties.ProjectName: Angora Creek fish passage improvement
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore and Protect Native Fish and Wildlife
properties.ProjectDescription: This project removed a culvert that was a barrier to fish passage and replaced it with a low water crossing that is completely passable to fish. This project, along with culvert retrofits on Angora Creek at View Circle and Lake Tahoe Blvd, make the entire length of Angora Creek accessible to migrating and residential fish.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

properties.ProjectName: Angora Creek restoration project - golf course reach
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: In the mid 1900's Angora Creek was diverted to dry the meadow for grazing. Construction of the Lake Tahoe Golf Course in 1960 on the dry meadow obliterated the eastern third of the meadow and channel. In 1997, the meadow channel was restored by enhancing remnants, constructing new sections of the historic channel and removing dams and drainage ditches. An entirely new channel restored geomorphic function. This two-stage channel was built by excavating a channel and constructing banks with coir fabric encapsulated soil lifts. The project restored geomorphic function, raised the water table and shifted the meadow vegetation to wetter species, improving riparian habitat and water quality.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Angora Creek Restoration Project - Sewer Line Capture
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: A reach of Angora Creek was captured after sewer construction, taking on a new course following a sewer line that runs down the meadow. This new creek alignment ran in a straight line for over 2,000 feet. This in turn caused severe down-cutting of the creek bed and lowering of the water table, resulting in drying of the meadow vegetation and impaired habitat. The creek was suffering from water quality issues as well because there was effluent from the sewer line leaching into the creek and ground water. State Parks implemented a restoration project in 2002. A new meandering channel was constructed at grade with the meadow, and the sewer line channel was backfilled and re-vegetated.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Blackwood  Creek Fish ladder removal  and Culvert Replacement
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Between  2003 and 2006,  the U.S. Forest Service removed a large concrete fish ladder and replaced a large culvert with a bridge, including reconstruction of adjacent stream channels at both sites. These features were replaced with a series of constructed boulder step pools to maintain a stable stream profile, while restoring function in terms of coarse bed load sediment transport and fish passage. https://www.fs.usda.gov/Internet/FSE_DOCUMENTS/fseprd498677.pdf
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Blackwood Creek restoration - Phase 1
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Blackwood Reach 1 project was completed in October 2012. The project was designed to provide a physical structure necessary for this segment of stream to possess desirable geomorphic function and higher quality aquatic habitats in the near future. For more information, see https://www.fs.usda.gov/Internet/FSE_DOCUMENTS/fseprd498677.pdf
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Spooner Landscape Resilience Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Native Vegetation and Forest Communities
properties.ProjectDescription: The Spooner landscape resilience Project (Spooner LRP) is a 300 acre thinning located east and north of Spooner Lake in Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park. This project focuses on removing trees too large for hand crews.  All felled trees will be removed through a service contract using a helicopter. This project also includes enhancing aspen stands by removing designated conifers. The project is designed to increase forest resilience to disturbance events, particularly drought and wild fire. Tree tops and limbs were chipped and delivered to the American Renewable Power 20MW biomass plant in Loyalton, CA. Logs were trucked to the Sierra Pacific Industries mill in Quincy, CA.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe License Plate Program; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Burke Creek Watershed Stormwater Improvements
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This 3 phase project will accelerate the implementation of the improvements identified in the 2014 Burke Creek-Rabe Meadow Complex Master Plan and the Kahle Drive Vision. Any expenditures and performance measures should be reported in each individual project. Phase 1 01.01.01.0150- Kahle Water Quality Basin Implementation is complete, Phase 2 03.02.01.0055- Kahle Complete Street will convert Kahle Drive to a Complete Street and raise the grade of the road to improve capture of stormwater, and Phase 3 01.02.01.0090-Burke Creek/Rabe Meadow Riparian Resoration will restore a straight line stormwater ditch at the end of Kahle Drive to a functioning meadow/SEZ.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Water Quality

properties.ProjectName: Dollar Creek Forest Health Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The Dollar Creek Forest Health Project restores forest health to improve forest resilience to the impacts of climate change, protect upper watersheds where the state’s water supply originates, promote the long-term storage of carbon in forest trees and soils and minimize the loss of forest carbon from large, intense wildfires, and promotes biodiversity.
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE); California Tahoe Conservancy; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Third Creek Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This portion of the restoration project fixed eroding stream banks, restored fish habitat, and restored historic floodplain connections to Third Creek between SR 28 and Incline Way.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District

properties.ProjectName: Lower Rosewood Creek Restoration and Reconfiguration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project moved Rosewood Creek from its alignment that drained directly into Third Creek just downstream of Hwy 28, back to its original alignment which flows into Third Creek just upstream of Lakeshore Blvd. More information on this project can be found in the Third and Incline Creek Watershed Assessment (http://www.ntcd.org/documents/library/3rdandInclineWatershedAssessment.pdf).

The new section of Rosewood Creek has natural processes that prevent erosion and filter out sediment and pollutants before entering Third Creek and the Lake. This project was completed in 2007.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District

properties.ProjectName: Evaluating the Reintroduction Potential of LCT at Fallen Leaf Lake
properties.ProjectDescription: Research funded by SNPLMA was published in the North American Journal of Fisheries Management titled “Evaluating the Reintroduction Potential of Lahontan cutthroat trout in Fallen Leaf Lake”. Recommendations from this study improved survival and management of LCT and are currently being implemented at Fallen Leaf Lake. These actions include: multiple stocking sites around the lake as a reintroduction strategy; sites with increased habitat complexity; small numbers of fish per site; hydroacoustics use to improve lake trout suppression; and stocking during periods of thermal stratification to minimize encounters with predators.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Fallen Leaf Recreational Access Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The Fallen Leaf Lake Area represents one of the largest concentrations of recreational use by visitors and residents in the Lake Tahoe Basin.  The proposed path extension will connect to the existing bike trail network from the City of South Lake Tahoe and the Meyers Community. The Project addresses existing safety conditions on Fallen Leaf Road by moving pedestrians and bicyclists from the roadway to a new shared use path extension reducing conflict hazards.  New parking areas near SR 89 and Fallen Leaf Lake Campground will be evaluated to reduce traffic/off roadway parking impacts. The proposed extension is from Fallen Leaf Campground to Tahoe Mountain Road.
properties.FundingSources: Regional Surface Transportation Program Funds (RSTP)

properties.ProjectName: Marlette Creek Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This project complements the NTCD Marlette Creek SR28 Crossing Retrofit and Restoration Project. The South Fork of Marlette Creek is steep and incised with extensive bank erosion. In 2003, the LTBMU removed a man made dam on the S. Fork channel and created a new channel through the former lake bed. This channel eroded and destabilized following completion of that project and requires in-channel stabilization measures and fish habitat improvement.  NEPA, permitting, and construction for restoration and stabilization of this S. Fork channel reach is included in this project.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

properties.ProjectName: Saxon Creek Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Restoration of Saxon Creek targeting the eroding channel, removal of a fish passage barrier, and restoration of three meadows. The watershed above the road is no longer connected to the floodplain due to previous land uses and conifer encroachment. The project includes NEPA and permitting. This restoration project will occur in three phases. Phase 1: Completed 2018. Replacement of aquatic organism passage barrier at Fountain Place Road.  Phase 2: Completed 2022, Adapt. Mgmt 2023. Restore 1,000 feet of channel and floodplain upstream and downstream of the bridge installation area. Phase 3: Channel and meadow restoration in three meadows (60 acres total). Anticipated implementation 2026.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Blackwood Creek Restoration Phase 4
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription:
Restore approximately 6,000 feet of stream and floodplain by strategic placement of large wood structures and boulders. Four stream reaches are identified for restoration in the Final Lake Tahoe West Restoration Project EA, issued in September 2025.
Impacts were in response to multiple floods occurring over the winter of 2016/17. Two floods exceeded 20-year flood levels. 
Projects are located in untreated areas. Floods caused stream incision, bank erosion and sinuosity loss.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Paradise Park Upper Truckee River Stabilization and Restoration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This project will restore the ecological function of the impaired reach of the Upper Truckee River lying between the Washoe Meadows golf course and the Tahoe Pines public access.  In this reach, streambank erosion impacts the UTR and has destroyed sections of established streamside trails on the east bank upstream of and alongside Lake Baron (which is infested with invasive fish and plant species), and on Forest Service land on the west bank. Restoration activities include re-contouring the vertical-cut streambanks & stabilizing by strategic placement of woody debris and boulders, relocation of streamside trails & creation of low-impact public access, and removal of AIS from Lake Baron.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Soil Conservation, Water Quality
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

properties.ProjectName: Westshore Fire Protection Water Infrastructure Phase 1
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: Madden Creek Water System (MCWS) has only one groundwater source. The Madden interconnection with Tahoe Swiss Village Water System is insufficient due to limited storage and source capacity, which limits the effectiveness.  Interconnection with the McKinney Quail System (MQS) provides sufficient source and storage capacity enhanced fire flows and access to the regional water from the West Lake Tahoe Regional Water Treatment Plant (WLTRWTP).  To provide adequate flow to the MCWS, a water main needs to be upsized in the MQS. In addition, interconnecting Tahoe Cedars Water System with the TCPUD MQS will provide access to a redundant water source, additional storage, and access to the WLTRWTP.
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe City Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: Food Web Interactions Associated with a Lahontan Cutthroat Trout Reintroduction Effort in an Alpine Lake
properties.ProjectDescription: To understand Fallen Leaf Lake food web interactions between nonnative species that prey on or compete with reintroduced LCT a combination of stomach content and stable isotope analyses was used to evaluate trophic characteristics within the aquatic species assemblage. LCT preyed on a variety of prey resources: mysid shrimp, insects, arthropods, signal crayfish and fishes. Diet overlap was greatest between L CT and Mountain Whitefish and both species exhibit a general feeding strategy that allows them to partition prey resources to avoid competitive interactions.  Predation by Lake and Brown Tout on stocked LCT was observed and should be considered in the context of predator management.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Clancy-Pohl Sensitive Land Acquisition
properties.EIPActionPriority: Acquire Environmentally Sensitive Lands for Restoration and Protection
properties.ProjectDescription: The State of NV through the NV Land Bank acquired 7.67 acres of sensitive land in the Granite Springs Subdivision in Lower Kingsbury, Douglas County in 2017. Edgewood Creek flows through the lower portion of the parcel.  The land was verified by TRPA as land capability districts 1b, 1a, 2, 4, and 6 and contains 22,483 square feet of existing/potential land coverage. Existing land coverage/disturbance is being restored using several available funding sources. Land coverage/disturbance restored with TRPA Excess Mitigation Funds has been permanently retired. The NV Land Bank is permanently retiring the parcel from future development and managing the parcel for environmental benefits.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Lands
properties.FundingSources: Excess Coverage Mitigation Funds; Nevada Land Bank

properties.ProjectName: Airport West (Fuels Reduction)
properties.ProjectDescription: Airport West is a forest fuels reduction project that is located on the City of South Lake Tahoe property along the East side of the Lake Tahoe Airport runway.  The unit will be hand-thinned, piled, then burned.  Project completion is expected in 2017.  6 acres total.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Vista Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The aquatic plant removal implemented at Tahoe Vista boat launch is part of a multi-year lake-wide strategy to remove aquatic invasive plants from the nearshore of Lake Tahoe Basin. Eurasian watermilfoil was detected at the boat launch in 2016. Contracted divers installed lake-bottom barriers in 2017 and 2018 to control this infestation. From 2018-2020, divers conducted surveillance monitoring to ensure that a re-infestation of Eurasian watermilfoil does not develop at this site. Funding dependent, this site will be monitored according to the Lake Tahoe Aquatic Plant Monitoring Program (2020).
properties.FundingSources: Proposition 1

properties.ProjectName: Tahoma Roads Water Quality Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: In partnership with El Dorado County, right of way storm water runoff in the Tahoma neighborhood will be addressed.  This watershed crosses county-lines and will be coordinated with El Dorado CSA5 Project.  Project complete.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Elks Club Drive Capital Overlay Rehabilitation Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Pavement rehabilitation and new asphalt concrete overlay of Elks Club Drive from Boca Raton to Pioneer Trail were installed with this project.  Included the construction of rolled curb and gutter from Pioneer Trail to Skyline drive which provides roadway widths for vehicles and bicycles, while eliminating sharp drop-offs at existing edge of road AC swales. The project established Elks Club Drive as a Class III bike route and allowed for a connection from the future Greenway Bike Trail Project. The Greenway is currently planned to cross Elks Club Drive near Boca Raton.
properties.FundingSources: El Dorado County General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Cave Rock Fire Protection Water Infrastructure Phase 1
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: Reconstruction of the Cave Rock Water System to address severely lacking water supply for fire suppression and protection for both municipal and federal lands. The project consists of replacing failing and undersized infrastructure including waterlines, pumping facilities and water storage tanks. Additionally, the improvements will include an intertie to the Douglas County owned Zephyr Water Utility District water system to improve water supply reliability and redundancy. Projected O&M cost saving is reduction in water leak repairs.
properties.FundingSources: Douglas County General Fund; Nevada Division of Environmental Protection

properties.ProjectName: D.L. Bliss Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: D. L. Bliss State Park operates an independent water system that supplies the entire park (including residences, visitor center, campground, beaches and fire hydrants) that was constructed in the 1930's and has not been updated.  The water line crosses under Hwy 89 and leaks continuously, reducing the amount of water available for public and firefighting use, and is at high risk of complete failure.  Project includes: new water plant $400k, expanded catch basin $125k, new SCADA system $250k, new well $310k and replacement of two 25,000 gallon redwood tanks with glass-lined steel tanks $225k.  Project also includes full replacement of all water lines, plus new fire hydrants throughout.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Fallen Leaf Lake/Angora Ridge Trail Project
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Tahoe Area Mountain Bike Association (TAMBA) and the U.S. Forest Service Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit partnered to build nearly 5 miles of new trail in the Angora Fire burn area connecting neighborhoods to Angora Ridge and Fallen Leaf Lake.  In 2017 TAMBA held over 60 volunteer trail days with about 150 volunteers and 2,000 hours of trail building.  In addition, the new 2 mile Lily Lake Trail connects Lily Lake to Angora Ridge.  This project captures the private funding contribution to the project; the USFS contribution is tracked in "Basin-wide Trail BMP Upgrades and Maintenance 01.01.04.0055 
Project video: http://www.tamba.org/homepage/angora-trail-project-year-end-recap/
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: TAMBA; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Assessment of groundwater nutrients and periphyton biomass in Lake Tahoe
properties.ProjectDescription: Understanding the transformation and fate of nutrients in groundwater and surface waters is of critical importance for protecting and managing water resources in lake systems. In this investigation, we collected nutrient samples from groundwater and surface water during a 9-month monitoring period to evaluate the timing and availability of nutrients in the nearshore zone of Lake Tahoe. We estimated seasonal groundwater discharge using continuous hydraulic head measurements in piezometers placed in the shallow lakebed. The results indicate that groundwater and nutrient discharge through the lakebed appear to stimulate periphyton growth along the eulittoral zone of Lake Tahoe.
properties.FundingSources: California Lahontan Regional Water Quality Control Board; U.S. Geological Survey

properties.ProjectName: Carnelian Bay Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: NTPUD owns the Carnelian Bay water system on the north shore of Lake Tahoe which is located at the wildland urban interface in North Tahoe. There are approximately 300 residential and commercial customers in this system.  There was an existing 2,500 linear foot 2-inch diameter watermain that was deficient in fire flows with no fire hydrants. This watermain has been replaced with a new 3,500 linear foot 12-inch watermain with fire hydrants spaced at 500 feet along NLB. The new watermain was extended to the Fulton Water System boundary for a future intertie connection for reliability and redundancy of water supply. This is a high-capacity intertie at 12-inches in diameter.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; North Tahoe Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: South Shore Fire Protection Water Infrastructure -Well #1
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: After the Angora Fire, the Lukins Brothers Water Company developed the 2009 Infrastructure Replacement Plan, an 11-phase plan to bring the system up to current standards. Lukins has successfully completed almost 2 phases, funded exclusively by customer contribution, increasing system-wide fire protection by 40%. A new well is the next key step to increase Lukins overall source capacity, which will also will bring a regional benefit through Tahoe Keys Water and STPUD future intertie projects. This project will allow all future upgrades guaranteed water capacity and will decrease the threat of destruction from catastrophic wildfire in a key area of South Lake Tahoe and adjacent USFS lands.
properties.FundingSources: Private (Business)

properties.ProjectName: Upper Bijou Park Creek Restoration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The Upper Bijou Park Creek Restoration Project is a watershed-scale project seeking to address water quality & flooding issues in a phased approach to provide treatment for urban runoff in an approximately 850-acre watershed that discharges to Lake Tahoe via Ski Run Marina. The City completed Phase 1 in 2018 with the Knights Inn redevelopment, replacing the failing storm drain with new treatment basins and conveyance system. The City is currently finishing Phase 2 of the project (design), focused on the large upper watershed that includes 8 separate projects. Phase 3 (construction) begins with one of the projects, Rockwood to Blackwood, in May 2025. The other projects are currently unfunded.
properties.FundingSources: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act; City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Proposition 1; SEZ Mitigation Funds; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Beowawie Road Slope Repair
properties.ProjectDescription: This project will repair an existing retaining wall along Beowawie Road in Crystal Bay, Nevada. This wall was installed as part of the Crystal Bay Erosion Control Project (1988) and is failing due to extreme runoff during and following the 2017 winter. The failing slope is located within 600 feet of Lake Tahoe, and a complete slope failure would have a negative effect on water quality.
properties.FundingSources: TRPA Operations & Maintenance Funds; Washoe County General Fund; Washoe County Road Enterprise Fund

properties.ProjectName: Douglas County Basin Maintenance and Upgrades - Kingsbury Grade/North Benjamin and Donna/Scott Way
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: To complete basin maintenance and upgrades to two Douglas County maintained stormwater basins within the Tahoe basin.  Both basins are located on property owned by the U.S. Forest Service with an easement provided to Douglas County to operate these basins.  The basins proposed for maintenance are located at Donna Way and Scott Drive (APN 1319-18-301-001) and Kingsbury Grade and North Benjamin Drive (APN 1319-19-202-002). Due to sediment accumulation and vegetation growth the basins no longer hold their original design volume of stormwater.  This project will remove the accumulated sediment and vegetation, restore original basin geometry, and construct a hard articulated block basin bottom.
properties.FundingSources: Douglas County General Fund; TRPA Operations & Maintenance Funds

properties.ProjectName: Rubicon Trail Accessibility Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription: This project involves accessibility improvements to a portion of the existing Rubicon Trail at D.L. Bliss State Park.  Accessibility improvements are in compliance with California State Parks accessibility guidelines and associated legal mandates.  The project will create approximately 1 mile of accessible trail by reconstructing portions of the existing trail surface with minor reroutes and/or the addition of rock retaining walls, benches, parking, and directional signage.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Incline Flume Trail Reconstruction
properties.ProjectDescription: The “Incline Flume” trail is located above Incline Village and is primarily accessed from Mt Rose Highway (HWY 431). It connects to numerous other trails and access points, such as the Tyrolean trail, Diamond Peak access roads and Tunnel Creek trail/road in Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park on the south end. This project provided trail maintenance and major reconstruction of several failed segments. It is popular with trail runners, mountain bikers, walkers and hikers - of all ability levels. This project has been a collaborative effort with Friends of Incline Trails, the USFS, the Tahoe Fund, and many local volunteers.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Recreational Trails Grant; Tahoe Fund; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: North Benjamin Parking Lot Recreation and Water Quality Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription: This project improved the informal parking at Kingsbury Trailhead. Parking was occurring on native surface, and was expanding into surrounding vegetation as the trailhead grew in popularity. Parking lot improvements include: paving and striping, BMPs, a vehicle turnaround and OHV loading ramp, restrooms, and relocating the existing kiosk.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Douglas County General Fund; Nevada State Parks

properties.ProjectName: North Upper Truckee SEZ Restoration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This Project is part of the North Upper Truckee Erosion Control Project series (I & II completed in the 1990s) with the main focus on enhancement of the stream environment zone (SEZ) area along North Upper Truckee Road.  The main goal of the project is to enhance the SEZ area along North Upper Truckee Road from Grizzly Mountain Drive to Lake Tahoe Blvd.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Kingsbury General Improvement District (KGID) Street Sweeper
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: KGID maintains 22 miles of roadway within the Lake Tahoe Basin. The purchase of a new high efficiency street sweeper will enhance KGID’s ability to maintain its roadway system, which will ultimately help Douglas County reduce the flow of fine sediment to the lake and meet its required TMDL mandate.  The County has registered KGID's road network within the Stormwater Tools and will receive TMDL credit for road operations, as long as the road score is at 3.0 or above.  KGID will enter into a contract with Douglas County to sweep the roads according to an approved sweeping schedule.  See https://stormwater.laketahoeinfo.org/RoadRegistration/Detail/3 for more information.
properties.FundingSources: AQ Mitigation Funds; Douglas County General Fund; Nevada Division of Environmental Protection

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay State Park Aquatic Invasive Plant Surveillance and Response
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription:
Annual monitoring is performed by contract scuba divers and the CA State Parks Dive Team to detect and remove any invasive aquatic weeds in Emerald Bay. Emerald Bay was infested with Eurasian watermilfoil and curly-leaf pondweed starting in 2007 and after implementing a removal project that was completed in 2015, this monitoring program was designed and implemented to continue the effort to keep invasive species from establishing in the bay. There is no completion date for this project. It will continue indefinitely. 

See project 01.03.01.0041 - Emerald Bay Aquatic Invasive Plant Control for most recent information.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay SP UC Davis Osprey Spatial Data Analysis
properties.ProjectDescription:
The osprey is a special status indicator species for the TRPA's environmental threshold evaluation. In order to better understand the relationship between osprey breeding success and human disturbance, Parks teamed up with UNR to conduct a spatial and statistical analysis 
from almost thirty years of osprey nesting data in Emerald Bay and D.L. Bliss State Parks.  Emerald Bay comprises of the most concentrated area of active nests around Lake Tahoe and is also one of the most highly visited recreation areas on the lake. Statistical analysis was developed for reproductive success in relation to distance from potential disturbance factors such as roads, trails, and campground facilities.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Forestry - Meadowvale SRA Grant
properties.ProjectDescription: This 10-acre fuel hazard reduction project was designed to protect the south end of Country Club Estates from ignitions originating on U.S. Highway 50.
properties.FundingSources: State Responsibility Area (SRA) Fire Prevention Project Funds

properties.ProjectName: DL Bliss State Park Cultural Resources Inventory
properties.ProjectDescription: Comprehensive survey and documentation of archaeological and historical resources located in park unit. Efforts to identify historic properties in the park involves archival research, reviewing historical maps, and intensive coverage pedestrian survey. The survey will likely identify artifacts, features, and archaeological sites associated with ancestral Washoe occupation along and early Euroamerican land use. Results will be reported in a cultural resources inventory report which will then be used to develop an updated interpretative program for the park unit.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay Maritime Heritage Trail
properties.ProjectDescription: The project developed an underwater interpretative trail to highlight the history of Emerald Bay and Lake Tahoe’s culture of recreation by way of shipwrecks. The bay is the final resting place of several recreational boats, launches, and barges used on the lake during the early 20th century. Underwater interpretative panels were placed at four dive sites in Emerald Bay. Waterproof interpretive cards created for divers are available at the park’s visitor centers, local dive shops, and online.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: North Tahoe Fire Hazardous Fuels Reduction and Defensible Space Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The scope of work for this project was drastically reduced for several reasons. However, 501 of the original 1013 urban lots were treated for fuels reduction to remove shrubs, smaller trees, downed logs, and woody materials. The cut biomass was chipped and removed from the site. The project serves to improve forest health for the larger trees that are retained. It also improves the defensible space for neighboring structures. The hand thinning work was completed in 2021, and the scope of work reduction was approved by the funder early in 2023 allowing for the project to be closed out.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Federal Emergency Management Agency

properties.ProjectName: Lower Wood Creek Water Quality Improvement Project - Phase II
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Phase II of the Lower Wood Creek Water Quality Improvement Project completed most components not constructed in Phase I.  The Incline Village-area project reduced the amount of fine sediment discharging into Lake Tahoe and helped Washoe County comply with its next 5 year milestone of the Lake Tahoe TMDL. Tasks included installation of stormwater infrastructure, treatment BMPs, and shoulder stabilization. Benefits include improved stormwater quality release to Wood Creek & Lake Tahoe.  Phase I and Phase II combined earned Washoe County 44 Lake Clarity Credits.
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Division of Environmental Protection; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Bonds Act; WQ Mitigation Funds; Washoe County General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Upper Truckee River Watershed Partnership
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Greater Upper Truckee River Watershed Partnership is a collaborative initiative that will link a variety of existing resource conservation and restoration programs in the South Shore. The greater Upper Truckee watershed primarily includes the Upper Truckee River and Trout Creek watersheds, as well as adjacent watersheds, comprising most of Lake Tahoe’s South Shore area. The initiative has created two synthesis documents that presents the range of existing projects and a renewed focus on landscape planning for climate resilience. The initiative will continue to evaluate resilience and identify further opportunities for community, forest, and watershed protection and adaptation.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Barton Neighborhood Urban Stormwater Treatment
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The project includes a stormwater treatment basin on California Tahoe Conservancy lands at the intersection of 2nd Street and Helen Avenue and associated overflow conveyances, sediment traps, drain inlets, curb & gutter road shoulder protection, and rock bowls for outlet protection in areas of the neighborhood with inadequate drainage or treatment. The improvements will address significant localized flooding in the the neighborhood. This drainage catchment flows to the Upper Truckee River Johnson Meadow Restoration Project site  (EIP project 01.02.01.0070), which was recently acquired by the Tahoe Resource Conservation District.
properties.FundingSources: California Natural Resources Agency (CNRA); City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Pioneer Trail Safety Improvement Project
properties.ProjectDescription:
Install dynamic speed feedback signs on Pioneer Trail on approaches. 
At intersection, install edge-lines and center lines, intersection warning signs for minor streets, intersection lighting, upgrade pavement markings, and widen shoulder.
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund; Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP)

properties.ProjectName: Ski Run Marina Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Pilot- Laminar Flow Aeration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription:
Laminar flow aeration (LFA) utilizes air diffusers, air compressors and air lines to add millions of very small air bubbles to the entire water column with the purpose of making it an oxygen rich environment. The oxygen rich environment has the potential to increase decomposition of the organic layer at the bottom of a waterbody, or in this case the marina.  The organic layer is used as food for plants and by reducing it there is potential to reduce plant populations as well. This pilot project will test the efficacy of LFA in Ski Run Marina. 

Results are encouraging and additional funds are being sought to research results and expand treatment further into the marina channel (lake-ward).
properties.FundingSources: Ski Run Marina

properties.ProjectName: 2019 North Tahoe Regional Park Multi-Use Trailhead Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription: This project included the restoration of the upper parking lot in the North Tahoe Regional Park and construction of a multi-use regional trailhead that will receive the North Tahoe Trail being developed and constructed by Placer County. This project also developed and constructed paved ADA multi-use access paths to the Tahoe TreeTop Top Adventure Parks course, tennis courts, and the Tahoe Unleashed dog park.  Approximately 62 parking spaces were striped, including three handicap spaces; installation of site amenities included bike repair stations, bike lockers and racks, and a bike wash station; and installed permanent BMPs for parking lot drainage.
properties.FundingSources: North Tahoe Public Utility District; Placer County Park Dedication Fees; Truckee Tahoe Airport District

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Aquatic Invasive Plant Enhanced Fragment Control Pilot
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association (TKPOA) implemented an integrated approach to preventing invasive aquatic plant fragments from spreading into Lake Tahoe. In addition to standard skimming and collecting efforts, TKPOA is experimenting with a boat back-up station, a bubble curtain and "seabins" to prevent this spread. The back-up station allows for boats to remove plants from the boat prior to entering Lake Tahoe proper, the bubble curtain provides a barrier that helps stop fragments from exiting the Keys water ways, along with the seabins that act as a floating collector, collecting fragments stopped by the bubble curtain. This pilot project is in the west channel.
properties.FundingSources: League to Save Lake Tahoe; Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association

properties.ProjectName: SNPLMA 15 Incline Village Prescribed Fire Project
properties.ProjectDescription:
This North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District project reduces hazardous fuels on at least 150 acres, but not more than 544 acres of local government owned land in the wildland-urban interface of Incline Village, Nevada to mitigate wildfire risk to the community and improve forest health.

The project promotes community protection and forest health by utilizing prescribed understory fire to cost-effectively reduce hazardous fuels and to protect life, property, and the environment from the effects of catastrophic wildfire. Understory burns restore resilient landscapes by reintroducing natural disturbance to a fire-adapted ecosystem.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: South Tahoe Greenway-Upper Truckee River Bridge at Johnson Meadow
properties.ProjectDescription: The South Tahoe Greenway - Upper Truckee Bridge at Johnson Meadow Project will build upon the overall South Tahoe Greenway shared use path network through the south shore of Lake Tahoe. The Project aims to construct approximately 1.2 miles of a Class 1 shared use path and replacing a heavily trafficked bridge over the Upper Truckee River damaged by the 2017 winter storms. The Project will provide active transportation users a critical link to Barton Hospital from the west and the Tahoe Sierra neighborhood and the Lake Tahoe Community College to the east.
properties.FundingSources: AQ Mitigation Funds; Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Program (CMAQ); Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) - California; Toll Credits

properties.ProjectName: Pioneer Trail Powerline Undergrounding- Washoan to Glen Eagles
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: Utility undergrounding of 3701 linear feet of powerlines along Pioneer Trail from Washoan to Glen Eagles rd in El Dorado County. Pioneer Trail is a designated scenic corridor. The project helps to obtain scenic quality thresholds.
properties.FundingSources: Liberty Utilities

properties.ProjectName: Liberty Utilities Undergrounding- South "Y" Phase II
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: Utility undergrounding of 0.70 miles of powerline along Lake Tahoe Blvd from Glorene to D Street.
properties.FundingSources: Liberty Utilities

properties.ProjectName: Liberty Utilities Undergrounding- South "Y" Phase III
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: Undergrounding of utilities on Lake Tahoe Blvd from D Street to Sawmill Road.
properties.FundingSources: Liberty Utilities

properties.ProjectName: Liberty Utilities Undergrounding- South "Y" Phase IV
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: 0.35 lines of utilities undergrounded on Lake Tahoe Blvd from Sawmill Road to Tahoe Mountain Road.
properties.FundingSources: Liberty Utilities

properties.ProjectName: Liberty Utilities Sierra Blvd Undergrounding
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: 1.89 miles of utility undergrounding along Sierra Blvd in South Lake Tahoe. This project is done in tandem with the Sierra Blvd. complete streets project: 03.01.02.0004.
properties.FundingSources: Liberty Utilities

properties.ProjectName: Liberty Utilities Pioneer Trail Undergrounding- Black Bart to Washoan.
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: Existing utilities are placed underground through the Rule 20A Program.  The County and City coordinate establishment of underground utility districts in consultation with the utility providers and the public in order to facilitate the work.  Rule 20A projects are focused in areas that 1) undergrounding will avoid or eliminate an unusually heavy concentration of overhead facilities, 2) where the street or road is extensively used by the general public and carries a high volume of pedestrian or vehicular traffic, or 3) the street or road adjoins or passes through an area of scenic interest. This project is located along Pioneer Trail,  approximately from Black Bart Ave to Jicarilla Dr.
properties.FundingSources: Liberty Utilities

properties.ProjectName: Liberty Utilities- Apache Ave Undergrounding
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: 0.75 miles of utility undergrounding along Apache Ave in Meyers.
properties.FundingSources: Liberty Utilities

properties.ProjectName: Liberty Utilities- Pioneer Trail Undergrounding- Elks Club to So. Pines 3500'
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: Undergrounding of utilities along Pioneer Trail from the intersection of Pioneer and Hwy 89 and Elks Club Drive.

properties.ProjectName: South Tahoe Fuels Treatment Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The South Tahoe Fuels Treatment Project area is located on the South Shore of Lake Tahoe in El Dorado County, on National Forest System Lands (NFS) within the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit (LTBMU).  Elevations of the project area range from 6,230 feet to 7,800 feet.  The project would primarily consist of forest thinning and vegetation treatments in areas that have been previously treated within the past 15-25 years to reduce fuels for forest fires and promote healthy and resilient forest stands.  Some areas of the project would be treated for the first time.  The project area is approximately 3,737 acres of NFS lands located in the Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) and general forest.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Stanford Rock Trail Re-route and BMPs
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Area Mountain Bike Association (TAMBA) and the U.S. Forest Service Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit have partnered to improve the Stanford Rock Trail.  Part of the trail that was an eroded section of logging road the trail was converted to singletrack resulting in water quality and recreation benefits.  New sections of trail were built to avert erosion and runoff that will reduce water quality impacts and overall coverage. The road has been replaced with a lower grade singletrack trail to enhance user experience and meet current standards.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Private (Business); TAMBA

properties.ProjectName: Bon Pland Hazardous Fuels Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: This project is an 85 acre fuel break located on both the north and south side of Bon Pland Creek. This is the first major drainage south of Tunnel Creek.  The proposed treatment will augment fuel reduction completed from Sand Harbor north to Tunnel Creek east of Highway 28. Project area is located in the lower reaches, west end, of the drainage.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Marlette Summit Hazardous Fuels Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: This is a 420-452 acre fuel reduction project within Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park located outside of the Marlette basin watershed boundary, south and west of Marlette Lake. Treatment areas will modify fire behavior for wildland fire progressing from the south and west to the east, upslope towards the Marlette basin.  The north unit west of Marlette Lake is approx. 220 acres and the south unit near the Secret Harbor diversion is approx. 232 acres. This proposal has been submitted for funding in SNPLMA Round 19.  Project would connect a large contiguous area where hazardous fuel reduction has been completed in the past.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Glen Alpine Creek Watershed Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore and Protect Native Fish and Wildlife
properties.ProjectDescription: Project will complete environmental documentation to restore physical and biological processes and functions to the natural range of variability to ensure Glen Alpine Creek Watershed is resilient to a changing climate and can support life history requirements of native special status/at risk species. Funding will be utilized to complete needed field assessments and data analysis to determine the existing conditions that will be used to develop a proposed action and associated environmental review with public input. The LTBMU entered a Participating Agreement with TRCD in 2023 to complete environmental review.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: California State Parks WUI Fuel Reduction and Prescribed Fire Program
properties.ProjectDescription: Reduce hazardous fire fuels and implement prescribed fire within wildland-urban interface (WUI) areas of Burton Creek State Park (SP), Sugar Pine Point SP, and Emerald Bay SP.
