Forest fuel reduction project work will include forest thinning with hand crews, chipping (and removal of wood chips), stacking burn piles, pile burning and/or understory burning.   Project will treat a minimum of 200 acres, up to a maximum of 354 acres in: Burton Creek SP (up to 88 acres), Sugar Pine Point SP (up to 196 acres), and Emerald Bay SP (up to 70 acres).  The State Parks crew will be funded by both LTRA funds, and matching funds provided by State Parks.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Incline Park Facility Renovations
properties.ProjectDescription: Improved existing softball/baseball Field #3, located near the Incline Middle School. Improvements including replacement of existing dugouts, backstop repairs, new electronic scoreboard, new batting cage, new sand-based rootzone infield, and drainage improvements.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District

properties.ProjectName: Burton Forest Health Restoration CCI
properties.ProjectDescription: The Burton Forest Health Restoration Project implements mechanical forest thinning and fuel reduction on 60 acres of Burton Creek State Park to the west of Rocky Ridge.  Project improves native forest composition and structure, reduce hazardous fire fuels, promotes increased carbon sequestration through increased future tree growth, and reduces potential greenhouse gas emissions from wildfire.  Treatment methods include mechanical forest thinning with tractors, removal of logs and chipped woody materials for utilization, and restoration/rehabilitation of recreation trail utilized by logging tractors for the project.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: Sierra Nevada Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Kahle Complete Street Project
properties.ProjectDescription: This project proposes to transform Kahle Drive into a complete street by improving drainage, adding sidewalks, bike lanes, crosswalks, a safe intersection, and undergrounding overhead utilities. This 0.5 collector road provides key linkages to the existing Stateline to Stateline bike trail, trails throughout Rabe Meadow, and a Douglas County community center. The current condition of the road is highly degraded, unsafe, and a detriment to water quality and the adjacent public lands.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: AQ Mitigation Funds; Barton Foundation; Douglas County General Fund; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Nevada Community Project Funding/Congressionally Directed Spending; Nevada Division of Environmental Protection; Nevada Energy; Private Property Owners; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Bonds Act; Tahoe Fund; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: U.S. Highway 50 Corridor Collision Reduction Improvements – SR89 “Y” Junction to Pioneer Trail (SHOPP)
properties.ProjectDescription: In El Dorado County on US 50 in South Lake Tahoe from the US 50/SR 89 "Y" junction to Pioneer Trail (PM 75.4/80.0). Install roadway lighting, pedestrian hybrid beacons at mid-block crossing between Truckee Road and River Drive (PM 76.3), Brockway Avenue and Blue Lake Avenue (PM 77.0), and Herbert Avenue and Ski Run Boulevard (PM79.1)., improve bicycle signage throughout the project limit and install a two-stage que box for bike turning movement at multiple locations, add green bicycle lane treatments, enhance the visibility of crosswalks to improve safety for pedestrians and bicyclists, and install a full signalized intersection at Johnson Ave (PM78.8).  EA 4H890
properties.FundingSources: SHOPP Funds

properties.ProjectName: Pavement Preservation - SR 28/SR 89 Junction to Nevada State Line (SHOPP)
properties.ProjectDescription:
On SR 28 near Tahoe City and Kings Beach, from SR 89 to NV/CA State line (PM 0.085/11.0). Rehabilitate pavement, rehabilitate drainage systems, and upgrade facilities to Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards. EA 0J010. 

PLA-28 Rehab Combine project (0J01U) combines PLA-28 Rehab (0J010) and Tahoe City Rehab Loc 2 (0J922).
properties.FundingSources: SHOPP Funds

properties.ProjectName: SR 28 Repair Drainage Infrastructure in Kings Beach (SHOPP Minor A)
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: In Placer County on the north side of SR 28 in Kings Beach from Chipmunk St to Beaver St. Install storm drain. Current drainage system becomes inundated during major weather events and causes a hazard across SR 28. EA 0J250
properties.FundingSources: SHOPP Funds

properties.ProjectName: Caltrans Tahoe City Maintenance Housing Replacement (SHOPP)
properties.ProjectDescription: On SR 89 near Tahoe City, at the Caltrans Tahoe City Maintenance Station. Demolish existing employee housing and construct new dormitory building. EA 4H980
properties.FundingSources: SHOPP Funds

properties.ProjectName: Fuel Reduction Treatment Effectiveness
properties.ProjectDescription: This project involves post-fuel treatment sampling of two paired Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park sites for birds, mammals, ground-dwelling invertebrates, butterflies, and plants. Data is analyzed to assess the effects of fuel reduction activities on wildlife potential, the long-term ecological trajectory of forests and wildlife habitat, as well as genetic analysis of tissue samples from chipmunks at both locations.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe License Plate Program

properties.ProjectName: Slaughter House Creek/ Lot X
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Glenbrook Homeowners Association (GHOA), in cooperation with Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District (TDF) and Nevada Environmental Consulting (NVENV) are implementing a wildfire fuels management and habitat restoration project in Slaughterhouse Meadow . This 7 acre common area parcel is owned by GHOA. The prescribed burning of dead and live willow fuel in the riparian zone assists with concurrent habitat restoration efforts being conducted to address mosquito issues and restoration of human caused alterations to the wetland hydrology.  
Forest fuels treatment also took place at Lot X, a nearby parcel. TImber was cable yarded to the old HWY 50 road where the wood was processed.
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District

properties.ProjectName: Mysis Shrimp Removal
properties.ProjectDescription: Some of Tahoe's measured clarity decline is due to the introduction of shrimp and the subsequent loss of daphnia. Daphnia are exceptionally good at eating small (1-4 micron) algae and inorganic particles which are primarily responsible for Tahoe's clarity decline. Tahoe's warming surface waters, because of climate change, favors small algae because they sink slower. Reducing shrimp abundance to 27/m2 will allow daphnia to exist in the lake and result in improved clarity.
properties.LeadImplementer: UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Nevada Division of Environmental Protection; Private (Business)

properties.ProjectName: Lakeside Beach & Marina Aquatic Invasive Plant Control UV Light Pilot II
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project expanded on the first UV Light pilot project by utilizing lessons learned and increasing the size of the treatment areas. The initial pilot showed promising results in that most treated plants exhibited signs of deterioration 7-10 days following treatment. This second pilot expanded treatment areas within the marina and off-shore locations at 1 acre each. 

This pilot is now complete, and new projects for Lakeside Beach and Lakeside Marina have begun as separate projects, tackling the entire infestation at both locations, using UV and bottom barriers.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Pilot- Laminar Flow Aeration Pilot
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association (TKPOA) implemented a pilot project using Laminar Flow Aeration (LFA) in a six acre area, west of the main lagoon of the homeowner channel. TKPOA investigated LFA's potential to reduce plant growth and/or densities by the increased levels of oxygen LFA creates.  The project was implemented in the spring of 2019 and is now part of the Tahoe Keys Aquatic Weeds Control Methods Test (CMT)- comparing effectiveness of multiple methods to address invasive aquatic weeds in the Keys. Performance of LFA will now be tracked as part of the CMT project.
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association

properties.ProjectName: Highway 89 Corridor Tahoe Trail Feasibility Study
properties.ProjectDescription:
The purpose of the State Route 89 - West Shore Tahoe Trail Feasibility Study is to identify a recommended alignment to complete the Tahoe Trail between Meeks Bay and Spring Creek Road. This is the final section of the West Shore Tahoe Trail and will connect popular recreation sites, including Emerald Bay and D.L. Bliss with a shared-use trail. 

The Feasibility Study was completed in 2022.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Tahoe Regional Planning Agency

properties.ProjectName: Burke Creek/Rabe Meadow Riparian Restoration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The goal of the project is to complete the restoration of approximately 22 acres of Burke Creek and surrounding Rabe Meadow. Activities include partially filling Jennings Pond and constructing islands to prevent flooding and restore wetland habitat, filling man-made ditch on USFS land, improving trail conditions and filling man-made ditches to increase hydrologic connectivity in the meadow, and restoring Burke Creek channel at the Lake outlet.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: IVGID Bocce Courts Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The IVGID community-identified new bocce courts as a priority community service project. The courts were constructed in a community park for all members of the public to enjoy. The project included the construction of four (4) bocce courts, enough to host small tournaments or support a local league. The court complex allows the community to enjoy bocce locally, instead of driving out of town to seek these opportunities, adding a new recreation opportunity.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe City Lakeside Trail Missing Link
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project is the proposed 0.5 miles of Class I bike trail from Fanny Bridge/Dam through central Tahoe City to connect with the Commons Beach boardwalk trail.   

For funding and implementation management, Placer County has split apart the "Tahoe City Complete Streets & Highway Improvements" (EIP # 03.02.01.0024) into two separate, distinct projects.  The reason for the split is due to local funding and accounting of grant money.   Additionally, the two components of the originally-proposed project have separate timelines.
properties.FundingSources: Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax

properties.ProjectName: Burton Forest Restoration
properties.ProjectDescription: The Burton Forest Restoration project will treat 132 acres of forest on Burton Creek State Park.  Located in the wildland urban interface and the State Responsibility Area Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone, this work builds on existing and planned treatments creating a contiguous area of reduced fuel loading, protecting multiple at-risk communities.  Work will strive to enhance ecosystem resilience against catastrophic wildfire, pest invasions, and climate change by, reducing forest fuels and stem densities and increasing heterogeneity and habitat diversity.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation; California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Van Sickle Vision Plan
properties.ProjectDescription: Update to the 2005 Van Sickle Master Plan for the phased construction of new park facilities.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Nevada State Parks

properties.ProjectName: Spooner Lake Front Country Improvements Phase 2
properties.ProjectDescription: Redesign and development of Spooner Lake facilities. Phase 2 will include a lakeside picnic area, additional restrooms, a group event pavilion, a group picnic pavilion, improved pathway access, interpretive and wayfinding signage, picnic nodes, redesigned and enhanced parking lots, and an expanded maintenance area.  Construction began in the summer of 2022 and completed during the summer of 2023.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Nevada State Parks; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: US Forest Service Airport Eastside Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription:
The recently completed Airport East project was a 37-acre hazardous fuels reduction project located within the Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) of South Lake Tahoe, on lands owned by the City of South Lake Tahoe. 

Originally a 52-acre fuels reduction project, costs increases resulted in reduced treatment area. There therefore remains need to secure future funding to complete work on the remaining 15-acres of untreated land.
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: AIS Educational and Rest Area Gazebo
properties.ProjectDescription: Installation of a gazebo at the Meyers Watercraft Inspection Station to act as a shaded rest area and educational center for boaters that are waiting for their boat to be inspected and decontaminated.
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Fund; Tahoe Regional Planning Agency

properties.ProjectName: Lake Forest Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: NTPUD owns the Lake Forest No. 3 water system which is located at the wildland urban interface in North Tahoe at the bottom of Dollar Hill. The water system is comprised of watermains ranging from 2 inches to 8 inches in diameter. The system is deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and does not meet current fire codes. The project would install 3,000 linear feet of new 8- and 10- inch watermains to replace the existing 2- and 3-inch diameter steel watermains. Three new fire hydrants would be installed that would be accessible from North Lake Boulevard.  The new upsized watermains would also be equipped with a connection point for an intertie with Fulton Water
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; North Tahoe Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: Round Hill Fire Protection Water Infrastructure Tank
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: Construction of a water tank to increase water storage capacity by 150,000 gallons. This will increase fire protection and the ability to protect land during catastrophic wildfire .
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Ski Run "Mountain to Marina" Green Infrastructure Planning
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: A green infrastructure approach to stormwater management protects, restores, and mimics the natural water cycle. The project involves planning, analysis, outreach, and technical assistance within the greater Ski Run/ Bijou Park Creek watershed to reduce stormwater pollution from developed parcels and roadways collectively. The project identifies opportunities and constraints for regional treatment, public/private partnerships and green infrastructure solutions that achieve multiple benefits. Work with the community and stakeholders produced support for recommended strategies.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Soil Conservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Brautovich Park SEZ Restoration and Park Rehabilitation Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Brautovich Park SEZ Restoration and Park Rehabilitation was a joint effort between Douglas County and the Nevada Tahoe Conservation District (NTCD).  The Project restored over a half acre of a Douglas County-owned parcel (APN 1319-18-401-003) to historic stream environment zone (SEZ), relocated the existing baseball field and playground to less sensitive lands within the parcel, and upgraded the parking and water quality features to help achieve the Lake Tahoe TMDL.  The reconfiguration of the site incorporated improved stormwater treatment and erosion control to bring the parcel into BMP compliance.
properties.FundingSources: Douglas County General Fund; Private Property Owners; SEZ Mitigation Funds; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Lower Kingsbury Area-wide BMP Retrofit
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The project implemented an area-wide BMP retrofit project that installed linear rock-pool basins, an infiltration basin, double sediment cans with filter inserts and building dripline protection to prevent stormwater runoff from directly entering a tributary to Edgewood creek on constrained public and private parcels off lower Kingsbury Grade in Douglas County, NV. NTCD will work with TRPA to gather documentation to award parcel BMP certificates to associated parcels. NTCD will work with Douglas County to attain Lake Clarity Credits for the project.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Slaughterhouse Meadow Restoration Phase 2
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This project restores 0.7 acres of poor functioning fragmented wetland habitat to functional cold-water aquatic and terrestrial wetland habitat and  addresses mosquito habitat, water quality, wetland function and diversity though the construction of a beaver analog pond structure. This project results in no net loss of wetland acreage.  Total project impacts to a WOUS is 0.70 acres. Total project boundary including upland is two acres. Project  results in approx 30 CY of relocated fill, 10 CY of rock fill for erosion protection along roadway and +/- 1,800 for export of pond material. Plan calls for salvage and reuse of all wetland soils and plants.
properties.FundingSources: Glenbrook Homeowners Association

properties.ProjectName: 56 Acres Master Plan
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Project is the development of a master plan document for the City/County Park known as “56 Acres”.   

The purpose of the master plan is to develop a comprehensive strategy for the project site, facilities, programs and services that is responsive to the community’s demographics, social background, and recreational and health needs. The plan will serve to guide the City in a wide-ranging future capital implementation plan.

Projects resulting from this plan will be separate EIP projects:
1.	Rec Center
2.	Construction of Through Road (Tallac Avenue to Rufus Allen Blvd)
3.	Demolition of existing Rec Center
4.	Design and Construction of a new Campground
properties.FundingSources: Proposition 68

properties.ProjectName: Soroptimist Softball Field Renovation
properties.ProjectDescription: The softball field will be improved with the construction of new fencing, infield soil, outfield new sod and leveling, creation of a warm up area, new scoreboard, new back stop, PA system, bleachers, dugouts, water refill station/fountain, and a pathway from the Middle School parking lot to the new entrance to the ball field.  A portion of the parking lot will be removed in order to allow for the fencing and access to the warm-up area and BMPs will be installed.
properties.LeadImplementer: Soroptimist International of South Lake Tahoe
properties.FundingSources: Soroptimist International of South Lake Tahoe

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay McDonald's Bike Trail
properties.ProjectDescription: Complete reconstruction of a deteriorated bike trail located along the Emerald Bay Road McDonald's.
properties.FundingSources: AQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Permanent Watercraft Inspection Station- Meyers
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Lake Tahoe Watercraft Inspection Program has proven extremely effective and serves as a national model. A permanent location for the Meyers Watercraft Inspection Station has been proposed on California Tahoe Conservancy Asset Lands that will allow the program to have enhanced facilities to maintain protection of Lake Tahoe and provide excellent services to the public.

To stay up to date on the progress of this proposed project, please sign up for updates here: 

https://public.govdelivery.com/accounts/CAELDOR/subscriber/new?topic_id=CAELDOR_777
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Tactical Green Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The project involves watershed planning, stakeholder outreach and implementation of innovative stormwater technologies that reduce TMDL pollutants in the Tahoe Keys community of South Lake Tahoe, California. Project planning uses a regional stormwater treatment approach to identify opportunities for public/private partnerships and installation of innovative LID stormwater treatment.  Implementation of the multi-benefit project will improve water quality, enhance wildlife habitat, increase climate change resiliency, reduce wildfire threat, improve bicycle and pedestrian connectivity, and help protect investments in Tahoe Keys aquatic invasive species control.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: SR 28 Marlette Creek Water Quality and Erosion Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This project proposes to provide erosion control and stormwater treatment at directly connected outfalls from SR 28. Stormwater from State Route 28 will be captured and treated prior to entering Marlette Creek by constructing water quality treatment at each stormwater outfall.  Additionally, the project will stabilize SR 28 shoulders, road embankments, and dirt parking areas that are directly connected to Marlette Creek and alleviate ponding on SR 28.
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Department of Transportation; Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) - Nevada

properties.ProjectName: Glenbrook Underground
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription:
Undergrounding of all power lines in our small community will enhance fire safety, improve reliability of service, improve the scenic quality of the neighborhoods, and reduce insurance costs.  
Homeowners will contribute to a 501.c3 with the sole environmental purpose of putting these lines underground in our small community.  

As of the end of 2024, the project has reached 63% completion. Key progress includes connecting the Glenbrook utility spine to the substation and extending distribution/transmission lines to critical areas such as Back Road, Old Highway 50, Glenbrook Road, and beyond.
properties.FundingSources: Private Property Owners

properties.ProjectName: Sugar Pine SNPLMA Round 16 Hazardous Fuel Reduction Phase 2
properties.ProjectDescription: The SNPLMA Round 16 Phase 2 project will thin forest stands and reduce fire fuels on 150 acres within a 267-acre area of Sugar Pine Point State Park, continuing where Phase 1 left off.  The project is designed to reduce tree densities and surface fuel loading to modify potential fire behavior and reduce the threat of high intensity wildfire.  The project will also restore native forest composition, structure and function.  Forest thinning and fuel reduction treatments will include: hand crew thinning, chipping, pile burning and understory burning.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Lower Rosewood Creek Aquatic Organism Passage Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This project proposes to remove two standpipe/metal culvert crossings installed in 2003 at Incline Way and upstream near an existing multi-use path and replace them with structures that allow for the passage of native salmonids, along with improving the floodplain connectivity in one location between the two culvert crossings.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Tunnel Creek Alternative Trail
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tunnel Creek Alternative Trail is a Nevada Division of State Parks project, with partners such as Nevada Division of State Lands, Tahoe Fund, Great Basin Institute, and TAMBA. This 2.28-mile single-track trail starts at Tunnel Creek canyon's base, linking indirectly to the Tahoe East Shore Trail and the Incline Flume Trail. It addresses public safety issues on the congested, sandy, and steep Tunnel Creek road, responsible for many bike accidents every year. The trail will be built in two phases, expected to be completed by fall 2025.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe License Plate Program; Land and Water Conservation Fund; Nevada State Parks; Recreational Trails Program Funds; TAMBA; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Offshore Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The 2019 Lake Tahoe Region AIS Action Agenda identifies this site as a Tier 1 priority for treatment. Aquatic invasive plant control at this site commenced in September 2020. Diver-assisted suction removal has been the primary method of plant control thus far. In September 2023, an aquatic invasive species, New Zealand mudsnail (Potamopyrgus antipodarum), was detected by contracted divers within the project area. Work was paused to reduce risk of spread of this species.When work recommences, future reporting for this project area will be documented in Project # 01.03.01.0051-South Shore Offshore Aquatic Invasive Plant Planning and Control, occupying all or portions of sub-units 7, 8, and 9.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; League to Save Lake Tahoe; SB630 Funds

properties.ProjectName: Spooner Front Country Hazardous Fuel Reduction
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: This 42 acre project focused on creating defensible space around the new Visitors Center and other existing structures located in Spooner Lake and Backcountry State Park. All roads are managed as fire lanes to help ensure public safety and allow firefighters safe ingress/egress in case of emergency. Thinning prescriptions varied to meet a range of management objectives (i.e. defensible space, firefighter access, forest restoration) and included mechanical thinning, hand thinning, chipping, and pile burning. Wood mulch created through this project was used on-site for revegetation around the new parking lots.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Nevada Department of Transportation/Douglas County Shared Stormwater Decant Facility
properties.ProjectDescription: The Nevada Department of Transportation (NDOT) and Douglas County have a need for a safe and effective way to decant and treat their stormwater from various maintenance operations in the Lake Tahoe Basin. The proposed facility will allow primary and secondary treatment of stormwater treatment byproducts such as water from drop inlets or sweeper material with wastewater eventually discharging to the sewer system. The facility also provides a safe and environmentally-friendly place to store materials and wash equipment.
properties.FundingSources: Douglas County General Fund; Nevada Department of Transportation

properties.ProjectName: Fallen Leaf Lake SCUBA Clean-up
properties.ProjectDescription: In 2023 the CUTL dive team covered 4.84 underwater miles at Fallen Leaf Lake as part of a pilot litter collection project. During this remediation, the team found Fallen Leaf Lake to be the dirtiest lake in organizational history, based on litter items collected by mile. Over 10 days, the team collected 8,322.9 lbs of litter including 3,310 litter items. Notably the team removed 644 tires from Fallen Leaf Lake. The team was not able to complete a full circumnavigation of Fallen Leaf Lake due to a lack of funding. Clean Up the Lake is actively looking for funding in order to return to the lake to complete the pilot litter remediation and complete the establishment of a baseline litter dataset
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: Tif's Spiked Lemonade

properties.ProjectName: NTFPD Wildland Urban Interface Hazardous Fuels Reduction (NTFPD WUI HFR)
properties.ProjectDescription: North Tahoe Fire Protection District will reduce hazardous fuels on at least 300 acres, but not more than 700 acres of highest priority WUI Defense Zone areas within North Tahoe and Meeks Bay Fire Protection Districts as identified in the Lake Tahoe Basin Community Wildfire Protection Plan. These treatments will improve forest health and reduce the threat of catastrophic wildfire, protecting life, property, and critical infrastructure in the Lake Tahoe Basin.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: US 50 at Warrior Way Safety and Drainage Improvements
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The project modified the intersection of US 50 at Warrior Way by adding traffic signalization and pedestrian crossing infrastructure. The project also proposes to construct a storm drain to capture and convey roadway runoff to a proposed water quality basin.
properties.FundingSources: National Highway Performance Program; Nevada State Gas Tax

properties.ProjectName: Sand Harbor Hazardous Fuels Reduction/Defensible Space
properties.ProjectDescription: The primary objectives of this project were to reduce hazardous fuels and create defensible space within 150 feet of park infrastructure at Sand Harbor. Mature brush was hand thinned or masticated to reduce continuous fuel beds.  Large willow clumps were cut in select locations adjacent to park infrastructure.  Hand thinning of the forest focused on reducing tree densities and removing bark beetle infested and dead trees. Material not burned or hauled off-site was chipped and used on-site in high use recreation areas. Dwarf mistletoe in Jeffrey pine was reduced in a portion of the project.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Castle Rock Peregrine Falcon Habitat Protection
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore and Protect Native Fish and Wildlife
properties.ProjectDescription: Educational signage has been installed on route to a popular hiking and climbing destination and peregrine falcon nesting site. The goal is to reduce stress on the nesting peregrine falcons at Castle Rock by educating hikers and climbers of seasonal closures and nesting disturbance. Project includes installation of permanent educational signage at the North Benjamin Trailhead and temporary signage during the nesting season.
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Upper Diamond Peak Hazardous Fuels Reduction and Healthy Forest Restoration Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Decades of fire suppression and increased development in forested areas have led to overstocked stands that present extreme fire risks to the Incline Village community and surrounding land. This project has reduced hazardous fuels and restored forest health on 72.6 acres of Incline Village's Diamond Peak Ski Resort property and privately owned land. The project complements previous, ongoing and planned fuels treatments as part of a larger cross-boundary forest management strategy, which will contribute $4.6 million in match/leverage. Reducing fuels in this FAP Priority Area will lower the probability of catastrophic wildfire, protecting local communities.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District; Nevada Division of Forestry; Private Property Owners

properties.ProjectName: Forestry Education & Job Placement Program
properties.ProjectDescription: Lake Tahoe Community College's Forestry Education & Job Placement Program will increase the skilled workforce urgently needed to accelerate the pace of forest treatments in Tahoe and will subsequently reduce wildfire risk. The program offers stackable certificates leading to an associate degree in forestry with transfer opportunities to 4-year programs. By offering multiple education and career pathways for youth and adults, the program aims to recruit traditional and non-traditional students and place students in jobs during and after program completion.
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE); California Tahoe Conservancy; Good Jobs Challenge; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Lake Mill Meadows Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This project addresses two ongoing habitat concerns at Lake Mill Meadow. This project 1) Adjusts the hydraulic gradient to facilitate terrestrial obligate wetland vegetation, and 2) mitigates an erosion feature in the lower meadow that was altering the meadow hydrology and causing a drop in the groundwater table resulting in loss of wetland/meadow habitat. Project Completed October 2021
properties.FundingSources: Glenbrook Homeowners Association

properties.ProjectName: Bijou Park Class 1 Bicycle Trail - Greenway Connector
properties.ProjectDescription: This project proposes to construct 0.6 miles of bicycle and pedestrian trail that would link the Al Tahoe Mobility Project constructed in 2020 (Johnson Blvd & Al Tahoe Boulevard) with the CTC Greenway Trail Phase 1B (Constructed 2021).  The trail would be entirely located within the City's Bijou Park Property.  This project is a high priority project with the Community Mobility Group and the Measure S Joint Powers Authority Bicycle Committee.
properties.FundingSources: Community Development Block Grant Funds (CDGB)

properties.ProjectName: Johnson Boulevard Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription: Project proposes to modify the existing Johnson Boulevard travel way from the southern limits of Al Tahoe Boulevard to the northern limits of Fairway Avenue per preliminary concept design contained within the LTUSD Safe Routes to School Master Plan by reducing roadway width, construction of a Class 1 bicycle trail, construction of sidewalk and ADA improvements, construction of minor drainage improvements as required for project, installation of pedestrian safety lighting, and pave and stripe roadway for Class II bicycle lane on west side.  The total project length is estimated to be 4,900 linear feet (.92 miles).
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Cave Rock Water Quality Improvement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Over the past few years, the Cave Rock unit of Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park has experienced a high level of unauthorized walk-in visitor use and user-created trails have led to severe slope erosion and sediment runoff above the beach area at the southern end of the Park. This project will prevent walk-in visitor access through temporary and long-term fencing, and repair existing erosion through a mix of slope stabilization and revegetation. The project will also assess the existing Tahoe yellow cress (TYC) enclosure in the Park for possible relocation or expansion to protect the sensitive habitat from human use.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Lands
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Division of State Lands; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Delineation of Asian Clam Populations at Sand Harbor State Park
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: This project implements underwater surveys for Asian clams in Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park at Sand Harbor to determine recolonization rate following treatment and delineate current extent of the invasive Asian clam populations. Surveying and continued monitoring took place over three years, with number of dead and live clams recorded at each dive’s conclusion. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) flights will also be conducted to obtain aerial data on metaphyton coverage, and remote sensing of the clam survey area with UAV imagery will be used to assess potential growth of metaphyton associated with clam populations.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Lands
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Rubicon Trail and Emerald Bay Site Improvement Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Reconstruct approximately 800’ of the Rubicon Trail; install two new interpretative panels, two new benches, install symbolic fencing, and directional signage; remove redundant trails and trail features; thin trees and vegetation to improve access to the shore of Emerald Bay, enhance views of Fannette Island, protect vegetation and water resources, clarify paths of travel for easier visitor use, and improve day-use trail network near the Vikingsholm Castle located at Emerald Bay State Park.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Hicks Erosion Control Project Phase I
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The Hicks Urban Parcel is owned by the State of Nevada and is adjacent to Incline Creek. In the past few years, the site has experienced large scale surface erosion. The first phase of this project will analyze sources of erosion by completing hydrological, geotechnical, and topographical surveys, and prepare conceptual and 75% design documents for restoration and stabilization of the Hicks Urban Parcel. Construction of erosion control and hillside stabilization measures will take place in subsequent phase.
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: SR 28 Corridor Collision Reduction Improvements - Mackinaw Road to Grove Street (SHOPP)
properties.ProjectDescription:
In Tahoe City on Route 28 from Mackinaw Road to Grove Street. Place green colored bike lane treatment or High Friction Surface Treatment (HFST), install recessed striping, rectangular flashing beacons, and signs, and construct curb ramps.  EA 0J922. 

PLA-28 Rehab Combine project (0J01U) combines PLA-28 Rehab (0J010) and Tahoe City Rehab Loc 2 (0J922).
properties.FundingSources: SHOPP Funds

properties.ProjectName: Máyala Wáta Restoration Project (Phase 2)
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Máyala Wáta Restoration project seeks to restore approximately 283 acres of meadow habitat in Meeks Meadow though a number of techniques including conifer removal, vegetative treatments, and cultural prescribed fire. The overall goals for the project is to increase the density and frequency of culturally significant plants for traditional uses, and to get the Washoe people back on their homelands in the Tahoe Basin.
properties.LeadImplementer: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California
properties.FundingSources: Proposition 68; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; U.S. Forest Service; Wildfire Resilience

properties.ProjectName: Elgin Street Sweeper
properties.ProjectDescription: Purchase of one (1) Elgin Street Sweeper to replace one (1) failing unit.  Project is requesting $75,000 in AQ Mitigation Funds and $75,000 in WQ Mitigation Funds.   AQ & WQ Mitigation funds will be matched with $146,000 in City of South Lake Tahoe General Funds.   Total cost of unit is approximately $296,000.
properties.FundingSources: AQ Mitigation Funds; City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Airport Eastside Hazardous Fuels Reduction Project-Phase II
properties.ProjectDescription: Hazardous fuels reduction in the wildland urban interface (WUI).  Specific to this project is improving controllability of fuel along U.S. Highway 50 (Community evacuation route) and to provide defensible space to critical airport infrastructure (apron areas used during wildland fire events and airport structures adjacent to areas in yellow.)  100’ is defensible space   Concludes protecting the eastside of the airport property boundary full length.  Total project treatment area is 20.65 acres.  This project includes a CEQA Tahoe Program Timberland Environmental Impact analysis for hazardous fuels reduction work funded by Round 18 by SNPLMA
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Prescribed Fire Treatment at Airport for 2020-2021 CCC Treatment of Trees less than 14" dbh
properties.ProjectDescription:
California Conservation Corps (CCC) were hired by the Airport to perform forest health hazardous fuels reduction on trees located outside of the Stream Environment Zone.  Treatment occurred in 2020 and 2021 concluding in November 2021 (South Lake Tahoe Airport Improvement Project).  
All trees were hand cut and stacked into burn piles for future prescribed burn after wood has cured.  El Dorado AQMD permits must be secured prior to any ignition. Per TRPA MOU MM a Qualified Exemption is required for this project. 
CCC will be hired to perform prescribed burns on behalf of the airport.
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Fuel treatment effectiveness surveys, Caldor Fire
properties.ProjectDescription:
The project surveyed fuel treatment areas impacted by the Caldor fire to measure fire effects to vegetation using standard measures of fire severity and tree mortality. This work compliments studies being carried out by other teams of fuel treatment influences on fire-fighting effectiveness and structure protection. 
A link to the report and more information in the project details below. 
The study found: Across all treatment types, trees were 3x more likely to survive fire in treated areas. Fire severity measures were significantly lower in treated versus untreated areas. The most effective fuel treatment was multiple entry mechanical and hand thinning followed by mastication.
properties.FundingSources: League to Save Lake Tahoe; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay Gateway Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Modify and modernize the Vikingsholm Parking lot, which was constructed in the 1960's, to accommodate shuttle transport, tie in with planned bike path, rectify seep holes in parking area, install BMPs, remove concrete islands and redesign for snow removal, install a contact station and welcome center for visitors and staff with educational and interpretive elements; install ADA Accessible restrooms, install a covered veranda, provide for emergency response access and response resources, install solar power electrical systems, install security gates, upgrade and modify the entrance for visitor enjoyment, ADA access, and public safety for this iconic park.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Enhanced tributary monitoring to assess Caldor Fire impacts
properties.ProjectDescription:
Enhance the Lake Tahoe Interagency Monitoring Program to:

(1) Increase the number of samples collected per year by 5 at impacted watersheds of at Upper Truckee at South Lake Tahoe and Trout Creek at South Lake Tahoe sites (an increase from 21 to 25 samples per year) and one control at Third Creek at Incline Village with the option for up to all LTIMP locations.

(2) Analyze water-quality samples for post-fire impacts on ammonium and dissolved organic carbon. Constituents will be added at 2 impacted and 1 control site (26 samples a year).
properties.FundingSources: California Lahontan Regional Water Quality Control Board; Tahoe Regional Planning Agency; U.S. Geological Survey

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay Vikingsholm Pier Rebuild
properties.ProjectDescription: Rebuild the Vikingsholm Pier in Emerald Bay. The Vikingsholm Pier visitor dropoff walkway is in need of repair: the entire pier is in a state of deterioration with compromised visitor safety and is not accessible to boats during low water years nor is it compatible with water taxi service. The pier and path to the historic core of the Vikingsholm estate are not ADA accessible from the lake.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay Vikingsholm Restroom Replacement
properties.ProjectDescription:
Replace and improve the Emerald Bay restroom facility. 
Emerald Bay welcomes up to 1,000 boats per day and more than 10,000 visitors per day during busy summer weekends. Vikingsholm has one very old restroom which was constructed in the 1960s - due to its age, the restroom is deteriorating and is not ADA compliant.  This is a beautiful and iconic park and the restroom facility that serves these thousands of visitors is no longer up to the task.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay Boat Camp Pier ADA Access to Campground
properties.ProjectDescription: Improve trail access from the proposed ADA Accessible Pier to the Boat Campground for ADA access and compliance.  Campsites will also be improved for compliance and access.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe State Recreation Area Campground Pier Rebuild and ADA Access
properties.ProjectDescription: Construct a new pier at Tahoe State Recreation Area Campground in Tahoe City. With the completion of the bike path adjacent to the campground, substantial increased use of campground trails and pier is causing degradation of infrastructure.  Some boards on the pier have been replaced for public safety but the pier and its pilings need to be rebuilt in entirety. Additionally, CDPR would like to improve ADA access from the paved bike path to campground trails and pier.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Sugar Pine Point Bike Trail Repair, Beach Access, and Erosion Control
properties.ProjectDescription: The paved bike path was installed through the Z'berg preserve without a guiding maintenance plan. The paved bike path has deteriorated and is no longer safe for bikes. Visitors ride bikes from the paved bike path down the sandy trail and stair access to the General Creek Mouth Beach, resulting in substantial erosion of very sensitive soils - this erosion runs directly into Lake Tahoe. Required components of this project include erosion control, signage, interpretation, bike rack installation, repaving the existing bike path, and installing appropriate BMPs.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Sugar Pine Point Visitor Center and Historic Water Tower Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Cooperative project with Sierra State Parks Foundation- The existing visitor center is not ADA Accessible, was not designed as a visitor center, and needs major modification to this historic building, and major redesign of educational and interpretive elements. Connected historic water tank element is falling apart and requires major work for stabilization to maintain this important element of the story of the Ehrman Mansion and early Lake Tahoe settlement.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Sugar Pine Point Day Use Foot Bridge Replacement
properties.ProjectDescription: Upgrade footbridge in Sugar Pine Point Day Use area. Current undersized footbridge is causing ongoing erosion issues in General Creek and does not allow for adequate public safety access.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe City Gateway Trail Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Provide formal pedestrian and bike access to the extensive Burton Creek State Park trail system directly from Tahoe City and Tahoe State Recreation Area campground. Tie in with public transit and bike path. Phase 2 will include public Lake Tahoe overlook, picnic area, and pedestrian footpath.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax

properties.ProjectName: Burton Creek SP Interpretive Prescribed Fire Management Trail Loop
properties.ProjectDescription: Showcase over 3 decades of prescribed fire management in different burn plots along a 2.5 mile loop trail system for public education and interpretation on using fire as an essential land management tool in this highly complex urban interface community. Project would include trail upgrades.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Burton Creek SP Access Bridge Replacement
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Goal is to upgrade emergency vehicle access and pedestrian bridge into Burton Creek State Park. Bridge requires replacement due to substantial ongoing erosion issues from the current undersized span over Burton Creek and inadequate size for fire response and public safety access.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Celio Barn Debris Removal and Meadow Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This project proposes to remove hazardous debris from the dilapidated Celio Barn site in Washoe Meadows State Park and restore the natural hydrology and native meadow vegetation. Over the last decade, the barn has collapsed and scattered debris over a 925 square foot area. The barn site will be decompacted to allow native vegetation to grow and surface water to percolate. The STPUD service road has been improved to add water diversion features that will convey water towards the restored meadow site. In 2023, the California Conservation Corps spent 2 weeks removing dense pine growth to further encourage surface water, promote meadow habitat, and improve wildfire resilience.
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Van Sickle Bi-State Park Phase 2
properties.ProjectDescription: This project involves new park improvements at Van Sickle Bi-State Park.  Plans currently call for the construction of employee housing and a maintenance shop.   Employee housing will provide affordable housing to park employees and allow for rangers to be stationed onsite.  An improved maintenance facility will allow park staff to station maintenance personnel onsite.  The facilities will be utilized to support future developments at Van Sickle Bi-State Park.  Construction is anticipated to begin during the summer of 2026.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Nevada State Parks; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Dennis Machida Memorial Trail (Greenway Phase 1C)
properties.ProjectDescription: This project is a continuation of multiple phases of the California Tahoe Conservancy's Greenway Multi-Use Trail Project.  This segment (1C) will provide for a multi-use paved trail from the easterly terminus of Phase 1A at Herbert Avenue, crossing into CTC-owned land connecting up and along Pioneer Trail right-of-way to the limits of Ski Run Boulevard.
properties.FundingSources: American Rescue Plan; California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Van Sickle Bi-State Park Phase 3
properties.ProjectDescription: Van Sickle Phase 3 is an improvement to the Van Sickle Bi-State Park Phase 1.  Nevada State Parks has hired a contractor to design a visitor center, improved parking, and restrooms.  The visitor center will include park offices, a gift shop, and interpretive spaces.  A multi-use paved path is being planned from the visitor to the center to the state border.   The planning team is coordinating with California Tahoe Conservancy to continue the path to Lake Parkway.  An improved stateline monument is being planned for the Nevada/California Stateline that will include additional interpretive opportunities.   Construction is tentatively planned for the summer of 2026.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: CSA #5 Erosion Control Project - Phase 3
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The County Service Area (CSA) # 5 Erosion Control Project includes the developed portions of the northwest corner of the Tahoe Cedars subdivision southwest of Highway 89 between the El Dorado County line and Poplar Street. The Project implemented improvements to reduce the concentration of fine sediment in the storm water which exits the Project area before reaching Lake Tahoe. The Project was split into multiple phases. The final phase (Phase 3) project area is roughly bounded by Placer Street to the east, McKinney Street to the west, and the Placer/El Dorado County line to the north and west.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Local Assessment Funds; Proposition 1; WQ Mitigation Funds

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys East Channel Bubble Curtain
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: Bubble curtains are demonstrating the ability to restrict invasive aquatic plant fragment spread. A bubble curtain system has been installed in the East Channel of the Tahoe Keys to prevent plant fragments from leaving the East Channel and spreading to other areas of Lake Tahoe. The Tahoe Keys Marina is taking over responsibilities for its operation.
properties.FundingSources: League to Save Lake Tahoe; Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association; Tahoe Regional Planning Agency

properties.ProjectName: Stateline Avenue Complete Streets Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The project seeks to rehabilitate Stateline Ave to provide safer pedestrian and bike access, lake access, and improved stormwater infrastructure. Informal dirt parking on shoulders and lack of sidewalk creates conflicts with pedestrians.  Informal dirt parking also generates sediment that runs off directly to the lake. The project looks to replace existing failing pipe with a new stormwater system that includes treatment while simultaneously addressing the unsecured shoulders. Constructing pedestrian and bike enhancements for the major tourist area is supported by The Tourist Core Area Plan. The project will be designed to connect to Park Ave, Lakeshore Blvd, and other regional connections.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Spruce and Blackwood Complete Streets Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The project seeks to improve the multi-modal community access to the Bijou Community School.  Current issues of inadequate pedestrian accessibility and safety, poor drainage and water quality impacts from parking in the dirt would be addressed through new stormwater infrastructure coordinated with new pedestrian and cyclist safety and accessibility improvements. The project will incorporate and evaluate mobility improvements recommended in the LTUSD Safe Routes to School Master Plan. The project will seek to provide improvements along Spruce Avenue and Blackwood Road to provide increased safety and accessibility for pedestrians to connect to existing and future improvements in the area.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities

properties.ProjectName: Park Avenue and Lakeshore Blvd Complete Streets
properties.ProjectDescription: The Complete Streets project would improve the segment of Park Ave and Pine Blvd from Hwy 50 to Lakeshore Blvd to reduce flooding, address sediment from unsecured road shoulders, formalize parking, and improve accessibility and safety for pedestrians. The area has been identified as having drainage problems and lacking adequate pedestrian sidewalks, parking or streetscape elements. The rehabilitation of the roadways would include the construction of bike lanes, sidewalks, or shared use paths.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities

properties.ProjectName: Fallen Leaf Road Rehabilitation Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Fallen Leaf Road is ~5 miles in length from SR 89 to the south end of Fallen Leaf Lake at Stanford Sierra Camp.  The proposed project will complete roadway improvements in three phases: 1) SR89 to the Campground (0.6 miles); the Campground to Tahoe Mtn (1.8 miles), and Tahoe Mtn to Stanford Sierra Camp (2.9 miles).   Proposed improvements will include improving the pavement condition, eliminating substandard roadway geometry, and install drainage improvements to extend the service life of the roadway.  Widening of the roadway from SR 89 to the campground will be evaluated along with paving the existing roadway pullouts from the campground to Tahoe Mountain to improve the safety for all users
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: El Dorado County Transient Occupancy Tax

properties.ProjectName: Ski Run Community Park
properties.ProjectDescription:
Ski Run Community Park is South Lake Tahoe’s newest playground and community gathering space. The park is an example of what the community can accomplish to achieve a common goal to make Tahoe’s outdoor equitable for all.  
The Park includes an iconic 20-foot-tall rope climbing structure, accessible swing, hill slide, ski chair park benches donated by Heavenly Mountain Resort, play lawn, giant picnic table, and climbing boulder. The entire park was designed with accessibility in mind including an ADA parking space, accessible features, and bi-lingual signage. 

Ski Run Park opened in August 2024.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: Private (Business)

properties.ProjectName: SR 28 North Parking, Sidewalk, and Water Quality Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription: The SR28 North Parking, Sidewalk, and Water Quality Improvements includes environmental analysis, final design & construction of 30+ parking spaces (depending on design) north of the existing Tahoe Eastshore trailhead parking at Sweetwater Rd; build a connecting pedestrian path to the new Tahoe East Shore Trail connecting parking areas, 4-6 parking spaces at Rocky Point, address erosion and signage at Sunset Vista pullout, and 2-3 parking spaces for operational employee parking at the Tahoe Eastshore Trailhead, and water quality improvements within the existing NDOT Right of Way as part of the parking improvements. Once constructed, extend no parking zone from Ctry Club Dr to Sweetwater Rd.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: Carbon Reduction Program – Nevada; Nevada Transportation Alternatives (TAP) Funds; Nevada Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) Funds; Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) - Nevada; TTD Interest Income; Tahoe Fund; Washoe County Bond

properties.ProjectName: SR 28 Central Corridor- Sand Harbor to Thunderbird Cove - Trail, Transit, and Safety Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription: The project is located in Washoe County along SR 28, includes design and construction of 1.75 miles of multi-use path between Sand Harbor State Park and Thunderbird Cove, vista pullouts, and safety improvements.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: Carbon Reduction Program – Nevada; Conserve NV; Nevada Department of Transportation; Nevada Highway Infrastructure Program (HIP); Nevada State Gas Tax; Nevada Transportation Alternatives (TAP) Funds; RAISE; Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) - Nevada; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Diamond Peak 25 Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: This 46.8-acre project has completed fuels reduction treatments throughout the Diamond Peak Ski Resort. Most of the ski area has already been treated for fuels reduction through NLTFPD’s previous and on-going projects.  Neighboring property consists of USFS and private property. Funding has already been secured to reduce fuels on the USFS property and NLTFPD is also implementing treatments on the private property as part of their NV Regional Fuels Reduction Project. This project area is the final piece of the puzzle that will connect over 1,000 acres of contiguous hazardous fuels reduction treatments within the WUI Threat Zone of Incline Village.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District; Nevada Division of Forestry; Private Property Owners

properties.ProjectName: North Lake Tahoe Defense Zone Improvement Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District (NLTFPD) will reduce hazardous fuels on 210-620 acres and plan for additional hazardous fuels removal on federal and non-federal lands in the wildland-urban interface of Incline Village and Crystal Bay, NV to mitigate the wildfire risk to the community and improve forest health. The project will be accompanied by two public outreach activities that will showcase fuels reduction treatments and provide education on forest health, fuels treatments, and Fire Adapted Community concepts. These activities will create a better informed and more prepared Fire Adapted Community in Incline Village and Crystal Bay, NV, an area with extreme wildfire risk.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District; Nevada Energy; North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District; Private Property Owners; Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act; Washoe County General Fund

properties.ProjectName: West Shore Water Storage Augmentation
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Project will improve storage capacity to meet fire flows along the west shore of Lake Tahoe. The project will analyze the suitability of 4 water storage tanks, and associated transmission main layout within the TCPUD west shore service area to establish a common static hydraulic grade line, increasing storage capacity to meet fire flows.

Phase I is the construction of two new water tanks
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe City Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: TCPUD Fire Flow Capacity Improvements and Hydrant Installation, Phase I
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription:
This Project provides improved fire flow capacity and fire hydrant coverage across the TCPUD water service areas. This phase occurs within the Dollar Point neighborhood, and will replace 1,500 linear feet of water mains and install additional 4 fire hydrants.

The objective is to improve water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage area.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Tahoe City Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: TCPUD Lower Meeks Bay Water Pressure for Fire Flow
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: The Project consists of the installation of approximately 600 feet of new 8” water main and a pressure reducing valve station to connect the Meeks Bay Vista pressure zone to the Tahoe Hills distribution system. The system experiences severe head loss under fire flows. Providing a northernly connection will greatly improve fire flow at all hydrants along Meeks Bay Avenue and creates a redundant connection to the system in the event of a failure. Project improves water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage area.
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe City Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: Brockway Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: The water system is comprised of watermains ranging from 2 inches to 8 inches in diameter. The system is deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and does not meet current fire codes. The project would install 7,000 linear feet of new 8- and 10-inch diameter watermains to replace the existing less than 6-inch diameter watermains. Fifteen new fire hydrants would be installed that would be accessible from the public right of way.  The new upsized watermains would also improve flow capacity of the existing intertie with Incline Village GID which is limited to 200 gpm. Flow and pressure to customers would be improved for those served by the 2-inch backyard mains.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; North Tahoe Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: Trout Street Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Main water system in Kings Beach, CA was comprised of watermains ranging from 1- to 8- inches in diameter. The system was deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and did not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid.  The project installed 2,568 linear feet of new 8-inch watermain and 5 new fire hydrants on Trout and Brook Ave. to replace the existing 1- and 2-inch diameter steel watermain that serves the properties. Project improved water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage.
properties.FundingSources: North Tahoe Public Utility District; U.S. Environmental Protection Agency

properties.ProjectName: Post-Caldor Fire Stream Aggradation using Beaver Dam Analogues: Saxon and Trout Creeks
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The watersheds within and downstream of the Caldor Fire Scar presented an opportunity to use the expected erosion from the landscape to promote channel aggradation within incised areas of the creeks. 80 BDAs were installed along Saxon and Trout Creeks, concentrated in areas that benefited from channel aggradation and riparian width expansion potential. Monitoring has shown a more dynamic channel morphology, increased aquatic species habitat complexity, channel aggradation, increased inset floodplains and improved floodplain connectivity. BDA projects can extend restoration efforts into remote areas where conventional projects would be cost prohibitive.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Community Watershed Planning Forest Health Implementation- North Shore
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: Work with private parcel owners to secure access to property and perform fuels management, stream restoration (handwork using downed timber or willow debris) and terrestrial invasive weed identification and removal. Funding will be pursued and project details developed.

properties.ProjectName: LTBMU Caldor Hazard Tree and Fuel Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Hazard tree removal and fuel reduction on approximately 1500 acres related to the Caldor Fire along roads, trails, adjacent to private property, and in developed sites.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: LTBMU Caldor Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Long term restoration of the Caldor Fire area within the Lake Tahoe Basin, including removal of fire-killed trees, fuels reduction, reforestation, trail restoration, and terrestrial and aquatic habitat restoration.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Crystal Peak Road - Watermain Replacement for Fire Protection
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: Replacement of 2300 linear feet of 6-inch water main with new 8-inch water main and increase quantities of fire hydrants to meet 2018 IFC code requirements. This project is a continuation of the multi-year program to replace 1960's era thin wall steel water mains and other deficient water mains. We also work closely with the North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District to determine areas of low fire flow, which may indicate a need for increased capacity in that area. Project improves water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage area.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: STPUD Wastewater Treatment Plant Fuels Reduction project
properties.ProjectDescription: South Tahoe Public Utility District treated 100 acres adjacent to the wastewater treatment facility with fuels reduction efforts.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Ralph Tank BMP and SEZ Restoration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: Removal of water tank, associated structures and other coverage to access the facility located in SEZ near Bijou Creek. SEZ vegetation has been restored.    Parking barriers installed and water spreading BMPs in place on 2 parcels to permit foot access to remaining monitoring well facility.  4,428 sf total coverage removed & banked on APNs  025-551-006 & -007 as part of project.

properties.ProjectName: Bowers/Bijou Area Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: STPUD deficiencies in fire flows and the number and spacing of fire hydrants did not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid. The Bowers/Bijou Area is located within the South Tahoe Public Utility District service area. The properties on the street are served by undersized water mains (2 to 4 inches in diameter) and cannot support fire hydrants adequately for required fire suppression. Additionally, the number and spacing of fire hydrants do not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid. These residential properties also have daily flow and pressure deficiencies. The project installed 10,400 feet of 8-inch water mains, improved system looping and added 15 new hydr
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Black Bart Area Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Black Bart Project installed 7,700 linear feet of new 6-inch water main to replace the existing 1- and 2-inch diameter steel water main that serves the properties. Nine new fire hydrants would be installed that would be accessible from the public right of way.
The project improves water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage area.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: STPUD Fire Hydrant Upgrades and Improvements Fire Protection Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: STPUD updated, replaced, and/or installed 57 fire hydrants throughout its service area to reduce the current deficiencies in fire flow and available fire protection. The project will improve water supply by enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage areas.
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund; El Dorado County Water Agency; South Tahoe Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: Slott Peak Waterline  Improvements
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: Replacement of 330 linear feet of 6-inch water main with new 8-inch water main and replacement of one fire hydrant to meet NLTFPD code requirements. This project is a continuation of the multi-year program to replace 1960's era thin wall steel water mains and other deficient water mains. Replacement criteria is twofold: Replace those water mains with the most leaks and in streets with aging pavement. Since our water loss is now less than 6%, our main objective is to work closely with the Washoe County Road Department to replace water mains just prior to the County's repaving the street. Project  enhances fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District

properties.ProjectName: Pioneer Trail/US Highway 50 Intersection Safety Improvement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This project aims to improve the intersection of US Highway 50/ State Route 89 and Pioneer Trail in the community of Meyers by replacing the existing signalized intersection with a modern roundabout. Once constructed features will include improving mobility, walkability, and sustainability of the intersection. Enhanced multimodal transportation improvements like visible crosswalks for bicycle and pedestrian movements, providing for future growth for transit facilities to enhance circulation and provide opportunities to experience Meyers as an active transportation user.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Soil Conservation, Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
