properties.FundingSources: AQ Mitigation Funds; Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Program (CMAQ); Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP); Local Partnership Program; Regional Surface Transportation Program Funds (RSTP); Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) - California

properties.ProjectName: Burnt Cedar Beach - Lakeshore Blvd Stormwater BMPs
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription:
IVGID’s Burnt Cedar property currently receives storm water that enters the property during precipitation and snowmelt events. This water enters the property through an 18-inch CMP culvert and comes exclusively from the Washoe County roadway swales. 
Currently, the only BMP is the grass area adjacent to the culvert. There are no permanent BMP’s to slow the stormwater and stop sediment from entering the lake. This also results in beach sections being washed out as the water flows down the property. IVGID proposes a permanent BMP system in which this storm water is controlled and will slow the rate of water allowing the sediment to drop out of the water prior to it entering the lake.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District

properties.ProjectName: Marlette Virtual Nature Trail
properties.ProjectDescription: The Marlette Virtual Nature Trail follows 12 miles of existing trails from Spooner Lake to Tunnel Creek. The trail starts with a sign in the Spooner Lake parking area with instructions on how to access the trail information. A second sign is placed at the Tunnel Creek trailhead. The trail is hosted on the Google Earth platform, which offers Android and iPhone apps, as well as web-based maps. The trail follows the existing North Canyon, Marlette Flume, and Tunnel Creek trails. The trail has 20 points of interest highlighting plants, animals, geology, and human history such as Washoe culture and Comstock logging and mining.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe License Plate Program

properties.ProjectName: Quantifying the status, trends, and demography of Tahoe draba (Draba asterophora), a Lake Tahoe Basin rare alpine plant
properties.ProjectDescription: The alpine plant, Tahoe draba (Draba asterophora), is among the endemic plant species that occurs only in the Lake Tahoe region. We assess the status, long-term trends, and demographic vulnerabilities of Tahoe draba in the northern and southern Lake Tahoe Basin (LTB). To accomplish this, we: 1) Collate and digitize historic monitoring data of Tahoe draba populations; 2) Reestablish density and demographic monitoring transects of Tahoe draba in both its northern and southern LTB populations and monitor plants for 3 years; 3) Analyze current and historic data to quantify demographic rates, current status, and long-term trends of Tahoe draba in northern and southern populations.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe License Plate Program

properties.ProjectName: Golden and Rainbow Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Main water system in Kings Beach, CA is deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and does not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid. This project installed 7,700 linear feet of new 8-inch watermain in Golden Ave., Rainbow Ave., and upper Secline Street to replace the existing 1- and 2-inch diameter steel watermain that served the properties. Twelve new fire hydrants have been installed that are accessible from the public right of way. The project improved water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; North Tahoe Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: Brook, Salmon, Yacht, and Dip Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: North Tahoe Public Utility District owns the Tahoe Main water system that serves the Kings Beach residential grid neighborhood. The water system is comprised of watermains ranging from 1- to 8- inches in diameter. The system is deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and does not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid. The project would install 2,650 linear feet of new 8-inch watermain on Brook, Salmon, Yacht, and Dip streets to replace the existing 1- and 2-inch diameter steel watermain that serves the properties. Five (5) new fire hydrants would be installed that would be accessible from the public right of way.

properties.ProjectName: Y-Mobility Hub
properties.ProjectDescription: The Y-Mobility Hub would provide multi-modal access to popular destinations within the City and Lake Tahoe beaches along the State Route 89 corridor north of the Y to facilitate other modes of transportation. The Mobility Hub would include a Park-n-Ride and facilities for fixed-route transit, micro transit and regional shuttle options to decrease dependency on private vehicles. The SR 89 corridor has multiple destinations and high visitation rates during peak season result in congestion and parking issues. East of Y on Highway 50 there is a need to connect people with residential and commercial areas along the Highway 50 corridor and the Stateline/Heavenly Village Tourist Core Area.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Transportation and Sustainable Communities

properties.ProjectName: South Shore Microtransit Electrification
properties.ProjectDescription: The City of South Lake Tahoe has partnered with the South Shore Transit Management Association to help facilitate the transition of the Lake Link microtransit fleet to electric. Dedicated overnight parking and Level 2 and Level 3 chargers are necessary to ensure success. The City has an aspirational goal to achieve 24/7 carbon free energy by 2030 and seeks to support Level 2 charging with with stored solar energy for overnight charging at a "Microtransit EV Charging Base Station".  The Level 3 charging will be for on-route charging as needed. The project takes an innovative technology approach to tracking carbon intensity of the fleet, a step toward 24/7 hourly certification.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund; SB 125; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Lake Link South Shore Microtransit
properties.ProjectDescription: Microtransit service started on the South Shore July 2022 and expanded in January 2024. The South Shore Transit Management Association contracts with Downtowner to provide the Lake Link service, with free rides between any location in the service area. The expanded service area extends from Round Hill in Douglas county, NV to the Sierra Tract neighborhood the City of South Lake Tahoe, CA. The first year was a success, averaging over 10,000 riders per month. In the first month of expanded service, ridership increased 84% compared to 2023 with over 24,000 riders. Microtransit reduces traffic congestion, improves quality of life for locals and the visitor experience, and reduces GHG emissions.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: ADVANCE; Barton Foundation; City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund; Douglas County; Edgewood Companies; El Dorado County General Fund; Heavenly Ski Resort; Lake Tahoe Community College; Lake Tahoe Visitors Authority; League to Save Lake Tahoe; Private (Business); Ski Run Marina; South Lake Tahoe Tourism Improvement District; South Shore Transportation Management Association; South Tahoe Alliance of Resorts; Tahoe Blue Event Center; Tahoe Douglas Visitors Authority; Tahoe Regional Planning Agency

properties.ProjectName: Spooner Meadow Restoration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Spooner Meadow is an important ecosystem along Tahoe’s east shore. It provides cover, perennial water, and food resources for over one hundred species of wildlife. Historical water channelization, grazing, logging, and a lack of natural fire events have reduced its capacity to function as a normal, healthy meadow ecosystem. Climate change threatens to eliminate Tahoe’s meadows via reduced snowpacks, declining groundwater, and warmer temperatures. Restoration of Spooner Meadow would maintain its role as a vital wildlife nesting and migration corridor. Restoration will involve Nevada Division of State Parks in order to balance natural resource objectives with recreational opportunities.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Lands
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe License Plate Program

properties.ProjectName: Lake Forest Boat Ramp Restroom Replacement Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The project replaced an existing seasonal restroom with the construction of a year-round, ADA compliant facility to enhance the enjoyment of the Lake Forest Boat Ramp property. The new restroom is a pre-fabricated building with upgraded materials and construction, including indoor plumbing and hydronic floor heating, single occupancy use, vandal resistant locking mechanisms, and refillable water stations.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Proposition 68; Tahoe City Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: SR 28 Spooner Mobility Hub and AIS Inspection Station
properties.ProjectDescription: The project includes design and construction of a transit mobility hub with 250 parking spaces and restrooms, an AIS inspection station, 0.5 miles of multi-use path and a pedestrian crossing from Spooner State Park to the junction of SR28 and US50 adjacent to transit mobility hub.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

properties.ProjectName: Preston Field Water Quality Improvement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This is a water quality improvement project located in Incline Village. The area is highly connected to Lake Tahoe and is a priority treatment area due to a relatively large baseline FSP load. The project proposes to install stormwater treatment BMPs and shoulder stabilization within the existing Washoe County right-of-way and undeveloped public parcels, providing treatment for urban stormwater runoff to meet the Lake Tahoe TMDL. This project is on the 5-year list. Once funding is secured, Washoe County intends to hire a consultant and begin planning and design of this project https://eip.laketahoeinfo.org/EIPActionPriority/Detail/1in 2024.

properties.ProjectName: Burnt Cedar/Lakeshore Blvd Water Quality Improvement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This is a water quality improvement project located in Incline Village. The area is highly connected to Lake Tahoe and is a priority treatment area due to a relatively large baseline FSP load. The project proposes to install stormwater treatment BMPs and shoulder stabilization within the existing Washoe County right-of-way and outfall conveyance that safely conveys overflow to Lake Tahoe, providing treatment for urban stormwater runoff to meet the Lake Tahoe TMDL. This project is on the 5-year list. On behalf of Washoe County and IVGID, NTCD is seeking funding to plan, permit, design and implement the project in the summer 2026.

properties.ProjectName: Second Creek (B02) Water Quality Improvement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: This is a water quality improvement project located in Incline Village. The area is highly connected to Lake Tahoe and is a priority treatment area due to a relatively large baseline FSP load. The project proposes to install stormwater treatment BMPs and shoulder stabilization within the existing Washoe County right-of-way and undeveloped public parcels, providing treatment for urban stormwater runoff to meet the Lake Tahoe TMDL. properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels

The area is highly connected to Lake Tahoe and is a priority treatment area due to a relatively large baseline FSP load. The project proposes to install stormwater treatment BMPs and shoulder stabilization within the existing Washoe County right-of-way and undeveloped public parcels, providing treatment for urban stormwater runoff to meet the Lake Tahoe TMDL. properties.ProjectName: NTFPD Carnelian Canyon Project
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project reduced hazardous fuels using hand-thinning and pile-burning on 78 acres of private and local government-owned land.  The treatment increased conifer spacing, along with the mean diameter of leave trees.  This equates to a substantial reduction in the threat of catastrophic wildfire and drastic improvements in forest health.  All areas treated were within the defense zone of the wildland-urban interface, and adjacent to the community of Carnelian Bay, CA. It is among highest priorities identified in the Lake Tahoe Basin Community
Wildfire Protection Plan and is endorsed by the Tahoe Fire and Fuels Team.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Van Sickle Hazardous Fuels Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: Van Sickle Bi-State Park is a unit of Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park. Development of the park (on the NV side) is in the planning phases and will include a new visitors center, staff housing, offices, and a new trail. Project activities will begin in 2023 and focus on reducing hazardous fuels around the proposed new park infrastructure and also focus on removing trees for construction activities. A combination of hand thinning, chipping, pile building, and pile burning are proposed.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Taylor Tallac Restoration Project – Sewer line relocation
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The proposed project relocates 2200 LF of gravity sewer main from the current location along the Edge of Lake Tahoe to follow the edge of an existing roadway.  The relocation reduces the risk of sewer discharge directly to Lake Tahoe by moving manholes currently located on the shore of Lake Tahoe (within a yellow cress protection area) and within tributaries away from these sensitive areas. Facilitates Taylor-Tallac Restoration by USFS.
properties.FundingSources: South Tahoe Public Utility District; U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Quail Lake Dam Feasibility Analysis and Watershed Assessment
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: A feasibility study of the Quail Lake Creek watershed and Quail Lake dam, identify causes of concern and develop a list of prioritized projects to improve the function of uplands and riparian and aquatic/wetland ecosystems, evaluate storage capacity to meet the current and future water supply needs for aquatic, wildlife habitat, identify water resources concerns and opportunities, develop recommendations for dam retrofit, and future action with climate change. The study of each alternative to be assessed with respect to the dam infrastructure, floodplain/wetland, sediment, ecological habitat, hydrology and hydraulics, water quality/quantity, flow regimes, recreation, social impact.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.LeadImplementer: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: 2023 STPUD Pioneer Trail Fire Suppression Infrastructure
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription: This project installs approximately 11,300 linear feet of new 12 and 16” water mains and 10 fire hydrants on Pioneer Trail from Marshall Trail to Susquehana. This is a sparsely populated road but a main evacuation route and fire break for the community of South Lake Tahoe. There is currently not water service along this route. The project will install fire hydrants at less than 1000 ft spacing in accordance with the Fire Code for undeveloped areas and will provide fire flow in excess of 3000 gpm.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; South Tahoe Public Utility District; U.S. Environmental Protection Agency

properties.ProjectName: 2023 STPUD Bijou 1 Waterline and Fire Hydrants
properties.EIPActionPriority: Upgrade Priority Water Infrastructure to Fight Catastrophic Wildfire
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project replaces approximately 15,900 linear feet of waterlines, and install fire hydrants, water main interties, and appurtenances, in two phases. The Herbert-Walkup Waterline Replacement (Phase 1) includes the replacement of approximately 9,400 linear feet of waterline, along with the
installation of 16 fire hydrants and 9 water main interties. The Bijou #1 Waterline Replacement (Phase 2) includes replacement of approximately 6,500 linear feet of waterline, along with the installation of 12 fire hydrants and 7 water main interties.
properties.FundingSources: South Tahoe Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: HWY 50 Fuel Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat between 90 to 115 acres of forestland within the Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) along the US Highway 50 corridor between Glenbrook and Zephyr Cove, NV. This treatment will help to modify potential fire behavior such that firefighters will be able to safely protect life, property, and the environment from an approaching wildland fire. This project will also drastically increase the sustainability of the ecosystems by returning the environment back to a more “natural” landscape in terms of vegetation/tree density and species composition. Treatment will include thinning and removal of fuels within the project areas.
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Cattlemans/Black Bart Retrofit Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The Cattlemans and Black Bart Basins were constructed as part of the Pioneer Trail III Erosion Control Project in 2001.  The improvements included corrugated steel pipe outlet structures with atrium racks near the edge of the basin side slopes.  Since construction the basins have become wet basins with the outlet structures now under water most of the year.  The 2025 project focused on retrofit of the outlet pipes so as discharge runoff above the existing basin surface water elevations allowing for proper inspections and maintenance related to runoff and sediment transport.
properties.FundingSources: TRPA Operations & Maintenance Funds

properties.ProjectName: Lahontan Cutthroat Trout fish planting in Echo Lake and Sawmill Pond
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore and Protect Native Fish and Wildlife
properties.ProjectDescription: Annual fish planting in Echo lake and Sawmill Pond. Organization of a family fishing event at Sawmill pond each summer.
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Fragment Containment
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription:
Containment of aquatic invasive plant fragments in the Tahoe Keys is a high priority for AIS Program partners as the Tahoe Keys are the main source of AIP to the rest of the lake. Partners are coming together to implement and guide innovative and diverse containment practices, described in the Containment Plan (see link). The collaborative includes the Tahoe Keys Marina, the Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association, Keep Tahoe Blue, TRPA, Tahoe RCD, EcoClean Solutions, Marine Taxonomic Services, Inventive Resources Inc, US Forest Service, and Lahontan. 
Efforts will be monitored and reported each season while a holistic long-term plan for control of the Tahoe Keys is developed.
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Keys Marina (Suntex)

properties.ProjectName: Edgewood Creek Restoration & Forest Health Project within TRPA/NDOT parcels
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This project along Kingsbury Grade/SR207 within Douglas County proposes to perform fuels reduction and restore a portion of Edgewood Creek to improve stream function and water quality, along with improving the stormwater treatment directly connected to Edgewood creek via the TRPA treatment BMPs. Specifically (1) Capture and treat TRPA stormwater runoff prior to entering Edgewood Creek by improving treatment BMPs. (2) Remove unnecessary fill and restore the channel of Edgewood Creek. (3) Perform fuels reduction throughout the entire project area, but specifically within the SEZ. (4) Prevent, control, or eradicate terrestrial invasive species.

properties.ProjectName: Lake Tahoe East Shore Asian Clam and Metaphyton Delineation and Control
properties.ProjectDescription: The expanse of non-native Asian clam populations with the concurrent appearance of metaphyton (unattached algae) along Lake Tahoe’s east shore beaches has become an increasing concern. Due to the high nutrient concentrations from clam excretions and their stimulatory effect on algal growth, nuisance algae is starting to accumulate underwater and on beaches having negative aesthetic impacts. Five beaches were surveyed in summer 2023, using SCUBA and UAV imagery, to delineate the extent and density of Asian clams and any associated metaphyton growth. A metaphyton removal pilot study to determine the effectiveness of removing metaphyton algae before contaminating beaches was conducted.
properties.LeadImplementer: UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center
properties.FundingSources: UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center

properties.ProjectName: Skyland Shaded Fuel Break
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat approximately 17 acres of US Forest Service lands to the South and East of the Skyland community.  Treatment will consist of hand treatment and forest fuels mastication to create a “Shaded Fuel Break” as defined by the National Wildfire Coordinating Group; Fuel breaks built in timbered areas where the trees on the break are thinned and pruned to reduce the fire potential yet retain enough crown canopy to make a less favorable microclimate for surface fires.
properties.FundingSources: U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Spooner Lake and Backcountry State Park Trail Plan
properties.ProjectDescription: This project will update the  parks' master plan for the park.  The primary goal of this project is to move non-motorized users off the parks service roads and improve connectivity to the backcountry trail system.  A planning firm will be utilized to complete a resource assessment of the project area.   The resource assessment will identify wildlife, water quality, forest health, and historical resource concerns. The team will utilize the resource assessment to identify possible trail corridors for trail construction or improvements.  New trail corridors that meet the project goal will then receive further environmental review and trail construction documents will be produced.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Recreational Trails Grant; Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: North Canyon Road Shaded Fuel Break
properties.ProjectDescription: Beginning at the start of North Canyon Road in Spooner State Park, Nevada Division of Forestry crews will hand thin and create burn piles 100 feet off both sides of the road up to Marlette Lake. The goal is to create a shaded fuel break to strengthen the use of North Canyon Road as a Potential Operational Delineation for future wildfire firefighting efforts. Crews will cut and construct piles during the summer and fall months of 2023 and 2024 and burn the piles in the winters of 2025/2026 and 2026/2027.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: NV Community Watershed Planning Forest Health Implementation- South Shore
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: Work with a public parcel owner to secure access to property and perform fuels management, stream restoration (handwork using downed timber or willow debris) and terrestrial invasive weed identification and removal. Funding will be pursued and project details developed.

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Lagoons Long Term Water Quality Improvement Project Planning
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys POA is planning, addressing technical issues, and engaging stakeholders to identify actions to improve the long-term quality and beneficial uses of waters of the Tahoe Keys Lagoons (i.e., the Marina, West, and Lake Tallac lagoons).   Existing condition evaluations are focusing on non-point sources of nutrients.  Future evaluations will include:  1) nutrient inputs from upgradient shallow groundwater and surface sources internal to the lagoons, 2) methods to improve the lagoons circulation and reduce algae/HABs, 3) Lake Tallac Lagoon outflow effects on Pope Marsh, 4) lagoons organic sediment nutrient contributions to water quality, and 5) possible mitigations for climate change
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association

properties.ProjectName: East Shore Trail Bark Beetle Outbreak
properties.ProjectDescription: Hand thinned and chipped bark beetle killed trees along the East Shore trail in Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park. Chipping of bark beetle infested trees reduces the bark beetle populations and offers protection to the remaining trees. Felling of dead trees along the East Shore Trail eliminates hazards to the public. Several logs from the project were placed as log erosion barriers, for restoration of eroded slopes due to off-trail lake access.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Vista Recreation Area Peninsula Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription: This project consisted of the installation of pervious pavers, rock slope protection, stone seats, metal guardrail modifications, concrete curbs, concrete stairs, utility trench, and other related work necessary to complete the Tahoe Vista Recreation Area Peninsula Improvements.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; North Tahoe Public Utility District; Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax

properties.ProjectName: Meeks Creek Bridge - SHOPP Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Near Meeks Bay, at Meeks Creek Bridge No. 25-0019. Replace Meeks Creek Bridge, restore creek to address bridge scour and fish passage barriers, add wildlife terrestrial crossing improvement under bridge, and add bicycle and pedestrian improvements. EA: 4J090
properties.FundingSources: SHOPP Funds

properties.ProjectName: Elks Club Water Quality and Accessibility Improvements
properties.ProjectDescription: The Elks Club site is important for residents and visitors to access the Upper Truckee River and broader trail network. The Conservancy improved the parking lot and ensured accessible connections to trails leading to the river and other public lands. The Conservancy achieved multiple benefits through the project by reconstructing the parking lot; installing Best Management Practices to capture storm water runoff to protect water quality; and providing accessible parking spaces, including compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. The Conservancy planned the project with El Dorado County's Environmental Improvement Program Country Club Heights Erosion Control Project #01.01.01.0067.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; Climate Resilience

properties.ProjectName: Washoe Meadows Quarry Site Enhancement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: California Department of Parks and Recreation is in the initial stage of designing a wetland enhancement project in the old quarry pit and pile near Dry Meadow in Washoe Meadows State Park. The site currently holds water until early summer and has established wetland vegetation - design goals would include expanding wetland habitat by lowering surface elevation, removing discarded quarry debris, maximizing wildlife habitat components, and extending surface water longer into the summer months.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation
properties.LeadImplementer: California Department of Parks and Recreation
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Parks and Recreation

properties.ProjectName: Picnic Area and Lake Access Improvements at Patton Landing Beach
properties.ProjectDescription: The Conservancy will construct improvements at Patton Landing Beach to improve picnic areas, paths of travel, and lake access so that all people can better utilize the facility and the lake access it provides. Improvements include resurfacing walkways, providing accessible paths to the lake shore, installing accessible picnic areas and tables, and improving restroom facilities.
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Fish and Wildlife; California Tahoe Conservancy; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Picnic and Lake Access Improvements at North Tahoe Beach
properties.ProjectDescription: The Conservancy will construct improvements at North Tahoe Beach to improve picnic areas, paths of travel, restrooms, and lake access so that all people can better utilize the facility and the lake access it provides. Improvements include resurfacing walkways, providing accessible paths to the lake shore, installing accessible picnic areas and tables, and improving restroom facilities.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; North Tahoe Community Alliance

properties.ProjectName: Emerald Bay Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: Emerald Bay is one of the most successful aquatic invasive plant (AIP) control treatments completed to date by the Lake Tahoe AIS program. Zero to few aquatic invasive plants had been detected since 2014, until recent surveillance monitoring in 2022 revealed AIP that required a higher level of work that was no longer considered a rapid response action. Dedicated treatment includes diver-assisted suction removal and hand-pulling. To ensure the long-term effectiveness of this work, routine surveillance monitoring is occuring, and training of California Department of State Parks divers to conduct annual monitoring and removal of any emerging aquatic invasive plants.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Sand Harbor State Park Master Plan Update
properties.ProjectDescription: The current Sand Harbor layout was designed in 1970 and improperly designed for the current visitation.  This project updates the 1990 master plan for the park and create a sustainable vision for the future of Sand Harbor.  The master plan will then be implemented in a series of EIP projects to improve traffic flow, recreation experience, and sustainability of the site.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Pilot project: Sonar Methods for Aquatic Plant Monitoring
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: Pilot project to better understand capabilities of sonar to enhance monitoring of aquatic invasive plant infestations. Methods include multibeam, side scan, dual frequency sonar, and comparison of commercially available sonar software.
properties.FundingSources: California Lahontan Regional Water Quality Control Board; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Lake Valley Fire Protection District Capacity Planning Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The LVFPD will be responsible for planning and preparing for the implementation of high priority fuels reduction and wildfire prevention projects on state, local government, and private lands in the South Shore area of the Lake Tahoe Basin (Basin). This work will be done in coordination with the Conservancy, the Tahoe Fire and Fuels Team (TFFT), the Tahoe Resource Conservation District, and other Basin partners. Once implemented, the fuels reduction and wildfire prevention projects will help to restore the resilience of Basin forests and watersheds, foster Basin-wide climate change adaption, reduce fire risk for communities, and increase the capacity for planning and implementing projects.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Logan Shoals Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: Aquatic invasive plant removal implemented at Logan Shoals is prioritized in the Action Agenda, a multi-year lake-wide strategy to remove aquatic invasive plants along the shoreline of Lake Tahoe. Methods of removal included barrier installation, diver-assisted suction (if needed), and hand removal. Barriers were installed at this site in 2023 and removed in 2024. Divers continued surveillance monitoring at this site throughout the 2024 and 2025 plant growing seasons. Future reporting for this project will be documented in Project # 01.03.01.0037 Lake-wide Surveillance and Site Assessments.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe License Plate Program; Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Wovoka Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: In October 2022 during a surveillance monitoring survey, a dense Eurasian watermilfoil infestation was observed by divers. In 2023, Tahoe RCD's contracted dive team installed barriers in June to control Eurasian watermilfoil. Barriers were removed in November 2023, and follow-up surveys and  plant removal continued in 2024. Due to successful diver removal efforts and minimal detection of newly rooted Eurasian watermilfoil during surveillance visits in 2024, this project has reached post-implementation surveillance status. All future surveillance visits will be documented in Project # 01.03.01.0037 Lake-wide Surveillance and Site Assessments.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Lagoons (Entirety) Aquatic Invasive Weed Control Planning
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys is the highest priority location of invasive aquatic weed control. With the completion of the Tahoe Keys Control Methods Test, data collected will inform a holistic treatment regime for the entirety of the Tahoe Keys. Maximizing fragment containment and interim treatments will take place in 2025, as well as stakeholder engagement. Planning and environmental review will be the next step planning to solve this complicated infestation.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Terrace View Sewer Line Burke Headwaters Restoration
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: Between Terrace View and N. Benjamin Road, there is an export sewer line under a branch of Burke Creek that will be relocated out of the stream zone as part of its life span replacement. This project proposes to restore the SEZ that has been impaired by the dirt sewer line access road and trails.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality

properties.ProjectName: Burke Creek Rabe Meadow Upper Meadows Restoration and Pump Station Road Realignment
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: This project achieves items that were not covered in the Burke Creek Rabe Meadow Riparian Restoration and includes trail realignments out of riparian areas, filling of ditches that drain meadows, removal of conifers that encroach on meadows, and the construction of a new access in higher capability land for the existing sewer pump station on NV Beach.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Rabe Meadow Drought and Climate Resilience Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: There are 2 ephemeral drainages that flow into the existing Douglas County Lake Tahoe Sewer Authority (DCLTSA) emergency overflow pond. Per their NDEP permit, this clean water is pumped out to be treated at the sewer plant and then exported over the hill. These natural drainages should be flowing into Rabe Meadow as spring runoff and will help with water quantity in drought years. This project establish flow paths and SEZ areas around the existing DCLTSA emergency overflow pond and this water will eventually reach Rabe Meadow.

properties.ProjectName: TCPUD Multi-Use Trail System Reconstruction and Safety Enhancement Project
properties.ProjectDescription:
Trail reconstruction and safety improvements for 13.1 miles of multi-use trail. The project will be completed in seven phases.

2024 - North Shore Trail
2025 - West Shore Trail Segments 2 & 3 (Sunnyside to Idlewild Way)
2026 - West Shore Trail Segment 1 (64 Acres to Sunnyside)
2028 - West Shore Trail Segment 4
2030 - West Shore Trail Segment 5
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax; Tahoe City Public Utility District; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: Echo Lake 2023- Pilot Underwater SCUBA Litter Clean Up
properties.ProjectDescription: In the Echo Lake Pilot Research project, the team conduct a comprehensive assessment of the factors threatening Echo Lake’s health as well as remove litter. The findings of this project suggest that for Echo Lake, there is a low urgency for a full circumnavigated cleanup which are typically recommended for lakes that rank medium to high urgency as they allow our teams to address the heavily littered lake beds. Our organization was encouraged by the result of the pilot research that indicated lower levels of litter accumulation in Echo Lake.
properties.FundingSources: Private (Business)

properties.ProjectName: Airport Fuel Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: Fuels reduction pile burning to reduce fuel loading around airport property
properties.FundingSources: City of South Lake Tahoe General Fund

properties.ProjectName: Spooner Lake Phase 3
properties.ProjectDescription: The Spooner Lake Front Country Phase III project includes a new lake viewing platform and a non-motorized boat launch to provide high quality visitor services at Spooner Lake in Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park.  The Non-Motorized Boat Launch will be a concrete ramp that begins above the high-water mark and curves into the lake following the natural contour of the lake bottom. The Lake Viewing Platform is an elevated walkway leading to a square or rectangular platform with benches, supported by piers.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Private (Business); Tahoe Bonds Act; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: South Tahoe Refuse Wood Energy
properties.ProjectDescription: South Tahoe Refuse & Recycling (STR) is exploring the installation of a 125-250kW wood waste gasifier at its South Lake Tahoe facility. Gasification has been around since the early 1800’s – instead of burning, chemical reactions turn the green waste into a gas that is a cleaner substitute for fossil fuels. If installed, the net metering system would offset the majority of grid electricity and natural gas used at the STR site by using 10-15% of the wood waste currently collected by STR, and reduce traffic and emissions from transporting waste material out of the Basin by over 70 truckloads each year.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Vegetation Preservation, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: Wood Innovations Grant Program

properties.ProjectName: Washoe Meadows State Park and Lake Valley State Recreation Area WUI Hazardous Fuels Reduction - Planning
properties.ProjectDescription: Washoe Meadows State Park and Lake Valley State Recreation Area WUI Hazardous Fuels Reduction - Planning Project will address the long term program of forest management and fuel reduction on state lands in South Lake Tahoe. The primary objective of the project is to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires that could damage Lake Tahoe Basin forests, watersheds, habitats, and communities and increase the pace and scale of fuel reduction in the park and recreation area. Once completed, state implementers can efficiently and comprehensively evaluate the effects of forest management, and improve the project approval and delivery process for subsequent activities.
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Secline Beach Enhancement Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The NTPUD, CTC, and Placer County are working together to improve Secline Beach in Kings Beach, California. Phase I includes community outreach, a needs assessment, and the development of conceptual improvement plans. Possible improvements to Secline Beach area include the construction of new public restrooms, formal picnic areas, organized kayak and paddleboard storage, e-bike and electric vehicle charging stations, and coordinated public transportation for beach visitors.  Additional public access enhancements could also include walkable connections to the nearby North Tahoe Beach and Kings Beach State Recreation Area, as outlined in the current Tahoe Basin Area Plan.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy; North Tahoe Community Alliance; North Tahoe Public Utility District

properties.ProjectName: Truckee-Tahoe Regional BurnBot Pilot
properties.ProjectDescription:
A broad coalition of stakeholders, including the Tahoe Fund, North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District, Tahoe Fire & Fuels Team, Martis Fund, and the Tahoe Truckee Community Foundation, are bringing BurnBot to Tahoe to pilot and showcase its potential to help increase the pace and scale of forest health treatments safely and effectively. 

We hope this two-part pilot will lead to the incorporation of BurnBot into our regional forest health and wildfire prevention strategy. BurnBot provides remote-operated, tech-driven systems for both mastication and prescribed burns that make each process faster, safer and easier to carry out.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District

properties.ProjectName: SR 267 Roadway Rehabilitation
properties.ProjectDescription:
Near Truckee, from Nevada County line to Dolly Varden Avenue.  Rehabilitate pavement and drainage systems, upgrade guardrail and facilities to Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards, and extend southbound truck climbing lane. (PM 0.0 to PM 9.63)  EA 2J190

The Tahoe basin portion of the project will install bike route signage and striping from Carnelian Bay Ave to PM 9.63.
properties.FundingSources: SHOPP Funds

properties.ProjectName: Dennis T. Machida Memorial Greenway (Phase 3)
properties.ProjectDescription: The Dennis T. Machida Memorial Greenway Phase 3 project would extend this Class 1 shared-use trail from Ski Run Boulevard to Van Sickle Bi-State Park.
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: SLT Bikeway Realignment and Restoration at Link Road
properties.ProjectDescription: Relocate a section of the South Lake Tahoe Bikeway out of the Upper Truckee Marsh and into the adjacent uplands in the vicinity of Link Road and create a direct connection to Sussex Avenue. This project will allow for significant SEZ and Wetland restoration and formalize a heavily trafficked native surface route that is much more direct. The existing alignment was intended to be temporary until acquisitions were completed.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Scenic Resources, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife

properties.ProjectName: SR 28 South Corridor Secret Harbor to Spooner
properties.ProjectDescription: Five miles of East Shore Trail and 40 parking spaces at Skunk Harbor.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Transportation and Sustainable Communities

properties.ProjectName: Kingsbury Shaded Fuel Break
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat approximately 16 acres of US Forest Service lands of the Upper Kingsbury Area to the East of Andria Street . Treatment will consist of hand treatment, prescribed burning, and forest fuels mastication to create a “Shaded Fuel Break” as defined by the National Wildfire Coordinating Group; Fuel breaks built in timbered areas where the trees and brush on the break are thinned and pruned to reduce the fire potential yet retain enough crown canopy to make a less favorable microclimate for surface fires.

Reporting for this project is under 02.01.01.0097 - Urban Forest Defense Zone Fuels Reduction and Healthy Forest Project
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Lower Kingsbury Shaded Fuel Break
properties.ProjectDescription:
The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat approximately 12 acres of US Forest Service lands to the North of the Lower Kingsbury community. Treatment will consist of hand treatment, prescribed burning, and forest fuels mastication to create a “Shaded Fuel Break” as defined by the National Wildfire Coordinating Group; Fuel breaks built in timbered areas where the trees on the break are thinned and pruned to reduce the fire potential yet retain enough crown canopy to make a less favorable microclimate for surface fires.
Project Accomplishments are reported in LTBMU project 02.01.01.0097 - Urban Forest Defense Zone Fuels Reduction and Healthy Forest Project
properties.FundingSources: Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act

properties.ProjectName: Homewood Forest Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The project includes forest fuels removal over 252 acres to improve forest stand conditions and overall forest health. The selection tree removal will target the removal of suppressed, dead, dying, and non-resilient stands of timber for forest health and risk reduction of catastrophic wildfire. The objective of the timber harvesting is to improve the remnant stands of forest and timber to a healthy and desirable physiological condition promoting forest resilience and the desired phenology throughout the area and to bolster public safety from severe wildfire.
properties.FundingSources: Private (Business)

properties.ProjectName: Mutushahoo Watah: Trout Creek Meadow Restoration
properties.ProjectDescription: The Lake Tahoe Community College is interested in reducing the risk of catastrophic wildfire, improving hydrologic function, and restoring lost habitat in the Trout Creek Meadow between Hwy 50 and Martin Ave. Ecosystem restoration will include the removal of ~20 acres of lodgepole pine that have encroached upon the meadow surface and the use of traditional ecologic knowledge and cultural burning practices. This project is part a larger effort to reconnect Indigenous Communities with the landscape and increase the diversity of native plants, habitat, & culturally significant species.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Wildlife
properties.FundingSources: California Tahoe Conservancy

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Truckee Airport District/ North Tahoe Fire-  River Road Project 1
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Truckee Airport District - North Tahoe Fire (TTAD/NTF) River Road Fuels Reduction Project 1 is located on the south side of the Highway 89 corridor where it parallels the Truckee River between Tahoe City and Alpine Meadows, CA. This portion of Highway 89 is a primary evacuation route for Lake Tahoe residents and visitors and it is within the Defense Zone of the Wildland Urban Interface. The project addresses dead and dying trees, ladder fuels, and excessive ground fuels and will be part of a series of projects to reduce hazardous fuels and improve forest health, allowing for the highway corridor to better serve for evacuation among multiple benefits.
properties.FundingSources: Truckee Tahoe Airport District

properties.ProjectName: Regan Beach Enhancement and Accessibility Improvement Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The project will focus on a crucial segment of Phase 1, known as Regan Landing, to enhance both access and user experience. Planned improvements include creating a more welcoming pedestrian zone with upgraded pathways, redesigning the drop-off area for smoother vehicle access and safety, and enhancing ADA-compliant features. Additionally, the project will install new restrooms and a concession stand, establish designated picnic and barbecue areas with fixed seating, and provide SUP rental storage for residents. Landscaping enhancements will further beautify the park and promote a more sustainable environment.

properties.ProjectName: Edgewood Properties Fuel Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat approximately 15 acres of private lands East of the Hwy 50 corridor and West of the Bi-State Van Sickle State Park.
properties.FundingSources: Private Property Owners

properties.ProjectName: Cave Rock Boat Ramp Extension Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Located at Cave Rock State Park in Nevada, this project will extend the current boat ramp to accommodate low water years and serve the increasing use of the boat ramp. Currently, only one lane is usable during low water levels. The extension will expand the functionality and accessibility, ultimately enhancing the overall boating experience for visitors.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Division of State Lands

properties.ProjectName: Nevada Understory Burning Program
properties.ProjectDescription: This project aims to implement understory burning at Spooner Lake and Backcountry State Park and Van Sickle Bi-state Park. Understory burning improves forest health and resilience, reduces wildfire hazard, and improves wildlife habitat. Some of the project area will be a reburn from 10 years ago, while other project areas will see the first reintroduction of  beneficial fire in over 100 years. These forests historically burned every 5-20 years, and are long overdue for understory burning.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: North Lake Tahoe Division: CWPP Implementation and Completion Project
properties.ProjectDescription: This project will focus on reducing hazardous fuels in areas identified as having a high fire risk in the Lake Tahoe Basin Community Wildfire Protection Plan within the jurisdiction of North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District. The communities of Incline Village and Crystal Bay Nevada are located within the jurisdiction of North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District. Treatment methods that will be utilized to achieve the wildfire mitigation objectives of this project include hand thinning and piling, understory burning, and mechanical mastication.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District

properties.ProjectName: Zephyr Creeks SEZ Crossing and Restoration Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: The Zephyr Creeks SEZ Crossing and Restoration Project intends to reconnect floodplains below US-50, relocate existing stormwater assets outside of the SEZ, upsize or duplicate an existing culvert below US-50, and upsize an existing culvert on the USFS/Zephyr Cove Resort property. A resident beaver population utilizes an NDOT box culvert to dam the creek resulting in upstream flooding of the Zephyr Cove campground trails, US-50, and a nearby sewer pump station. NTCD will work with the USFS, NDOT and the Zephyr Cove Resort to design and implement the project.

properties.ProjectName: North Tahoe Fire FAC Coordination and Planning Capacity Support
properties.ProjectDescription: The project provides three years of funding to support NTFPD in improving it's Fire Adapted Communities program and in planning for fuels reduction and forest health treatments necessary in restoring and maintaining fire resilient landscapes. The project allows for a full-time primary support person for Fire Adapted Communities, it provides improvements in transportation for defensible space inspections, and it provides for training to support fuels management and Fire Adapted Communities. The project also provides funding to cover cultural and environmental surveys that are needed in planning high priority fuels reduction and forest health projects within the jurisdiction of NTFPD.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Vegetation Preservation, Transportation and Sustainable Communities
properties.FundingSources: California Community Forestry

properties.ProjectName: Van Sickle NEPA EA and Section 106 Evaluation
properties.ProjectDescription: Funding for the 2019 Van Sickle Bi-State Park Vision Plan improvements comes from federal funding sources such as Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) and Recreational Trails Program (RTP). To access these funds, an environmental assessment (EA) and Section 106 evaluation are required. This process analyzes the proposed park improvements outlined in the 2019 vison plan for environmental, social and economic effects and allow for public comment. The expected completion is July of 2025.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: South Lake Tahoe Division CWPP Implementation and Completion Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The South Lake Tahoe Wildfire and Fuels Division will be responsible for preparing and implementing high priority fuels reduction and wildfire prevention projects identified in our Community Wildfire Protection Plan (CWPP) on state, local government, and private lands in the South Shore area of the Lake Tahoe Basin (Basin). This work will be done in coordination with the Tahoe Fire and Fuels Team (TFFT) and other Basin partners. Once implemented, the fuels reduction and wildfire prevention projects will help to restore the resilience of Basin forests and watersheds, foster Basin-wide climate change adaption and reduce fire risk for communities.

properties.ProjectName: North Tahoe Regional Park Trail Extension
properties.ProjectDescription: This project extended the existing Class 1 Pam Emmerich Memorial Pinedrop Bike Trail approximately 1,100 linear feet in the North Tahoe Regional Park. The trail provides ADA accessibility between the existing bathroom in the lower parking lot and the existing Pam Emmerich Memorial Pinedrop Trailhead. Trail amenities include pervious paver plazas, trail signs, bike racks, bear boxes, a staircase, and two (2) ball field viewing areas. No additional vehicle miles were created with this project.

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe XC Lodge Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Relocate and expand the Tahoe XC Lodge, meeting growing outdoor recreation/education demand and improving the managed trailhead for an extensive network of skiing/hiking/biking trails. The new lodge is an adaptive reuse of a 1930s home with an addition; retaining the welcoming charm of the original house and upgrading the entire facility to a net zero, all electric structure. The project is the climate adaptation strategy for Tahoe XC, encouraging year-round connections between community members and nature. Educational and recreational opportunities abound on a site next to the high school and with ADA accessible grades which will serve all members of our community.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Recreation, Soil Conservation, Transportation and Sustainable Communities

properties.FundingSources: North Tahoe Community Alliance; Placer County Park Dedication Fees; Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax; Private Property Owners; Proposition 68; Tahoe City Public Utility District; Tahoe Fund; Truckee Tahoe Airport District

properties.ProjectName: North Tahoe Regional Park Community Gathering Space Improvement Project
properties.ProjectDescription: The project consists of constructing gathering spaces adjacent to the existing tennis and pickleball courts. The project involves concrete curbs, asphalt pavement, pervious pavers, acrylic surfacing, electrical improvements, adding a seat wall, trash enclosure ball backboard, bike racks, interpretive panels, and an art feature from a local artist.
properties.FundingSources: North Tahoe Public Utility District; Placer County Transient Occupancy Tax; Tahoe Fund

properties.ProjectName: SR 28 Safety Improvements-Northwood Boulevard to Northwood Boulevard
properties.ProjectDescription: Safety improvements, including a roundabout, crosswalks, and bus shelters on SR 28 in Incline Village. This project is identified in the Vision Zero Safety Strategy.

properties.ProjectName: Tunnel Creek Hazardous Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: Tunnel Creek is seasonal creek that is fed by multiple springs and drains into Lake Tahoe at Hidden Beach. Multiple fuels reduction projects and understory burning have occurred adjacent to the creek over the last 20 years, with light thinning occurring in the riparian vegetation 15 years ago. Recent mortality in both white fir and red fir from bark beetles, combined with declining riparian vegetation due to conifer competition, has created hazardous conditions. This projects objectives will be achieved through a combination of hand thinning, pile building, and mastication.
properties.LeadImplementer: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
properties.FundingSources: Tahoe Bonds Act

properties.ProjectName: Incline Village General Improvement District Fuels Reduction Project
properties.ProjectDescription: This project will focus on reducing hazardous fuels and maintaining healthy forest stands on land owned by the Incline Village General Improvement District.
properties.LeadImplementer: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District

properties.ProjectName: Northstar Community Services District Wood Energy Facility
properties.ProjectDescription: Northstar Community Services District is seeking to increase the scope and scale of its fuels management and defensible space programs through the development of a Wood Energy Facility project that will both reduce environmental impacts and minimize operating costs by creating a local use for otherwise non-merchantable biomass material. The project aims to serve as a valuable demonstration project for the greater Tahoe-Truckee region, acting as a catalyst for similar projects that could be replicated within the Tahoe-Truckee region as well as in other rural mountain and ski resort communities.
properties.FundingSources: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE); U.S. Forest Service

properties.ProjectName: Tranquility Estates Fuels Treament and Stream Restoration
properties.ProjectDescription:
Fuels reduction and stream restoration of up to 100 acres of fuel reduction work on a 200-acre private parcel to reduce wildfire risk, restore functions on McFaul Creek, and remove invasive weeds. 
Fuel treatments would include thinning of overstory trees, slash piling and burning. Understory brush would be cut, piled and burned, masticated, or chipped. 
Stream restoration would include performing low-impact process-based restoration water quality improvements while simultaneously performing fuels reduction within the SEZ.

properties.ProjectName: Zephyr Heights Community Defensible Space
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: Fuels reduction treatment on a minimum of 75 acres of private parcels located within the Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) of Zephyr Cove, Nevada. This project collaborates with private landowners to implement defensible space and fuels reduction treatments on their properties. The project emphasizes community empowerment through education and outreach efforts that promote fire-adapted practices. This includes the formation of a Firewise site in partnership with Zephyr Cove residents.

properties.ProjectName: Glenbrook Shaded Fuel Break Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription:
This project was completed on August 28, 2025 to improve defensible space for Glenbrook, the US Highway 50 primary evacuation corridor, and East Shore Tahoe tourist assets by:
 
creating and sustaining a fuel break on GHOA General Forest and privately owned land parcels adjacent to US Highway 50.

creating and sustaining 200 ft fuel breaks on GHOA General Forest lands and privately owned land parcels located between Glenbrook and USFS parcels west of Spooner Summit, NV.

The project utilized 2025 Lake Tahoe-Community Wildfire Protection Plan mitigation strategies to reduce combustible fuels via mastication and hand crew work on approximately 60.89 acres of privately owned land.
properties.FundingSources: Private Property Owners

properties.ProjectName: Hogan Court Drainage Improvement Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Reduce Stormwater Pollution From: Roads and Highways, Forest Roads, Public and Private Parcels
properties.ProjectDescription: The project includes installation of a new storm drain junction box at an existing NDOT outlet located upslope of 699 Hogan Court and approximately 440 linear feet of underground storm drain pipe, connecting to the existing storm drain system at the intersection of Hogan Court and Titlist Drive. The project intends to reduce SR 431 embankment erosion and improve storm water conveyance. The storm drain alignment will traverse NDOT right-of-way, the private property at 699 Hogan Court, and Washoe County ROW. The project is in collaboration with NDOT, Washoe County, NTCD, and private property owners of 699 Hogan Court.
properties.FundingSources: Nevada Department of Transportation

properties.ProjectName: Glenbrook - Yerington Area Tree Thinning Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: This defensible space enhancement project with the Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District thinned trees on 42 acres of land owned by 40 different individuals.  Goal was to restore parcel forests to a healthier density.  At the conclusion of project, defensible space around homes was expanded. Lean, clean, green zones are have been enhanced among closely spaced cottage and single family homes.  This project aligns with the Lake Tahoe - Community Wildfire Protection Plan and reduces wildfire risk in a designated Highest Priority Tier 1 Zone.
properties.FundingSources: Private Property Owners

properties.ProjectName: IVGID Skate Park Expansion
properties.ProjectDescription: The proposed skate park expansion is located southwest of the existing facility, occupying the area adjacent to the current entrance walkway from the regional bike path. The existing access route will be maintained to ensure consistent site circulation. The expansion will be physically integrated with the existing skate park to provide a continuous riding surface and cohesive design, supporting efficient user flow and operational functionality.
properties.FundingSources: Incline Village General Improvement District

properties.ProjectName: Upper Truckee Marsh South Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Restore Priority Meadows, Wetlands, and Lake Tahoe Tributaries
properties.ProjectDescription: A multi-benefit project that has restoration, public access, and forestry elements. The Conservancy aims to restore wetlands by removing fill placed from historic development, including over eight feet of fill over four acres at a former motel and two acres at a former maintenance yard. Additionally, the Conservancy is considering stabilizing banks, removing encroached conifers, and enhancing meadows. The Conservancy is also evaluating opportunities to enhance a portion of the South Tahoe Bikeway and provide other public access amenities.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Air Quality, Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Soil Conservation, Vegetation Preservation, Water Quality, Wildlife, Transportation and Sustainable Communities

properties.ProjectName: Lyons Ranch Fuel Hazard Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: The Lyons Ranch Fuel Hazard Reduction Project consists of manual and mechanical fuel hazard reduction treatments on 132 acres (33 acres of manual and 99 acres of mechanical) within the Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) in the south shore area of the Lake Tahoe Basin on Conservancy owned lands in El Dorado County. The treatments would reduce fuel loads near residential structures and are identified as priority treatment areas in the recently released Tahoe Basin CWPP. The project is designed to modify expected fire behavior/intensity in the treatment area and will serve to reduce wildfire risk to the adjacent residential south shore communities along Pioneer Trail.
properties.FundingSources: Wildfire Resilience

properties.ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Large Acreage Fuel Hazard Reduction
properties.ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys Large Acreage (TKLA) Project consists of manual and mastication fuel reduction treatments on Conservancy and LTBMU owned land within the Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) in the south shore area of the Lake Tahoe Basin in the City of South Lake Tahoe. The treatments would reduce fuel loads near residential structures and are identified as priority treatment areas in the recently released Tahoe Basin CWPP. The project is designed to modify expected fire behavior/intensity in the treatment area and will serve to reduce wildfire risk to the adjacent residential south shore neighborhood of Tahoe
properties.FundingSources: Proposition 4

properties.ProjectName: Upper Kingsbury Fire Adapted Community
properties.EIPActionPriority: Implement Defensible Space on Public and Private Parcels and Utility Corridors
properties.ProjectDescription: This three-year project will help at least 200 privately owned properties (approximately 70 acres) in the Upper Kingsbury community achieve Defensible Space compliance through home inspections, vegetation treatment, chipping services, and compostable material drop-off. The project will reduce wildfire risk by addressing cost barriers that prevent property owners from completing defensible space work. Efforts include coordinated outreach, contractor support, partial reimbursements, and Firewise community engagement to promote long-term compliance and neighborhood-wide wildfire resilience.

properties.ProjectName: Pope Marsh Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Project
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: The purpose of the project is to remove aquatic invasive plants (AIP) in Pope Marsh, and exclude plant fragments growing in Lake Tallac from flowing into and infesting the marsh and subsequently, Lake Tahoe. Pope Marsh is identified in the Lake Tahoe Region Aquatic Invasive Species Action Agenda 2021-2030 as a priority project. A survey conducted in July 2023 by Tahoe RCD’s contracted divers detected Eurasian watermilfoil (Myriophyllum spicatum) growing at various densities within a 1.8-acre area. In 2025, survey and hand removal of AIP was conducted by contracted divers and a metal screen was installed on top of the weir separating Pope Marsh from Lake Tallac to prevent further infestation.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: South Shore Offshore Aquatic Invasive Plant Planning and Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: Enhanced aquatic invasive plant monitoring has revealed sparse areas of plant infestations between previously defined project areas. The South Shore Offshore Aquatic Invasive Plant Planning and Control project implements a new strategy to evaluate, plan, and implement control treatments in aquatic invasive plant-infested areas over a larger landscape vs. individual, specific areas. Work commenced in 2025 in the following unit locations: Taylor-Tallac offshore, Camp Richardson, Edgewood 1, Edgewood 2, and Nevada Beach.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act

properties.ProjectName: Elk Point and Round Hill Rock Cribs Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
properties.EIPActionPriority: Prevent, Control, or Eradicate Aquatic Invasive Species
properties.ProjectDescription: From May to July 2025, divers conducting surveillance work north of Nevada Beach detected thousands of aquatic invasive plant fragments floating on the water surface and in the water column. Thousands of these fragments settled and rooted offshore in numbers and distribution far exceeding previous observations in this location. This discovery spurred a rapid response, and divers spent several days pulling the rooted plants and removing fragments. This project proposes to conduct site assessments and plant removal dive visits at this location and sites north of Elk Point in 2026, to ensure that no aquatic invasive plants are infesting the area.
properties.ProjectThresholdCategories: Fisheries, Recreation, Scenic Resources, Water Quality
properties.FundingSources: Lake Tahoe Restoration Act
